title: feat: v0.3.0 rewrite as SEO Pro Stack
body:
## Summary

v0.3.0 rewrite of the plugin, now named **SEO Pro Stack** (slug and text domain `seoprostack`, main file `seoprostack.php`). It replaces the v0.2.x code on `main` (the v0.2.5.1 line).

### Architecture
- One settings store (`seoprostack_options`) driven by a schema that each feature declares (`includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php`). The admin UI renders from that schema, saves instantly over AJAX and sanitises per field type (bool, int, text, url, lines, domains, select, multi, times).
- Features live in `includes/features/`, are registered in `SEOProStack::$core_features` (`includes/class-seoprostack.php`) and are off by default.
- Versioned migrations (DB version 4): each feature's `migrate()` imports the settings of the plugin it replaces, once, without touching that plugin's own options. Cards show "Replaces: …".
- Admin screen at Settings → SEO Pro Stack with tabs General, Workflow, Speed and Advanced (`admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`).

### Features
- **Modern admin colours**, **Magic login links**, **Publishing queue**, **iFrame block**, **Copy linked images to Media Library** (as before).
- **Admin bar and dashboard access by role** (replaces Admin Bar & Dashboard Access Control and the v0.2.5 Access Manager; imports both).
- **Dashboard and sidebar widgets** (replaces Widget Disable).
- **Notification emails** (replaces Manage Notification E-mails): each email is stopped with its own core filter. Non-admin password resets are never stopped.
- **Duplicate posts** (replaces Carbon Copy / Yoast Duplicate Post): always a new draft; choose what is copied.
- **Staged new versions**: edit a published post as a draft copy, then publish (or schedule) it over the original. The URL, comments and date are kept, and a revision is stored. Cron fallback completes the merge if the block editor tab closes early.
- **Shareable preview links** (replaces Public Post Preview): expiring token links; `noindex`, `no-referrer` and no-cache headers; robots meta also set for Rank Math and Yoast.
- **Sticky posts for any post type** (replaces Sticky Posts Switch): star column, editor option, archive and term lifting on core's sticky list.
- **Select all across pages** (replaces Bulk Actions Select All): bulk actions apply to every item matching the list filters, checked per item.
- **410 Gone** (replaces Ultimate 410): explicit paths, `*` prefixes, optional auto-add on permanent deletion. Only affects URLs that would otherwise 404.
- **Speed**: page preloading via Speculation Rules (tunes core on 6.8+, prints rules on older), delay scripts until interaction, delayed GA4 (replaces Flying Pages / Flying Scripts / Flying Analytics).

### Recommendations
- Free plugins use core Plugins → Add New card markup and `updates.js` for in-place install/activate.
- Plugins closed on WordPress.org stay listed as reminders with the closure date, reason and replacement, and no install action.
- Plugins replaced by native features are no longer recommended (`admin/data/free-plugins.php` notes which feature replaces each).

### Upgrade and uninstall
- Pre-0.3.0 `wp_allstars_*` options and `_wp_allstars_source_url` meta are migrated.
- Uninstall removes our options, transients, magic-login meta, preview-link / staged-version / duplicate markers and the staged-merge cron hook. Imported media, sticky lists and other plugins' settings are left alone.

## Verification
LocalWP (WordPress 7.1, PHP 8.2, Rank Math + WooCommerce + Kadence active):
- `php -l` / `node --check` on every PHP and JS file: pass.
- Admin audit `audit-v030.js`: 123/123.
- Staged versions + preview links `check-versions.js`: 20/20. The original's slug and date are kept, the draft is removed, a wrong or disabled token returns 404, and the preview is noindex in both the header and the meta tag.
- Sticky + select-all `check-lists.js`: 12/12. 12 posts across 3 pages were moved to the Bin and restored.
- Speed `check-speed.js`: 15/15. Covers the rules and exclusions, held scripts running in order after interaction or the time limit, and analytics loading once.
- 410 probes: explicit, wildcard, encoded and deleted-post paths return 410; live pages are unaffected.
- Staged-version merge probes, both immediate and scheduled.

Baseline (Docker, **WordPress 6.2 + PHP 7.4.33**, Twenty Twenty-One):
- PHP 7.4 lint of every file: pass.
- Fresh activation: migrates to DB version 4. Imports from Admin Bar & Dashboard Access Control, Manage Notification E-mails, Sticky Posts Switch, Flying Pages, Flying Scripts and Flying Analytics.
- With all 21 switches on, front-end, feed, login, list, editor, Widgets and all four settings tabs return 200. `/old-page/` and `/old-shop/item/` return 410, unknown paths return 404, the speculation-rules fallback prints, and `debug.log` stays empty.

Release build (`.distignore`, 61 files): Plugin Check "No errors found" after two fixes: a redundant `suppress_filters` was removed, and the shared cache-plugin names now carry documented ignores. Magic login HTTP flow 17/17 earlier in this PR.

CodeRabbit security review follow-ups (`2775915`):
- Settings saves read the stored option fresh, verify the write, and return an error if it did not persist. The admin UI queues saves one at a time.
- Migrations record the DB version only after the settings are confirmed stored, so a failed write is retried.
- Probe: 8/8. Covers normal and unchanged saves, keeping a concurrent change, reporting a blocked write, and a failed migration that stays unrecorded and then retries. Browser: 3 rapid saves ran one at a time and all persisted (7/7). Admin audit 123/123.

## Notes
- Imports from Flying Pages and Flying Scripts need their `FLYING_*_VERSION` marker, so leftover options from long-removed installs are not revived.
- Related follow-ups: #2 (maintenance mode), #3 (security toggles).

title: fix: refresh free plugin cards when a category's list changes
body:
## Summary

On the test site, Free Plugins → Admin still showed Admin Bar & Dashboard Access Control and Manage Notification E-mails after they were removed from `admin/data/free-plugins.php`. Each category's cards were cached for 12 hours under a name that depended only on the category (`seoprostack_plugins_v3_<category>`). That category had been cached before the removal, so the old list stayed on screen until the cache expired.

Sites updating from 0.2.x were not affected, because 0.3.0 introduced a new cache name. Any future list change would have been delayed the same way.

## Changes
- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`: new `cache_key()`, which adds the first 8 hex characters of an md5 of the category's slugs to the transient name. Editing a list changes the name, so the next load fetches fresh cards. `clear_plugin_cache()` uses the same key.
- Old-name transients expire on their own and are also removed on uninstall, which already matches `_transient_seoprostack_*`.
- `README.md` and `readme.txt`: Unreleased changelog entries for this change and PR #4.

## Verification (LocalWP, plugin-testing)
- Lint OK.
- Every Free Plugins category was loaded through the UI and waited on until its cards rendered. Card counts match the data file in all 19 categories: Admin now shows 7 cards, down from 9. None of the replaced plugins appears.
- Admin audit 123/123.

title: feat: regroup settings tabs by area and add feature search (#7 P1)
body:
## Summary

Phase P1 of the plugin-replacement programme. The settings tabs are now grouped by area, so the replacement features planned in the parent issue have obvious homes, and a new search finds any setting without knowing its tab.

## Changes

- **Tabs**: Admin, Content, Media, Links and Speed replace General, Workflow and Advanced. Plugins and Maintenance are registered now and stay hidden until a feature uses them (same rule as before: empty settings tabs are not shown).
  - `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`: `settings_tabs()` holds label and intro per tab; settings tabs render through `SEOProStack_Settings_Manager::render_tab()`.
  - `includes/features/*.php`: `tab` values moved (`general`→`admin`, `workflow`→`content`, image copying→`media`, `advanced`→`links`).
- **Compatibility**: `SEOProStack_Settings::LEGACY_TABS` maps old slugs. Old links (`?tab=general`) open the new tab, and settings added through `seoprostack_settings_schema` with an old `tab` still appear. The Plugins screen "Settings" link no longer names a tab.
- **Search**: a GET form in the header (`tab=search&s=…`) lists matching settings grouped by tab, using the normal cards, so they can be switched on and changed from the results. Matching covers the label, description, replaced plugin names and slugs, and child option labels (`SEOProStack_Settings::search()`). No extra JavaScript.
- **Removed**: `render_general_tab()`, `render_workflow_tab()`, `render_speed_tab()` and `render_advanced_tab()`; they were only used by the tab registry.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: tab names, search, extending notes and Unreleased changelog.

## Verification

title: feat: Plugins tab with admin bar toggle, plugin sizes and deleted plugin cleanup (#7 P2)
body:
## Summary

Phase P2 of the plugin-replacement programme: the Plugins tab gets its first three features, all off by default. Two replace separate plugins; the third, a Size column, helps find heavy plugins as groundwork for the wp-admin speed work.

## Changes

- **Plugins menu in the admin bar** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-toggle.php`, replaces Plugin Toggle, which has no settings to import).
  - Lists every plugin the user may switch, in wp-admin and on the site; active ones are bold. A confirm names the plugin (“Deactivate FluentSMTP?”).
  - Links run core's own `plugins.php` activate/deactivate action with core's nonce, then `wp_redirect` sends you back to the page you came from (a same-host path, checked with `wp_validate_redirect()`).
  - If that admin page belonged to the plugin you switched off, a one-off nonce sends you to the Plugins screen instead of “not allowed”. The argument is in `removable_query_args` and is never added to front-end addresses.
  - Plugin names are cached in one site transient, cleared on activate, deactivate, delete, update and Plugins screen load, so ordinary page loads never call `get_plugins()`. Network-activated plugins are left to the Network Plugins screen.
- **Plugin sizes** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-sizes.php`).
  - Size column with total plus PHP, JS, CSS, media and other. The screen renders from cache; missing sizes are measured over AJAX in batches with a 3-second server budget per request, and only installed plugins' folders can be measured.
  - Cache is one non-autoloaded option (a site option on multisite), keyed by plugin version, and forgets deleted plugins.
  - Sort button in the heading keeps core's update and notice rows under their plugin; sort is announced with `wp.a11y.speak`.
- **Clean up deleted plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php`, replaces the maintainer's “Fix ‘Plugin file does not exist’ Notices”).
  - On the Plugins screen, removes `uninstall_plugins` and `recently_activated` entries whose file is gone, and says which. `active_plugins` is left to core, which already deactivates missing plugins on that screen (reproduced locally before writing this).
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: registers the three features.
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: Plugin Toggle removed (replaced); String Locator removed, with a comment: searching code is better done in an editor or with WP-CLI.
- `uninstall.php`: removes the size cache and name transient.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature sections, tab list, Unreleased changelog. No external services are contacted.

## Verification

- `php -l` / `node --check` on all files (lint OK); every PHP file also lints under `php:7.4-cli`.
- LocalWP test site, synced with `.distignore`:
  - Plugins screen check, 22/22: tab cards; cleanup notice names both seeded missing plugins and does not repeat; menu lists 13 plugins; confirm names the plugin; cancel does nothing; activate from an admin page returns there; deactivate from the front end returns to `/` with no extra arguments; deactivating the plugin that owned the current admin page lands on the Plugins screen; all 13 plugins measured; sort largest/smallest keeps update rows under their plugin; sizes cached on reload; no page errors. Plugin states restored afterwards.
  - Existing admin audit: 152/152 checks at desktop and 390 px.
  - `debug.log` has no entries from the plugin.
- Screenshots reviewed at 1440 and 782 px.

title: feat: hide admin notices behind a Notices button (#7 P3)
body:
## Summary

P3 of #7, part one: **Hide admin notices** (Admin tab, off by default), which replaces Hide Admin Notices. Plugin and theme notices move into a **Notices (n)** button next to Screen Options and Help, so admin pages open at their content.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Admin_Notices`, registered in `SEOProStack::$core_features`.
  - Picks the same notices core's `common.js` moves under the heading (`div.updated, div.error, div.notice`, not `.inline` / `.below-h2`), plus the core update nag. It moves them into a panel inside `#screen-meta` and opens it with core's `screenMeta.toggleEvent`, so it behaves like Screen Options and Help.
  - Kept on the page: `#message` and `.settings-error` (feedback on what you just did), `.inline`, hidden notices, notices added after load, and `.sps-keep`. A setting can also keep errors, or warnings and the update nag, on the page.
  - A body class hides the notices with CSS until the script has moved them, so there is no flash or layout shift. The class is removed in a `finally`, and if `#screen-meta` is missing the notices stay where they are.
  - The count follows dismissals (MutationObserver), and the button disappears when the panel is empty.
  - Skipped in the block editor and iframe requests. No stored data, so no migration and no uninstall change. Hide Admin Notices has no settings to import.
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: Hide Admin Notices removed from Free Plugins, with a comment.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature section, table row, changelog.

## Not in this PR: Turn off updates

A "Turn off updates" feature (replacing Disable All WordPress Updates) was built and tested, then taken out. Plugin Check reports an **error**, `plugin_updater_detected` (`site_transient_update_plugins`), plus `update_modification_detected` warnings. WordPress.org's common issues guidance also asks plugins not to interfere with the built-in updater. The work is parked on `feature/disable-updates-parked` (commit 478685b) until there is a decision on shipping it. Free Plugins keeps recommending Disable All WordPress Updates.

## Verification

- `php -l` (PHP 8.x and 7.4) on every PHP file; `node --check` on every JS file.
- Plugin Check on a `.distignore` build: "No errors found".
- Browser check with seeded test notices, 23/23 on LocalWP (WordPress 7.1) and 23/23 on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4:
  - Button count matches the panel; notices are moved and hidden; inline and `#message` notices stay.
  - The panel opens and closes, `aria-expanded` is set, and other toggles are hidden while it is open.
  - Dismissing a notice lowers the count; Screen Options still works.
  - The button shows only when the panel has notices.
  - "Keep errors" and "keep warnings" work (on 6.2 the pending core update nag moves into the panel, or stays with "keep warnings").
  - Block editor untouched; no JS errors.
- Screenshots checked: the button sits left of Screen Options and Help on both versions.
- Existing admin audit: 152/152.
- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 smoke test with every feature on: all front-end and admin pages 200, `debug.log` empty.

title: feat: paste into the Media Library, replacing The Paste (#7 P3)
body: ## Summary P3 of #7, part two: **Paste into the Media Library** (Media tab, off by default), which replaces The Paste. Screenshots, pictures and files pasted from the clipboard upload straight away on the Media Library screen, in the media dialog, on Add New Media File and in the classic editor. It also fixes a bug in the shared settings sanitiser. Pattern fields lost `%date%` and `%day%` when saved, including Copy linked images' existing file name and alt text patterns. ## Changes - `includes/features/class-seoprostack-paste-media.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Paste_Media`, registered in `SEOProStack::$core_features`. - **Media screens and dialog**: pasted files go to core's own plupload instance (`addFile()`), the same path as dropping a file. File types, size limits, capability checks, progress, and the grid or dialog refresh stay core's. The active uploader is found by wrapping `wp.media.view.UploaderWindow.prototype.ready`, with `wp.media.frame` and `window.uploader` (Add New Media File) as fallbacks. The listener is on `window` and skips pastes another script has already taken, or that land in form fields. - **Classic editor**: a TinyMCE `paste` handler, prepended so it runs before the paste plugin (which then returns on `isDefaultPrevented()` and restores the caret). It uploads through `POST /wp/v2/media` (`wp-api-fetch` nonce) with the post ID and a title, then swaps a placeholder for ``. A `GetContent` filter keeps the placeholder out of saved content. Clipboards that include text (web pages, documents) are left to the editor. - **Names**: only clipboard pictures with no real name (`image.png`) are renamed, from `%post_title%` / `%user%` / `%date%` / `%time%`. `%post_title%` falls back to `pasted-image`. Copied files keep their names. - **Format**: optional JPEG or WebP at a set quality (default 82), via canvas. The original is kept if the result is not smaller or the browser cannot write the format. WebP falls back to JPEG when the site does not allow WebP. GIFs and copied files are never converted. - The block editor already uploads pasted images and is left alone; its media dialog is covered. - **Import** (`migrate()`): switches on if The Paste (`the-paste/index.php`) is active, including network-active. From the `the_paste` option it imports `tinymce_enabled`, `image_quality` and `default_filename` (`` → `%post_title%`, `` → `%user%`; skipped if other placeholders remain). Per-user options are not imported, and The Paste's options are only read. While The Paste is loaded, its classic editor handling is left to it so nothing uploads twice. - `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php`: - `DB_VERSION` 4 → 5, with a docblock line, because 0.3.1 shipped at 4. - The `text` sanitiser now sets a field's declared `tokens` aside around `sanitize_text_field()`, which strips `%` plus two hex digits (`%da…`). Fields without tokens are unchanged, and the result is the same when sanitised twice. - `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: The Paste removed, with a comment. - `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature section, table row, changelog and the fix. No uninstall change: everything is stored in `seoprostack_options`. ## Verification - `php -l` (PHP 8.x and 7.4) on every PHP file; `node --check` on every JS file and the extracted inline script. - Plugin Check on a `.distignore` build: "No errors found". - Browser check, 27/27 on LocalWP (WordPress 7.1) and 27/27 on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4: - Media Library grid: upload, name from pattern, shown in the grid, a copied file keeps its name. - Add New Media File: upload converted to WebP. - Classic editor: converted to JPEG, named after the page, attached to it and inserted as `wp-image-N`. The placeholder shows during upload but is never in `getContent()`. A paste that includes text is not uploaded. - Classic media dialog: upload attached to the page and shown in the dialog. - Block editor: a paste outside the dialog is left alone; in the media dialog, the file is named after the post. - Feature off: no script. No JS errors. - With The Paste also active: one upload per paste, not two. - Imports: - LocalWP, The Paste active, `%Y-%m-%d` template: on, quality 70, file name `%post_title% %date%`. - WordPress 6.2, `` template: file name skipped, classic editor off, quality 75. - WordPress 6.2 smoke test (fresh activation, The Paste inactive): not switched on, options imported. - The Paste's own option is unchanged afterwards. - Sanitiser: `%filename% %date% %day% x %20 %post_title%` → `%filename% %date% %day% x %post_title%`. Before the fix, `%date%` became `te%` and `%day%` became `y%`. - Existing admin audit: 152/152. WordPress 6.2 smoke test with every feature on: all front-end and admin pages 200, `debug.log` empty. title: feat: avatars without Gravatar, replacing Avatar Privacy (#7 P3)
body:
## Summary

P3 of #7, part three: **Avatars without Gravatar** (Admin tab, off by default), which replaces Avatar Privacy. Every avatar is served from the site itself, so visitors' browsers never contact Gravatar and commenters' email hashes are not published.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-avatar-privacy.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Avatar_Privacy`, registered in `SEOProStack::$core_features`.
  - **Resolution** (`pre_get_avatar_data`): an uploaded profile picture if the person has one, otherwise the Discussion default drawn locally: a silhouette SVG, a 7×7 symmetric pattern SVG from a keyed hash of the email (`wp_hash()`, so it cannot be reversed), or blank. Other stored defaults map at read time (`option_avatar_default`): Identicon/Retro/Birds and similar → pattern, Mystery Person and the rest → silhouette. Discussion lists only Silhouette, Pattern, Blank.
  - Guests are never matched to users by email address, so a guest cannot show someone else's picture. Avatars other plugins set (non-Gravatar URLs) are kept.
  - **Profile pictures**: upload field replaces core's "change it on Gravatar" text (`user_profile_picture_description`). Uploads need `edit_user` and the `update-user_{id}` nonce, are type-checked with `wp_check_filetype_and_ext()` (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), centre-cropped to a square and saved at 64/128/256/512 px through the image editor, which also drops photo metadata. The smallest size that fits is served. Replace, remove and user deletion delete the files. Uploads can be turned off separately.
  - **Migration** (settings v5): the feature is switched on if Avatar Privacy is active. Its uploaded pictures (`avatar_privacy_user_avatar`) are copied, because deleting Avatar Privacy deletes them. This happens on migration, when Avatar Privacy is deactivated, and otherwise lazily the first time an avatar is shown. Stored paths from another server fall back to the file name in `uploads/avatar-privacy/user-avatar/`. Missing files leave an empty record, so they are not retried. The Gravatar opt-in is not imported (the feature never uses Gravatar). While Avatar Privacy is active it keeps handling avatars. Avatar Privacy's options and files are never written or deleted.
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: Avatar Privacy removed from recommendations.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php`: v5 docblock covers this import (0.3.1 shipped at v4).
- `uninstall.php`: deletes `uploads/seoprostack-avatars/` on every site and the network-wide `seoprostack_avatar` user meta.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature section, replaced-plugins table, privacy note, uninstall FAQ, changelog.

## Verification

- `php -l` on every PHP file with current PHP and PHP 7.4: OK.
- Browser check (Playwright, 41 checks), all passed on **LocalWP (WordPress 7.1, Imagick)** and on **WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (Docker, GD)**. It covers: no Gravatar images or requests on Dashboard, Users, Comments, Discussion, Profile and a post; every avatar loads; a different pattern per person; Discussion choices; upload stored in four square sizes; admin bar uses 64 px; replace/bad file/remove; REST `avatar_urls`; lazy import; user deletion removes files; uploads off; feature off restores core Gravatar; no JS errors.
- Migration seeded with Avatar Privacy data on 6.2: a normal picture, a path from another server and a missing file. All three were handled; pictures were served locally after Avatar Privacy was deactivated.
- Admin audit (settings screen, desktop and mobile): 152/152.
- Plugin Check on the `.distignore` build: "No errors found".
- `debug.log` empty on both sites after the runs. Files under 12 bytes are refused before core's type check, because WordPress 6.2's `wp_get_image_mime()` logs an `exif_imagetype()` notice for them.

### Follow-up from the CodeRabbit security summary (second commit)

CodeRabbit (free plan: summary only) inferred two import risks. Both are fixed in `import_user()`:
- **Import overlapping a removal**: a lazy import could write a picture back after the user removed it. The meta is now re-read from the database (cache cleared) just before writing. If it changed during the copy, that change wins and the copy's files are deleted.
- **Failed processing**: an image-editor error was recorded like a missing file, so it was never retried and any earlier copy was deleted. Now the earlier copy is kept and the import is retried after a day. Missing files are still recorded once.

`avatar-import-edge.php` (WP-CLI, WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4): 8/8. The run covered failure with no earlier copy (recorded with a retry time, default shown, not retried early, retried after), failure keeping the earlier copy, and a removal written directly to the database mid-import (removal kept, import files deleted). The browser check was rerun afterwards: 41/41 on both sites, Plugin Check "No errors found", 6.2 `debug.log` empty.

Test-site note: on LocalWP, Rank Math's profile script cancels the profile form's submit with this feature on or off. The check submits the form directly there; on 6.2 it clicks Update Profile.

title: fix: wait while replaced plugins are active; move inline notices printed above the page (#7)
body:
## Summary

Fixes from the maintainer's LocalWP screenshots of Hide admin notices, with Plugin Toggle still active:

1. **Two "Plugins" menus in the admin bar.** Our Plugins menu and Plugin Toggle's both rendered. The root cause is general: when a plugin that a feature replaces is still active, both run. The same applies to two notice panels, two paste handlers, and Google Analytics loaded twice with Flying Analytics.
2. **"Test inline notice" stayed above the page, beside the Notices button.** Inline notices were always kept, as core's `common.js` does. One printed on `admin_notices` sits above the page, not in its content.
3. **The Notices button narrowed the SEO Pro Stack header.** Found in follow-up screenshots: the floated tab shared a row with the flex header.

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php`:
  - `enabled()` is now `switched_on() && !replaced_active(KEY)`.
  - `switched_on()` reads the switch alone.
  - `replaced_active($key)` returns the active plugins a setting replaces, read from the cached schema.
  - `active_plugins()` covers site and network-active plugins, keyed by folder, cached per request.
  - A class docblock describes the rule.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-access.php`, `class-seoprostack-widget-control.php`: the second switches (`DASHBOARD_KEY`, `SIDEBAR_KEY`), which read their setting directly, also wait.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-avatar-privacy.php`:
  - `boot()` registers the deactivation and user-deletion hooks when `switched_on()`, so pictures are still copied when Avatar Privacy is deactivated while this feature waits.
  - The card sentence about Avatar Privacy is dropped; the general card note covers it.
- `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`: under "Replaces: …", an active replaced plugin now shows "*X is still active, so it does this job and this setting waits until it is deactivated.*" with a "Deactivate X" link (nonce, `deactivate_plugin` capability, site-active only). Names are escaped once, so "Admin Bar & Dashboard…" shows correctly.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php`: the selectors are split into `kinds` and placement.
  - `kinds` are always kept: `#message`, settings errors, hidden, `.sps-keep`, and the chosen keep types.
  - Placement: `.inline` and `.below-h2` are kept only inside the page.
  - Direct children of `#wpbody-content` before the page starts (the first `.wrap`, or an element containing `.wp-header-end` or `h1`) are moved when they match the notice selector and not `kinds`. The loading CSS also hides them, so they don't flash.
- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin.css`: `.sps-wrap { clear: both; }`, so the Screen Options / Notices tabs sit above the header, as on core screens.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: replaced-plugin behaviour, Hide admin notices wording, changelog.

## Verification

- `php -l` with current PHP and PHP 7.4: OK.
- New browser check (21 checks), passing on **LocalWP (WP 7.1)** and **WP 6.2 / PHP 7.4**:
  - inline notice above the page moved into the panel on Dashboard, the settings page and Posts; action message stays; count matches the panel; no notices left above the page;
  - an inline notice inside the Posts list (`restrict_manage_posts`) stays;
  - kept errors stay;
  - with Plugin Toggle active: only its menu, and the card explains the wait with a working nonce'd deactivate link;
  - after deactivating through the card link: only our menu, and the note is gone;
  - "&" in plugin names shown once escaped; no JS errors.
- Screenshots of the settings page with the panel closed and open: header full width, tab above it.
- Avatar Privacy hand-over on 6.2: while it is active, our avatar filter is off and the deactivation hook is registered. `wp plugin deactivate avatar-privacy` copied the pictures (normal and moved-server paths; missing file recorded), and avatars are then served locally.
- Regression: admin audit 152/152, avatar check 41/41 (LocalWP).
- Plugin Check on the `.distignore` build: "No errors found". `debug.log` has nothing from the plugin on either site.

title: feat: SVG uploads, resize large uploads and replace media files, replacing Safe SVG, Imsanity and Enable Media Replace (#7 P4)
body:
## Summary

P4 of #7, part one (Media 1): three Media-tab features, all off by default, replacing **Safe SVG**, **Imsanity** and **Enable Media Replace**. Each one imports the replaced plugin's settings, waits while that plugin is active, and is removed from Free Plugins.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-svg-uploads.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Svg_Uploads`.
  - Allow-list DOM cleaner (`DOMDocument::loadXML` with `LIBXML_NONET`): keeps known SVG elements and attributes only. It removes scripts, event handlers, `foreignObject`/HTML, `set`/`animate`, comments, PIs, `@import` and external `url()` in styles, `data-*`, and non-local links. `<a>` may link to http(s)/mailto; `<image>` only to embedded PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP data URIs.
  - Refuses DOCTYPE/entities, encodings other than UTF-8/Latin-1 (UTF-7/16 included), files over 10 MB, and `<use>` expansion bombs and loops (memoised expansion count).
  - Cleans on `wp_handle_upload_prefilter` / `wp_handle_sideload_prefilter` (Media Library, editors, REST, sideloads), and again on `wp_generate_attachment_metadata` for files added without an upload. Width/height come from attributes or `viewBox`; every size points at the SVG.
  - Roles setting (default administrator and editor, plus `upload_files`); network admins always allowed. Writability uses `wp_is_writable()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-resize-uploads.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Resize_Uploads`.
  - Resizes on `wp_handle_upload` under the uploaded name, so no `-scaled` copy and no kept original. `big_image_size_threshold` is set to the limit, so WordPress 7.1 client-side processing (REST `image_size_threshold`) uses it too. Requests the browser already processed are detected and left alone.
  - Quality, BMP→JPEG, optional PNG→JPEG for opaque PNGs when smaller, animated GIF and `noresize` exclusions, orientation fixed, metadata kept. A result is kept only when it is smaller.
  - Optional deletion of core's kept originals after sub-sizes are made. Existing pictures: Media → Library row and bulk actions (capability + nonce, 20-second time box), and `wp seoprostack resize-images [--dry-run]`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-replace-media.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Replace_Media`.
  - Hidden `upload.php?page=seoprostack-replace-media` screen, linked from the list-view row action and from attachment details. Needs `upload_files` + `edit_post`, and a nonce.
  - Keep name (same type required, same address) or use the new name (any type, same folder). The upload date can be kept or changed to now. The new file goes through `wp_handle_upload`, so type checks, SVG cleaning and resizing apply. Old files, sizes and edited backups are deleted, and metadata is regenerated.
  - Link updates: each old size is mapped to the same new size, or to the full file. Post content, excerpts and custom fields are updated in plain, JSON-escaped and serialized form (object-holding values left alone), across publish/future/draft/pending/private. Candidate rows are found with two prepared `LIKE` searches on the shared path prefix; exact paths are matched in PHP.
  - New action `seoprostack_media_replaced` (attachment ID, old path, new path, post IDs).
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: the three classes registered.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php`: the v5 docblock covers these imports (0.3.1 shipped at v4, so no version bump).
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: `safe-svg`, `imsanity` and `enable-media-replace` removed, with a comment.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature sections, replaced-plugins table, hook, changelog.
- `uninstall.php`: unchanged. All settings live in `seoprostack_options`; there is no new option, meta, transient or cron hook.

Imports: Safe SVG upload roles (or every role with `upload_files` when unset); Imsanity largest limit, quality, BMP/PNG conversion and delete-originals; Enable Media Replace's last-used name and date choices. The Safe SVG block is not replaced: the read-only site survey found no use of it.

## Verification

- `php -l` with PHP 8.5 and PHP 7.4 (Docker `php:7.4-cli`) on every PHP file: OK.
- Plugin Check on the `.distignore` build (LocalWP): "No errors found".
- `media1-svg-test.php` (WP-CLI, production upload path, LocalWP WP 7.1): **43/43**. Covers the hostile-file corpus (script, handlers, foreignObject, iframe, `@import`, external refs, xml-stylesheet, comments, set/animate, `data-*`, SVG data URIs), kept-content checks, well-formed output, entity/`<use>` bomb/UTF-7/UTF-16 refusal, SVG renamed to `.png`, role permissions, and cleaning on metadata.
- `media1-resize-test.php` (WP-CLI, LocalWP): **20/20** (BMP skipped: GD cannot read BMP). Covers resize under the same name, no kept original, PNG kept vs converted, transparency, `noresize`, existing-image resize with original deletion, nonce'd row action, idempotency.
- `check-media1.js` (Playwright): **all passed on LocalWP WordPress 7.1 and on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (Docker)**. It checks cards and "Replaces" labels, SVG upload and display, resize on upload, the REST limit (1920 on 7.1; correctly absent before 7.1), row and bulk resize, and saved choices preselected (imported `new`/`now` on LocalWP, defaults on 6.2). Replace is checked with the same name, new name and type, date kept or changed, post, JSON and serialized custom-field links, front end, different-type refusal, subscriber 403 (LocalWP), and no page errors.
- `check-media1-editor.js` (WP 7.1 block editor, client-side processing): JPEG stored at 1920 with no kept original; SVG uploaded with dimensions. All passed.
- Migration: Safe SVG, Imsanity and Enable Media Replace options seeded on LocalWP, then `seoprostack_options`/`seoprostack_db_version` deleted with the plugin inactive and the plugin activated. Settings were imported; features waited while the replaced plugins were active and took over after deactivation.
- Admin audit (settings screen, desktop and mobile): 152/152.
- Debug log: no new entries from these runs.

title: GH#7: feat: watermark pictures, replacing Easy Watermark (#7 P4)
body:
## Summary

P4 of #7 (Media): new Media-tab feature **Watermark pictures** (`SEOProStack_Watermark_Images`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`), off by default, replacing Easy Watermark.

- Mark: site icon (default), site logo, or a picture chosen with a new generic `media` setting type (media dialog picker; sanitised to image attachment IDs). SVG marks are refused with a clear message.
- Placement: nine positions (default bottom-right), size and margin as shares of each picture, opacity 30% by default, so the mark looks the same on every size. Uses the smallest file of the mark that is large enough, so it is scaled down, not up.
- What is marked: the file, the original WordPress keeps for big pictures, and every size at least 400 px on the shorter side. Thumbnails, `nowatermark` file names, animated GIF/WebP/APNG, site icons/logos/headers, the mark itself and pictures Easy Watermark already marked are left alone; `seoprostack_watermark_attachment` filter for others.
- When: after every size is made and after Resize large uploads (priority 95). WordPress 7.1 browser-processed uploads are detected through `rest_request_before_callbacks` and marked at the `finalize` request, once every browser-made size exists.
- Kept originals: unmarked copy in `uploads/seoprostack-originals-<random>/` (random name because Nginx ignores `.htaccess`; `.htaccess` deny and `index.php` added anyway). Enables **Remove watermark** and re-marking with new settings. Replaced files drop the stale original; deleted pictures delete theirs (hooked even when the feature is off).
- Existing pictures: Add/Remove watermark row and bulk actions (20 s budget, result notice with marked/removed/no watermark/left alone/failed/left for later counts) and `wp seoprostack watermark-images [--remove] [--dry-run]`.
- Editors: custom GD and Imagick subclasses stamp with alpha-correct opacity, following WordPress's `wp_image_editors` order.
- WebP and AVIF images: marking deletes stale copies and metadata updates re-queue conversion, so copies carry the mark (and lose it on removal).
- Migration (settings version 5): imports Easy Watermark's image watermark (preferring an auto-add one): picture, alignment, opacity, scale, backup choice; switches on if Easy Watermark is active with auto-add. Text watermarks are not imported. Waits while Easy Watermark is active. Easy Watermark removed from Free Plugins.
- Uninstall: removes records and the folder-name option; marked pictures stay marked and the originals folder is kept (the site owner's pictures).
- README and readme.txt updated (feature, hooks, `media` type, uninstall, changelog).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (changes image files; originals kept by default)
- `php -l` (PHP 8.2 and 7.4) and `node --check` on all files: pass.
- **LocalWP** `plugin-testing.local`, WP 7.1.2 / PHP 8.2 / GD:
  - Block-editor upload with browser processing (`__clientSideMediaProcessing` true): main file and every size ≥ 400 px marked exactly once (pixel check at 50% opacity: 120,41,89 expected 120,40,90), 4 small sizes left alone, original kept, deleting the picture deleted the kept original, no page errors.
  - Settings panel, media picker choose/save/reload/remove, row actions switching between Add/Remove, bulk notices (“Watermark removed from 1 picture. 1 had no watermark.”; “1 picture marked. 1 was left alone…”) and clean URLs after notices.
  - Replace media on a marked picture: new file marked, stale original dropped. `wp media regenerate` on a marked picture keeps a single mark.
  - WebP/AVIF: import → marked → copies made from the marked file (WebP pixel 121,38,87) → remove → copies deleted and remade unmarked (40,60,158).
  - Migration: seeded an Easy Watermark image watermark with it active, deleted our settings, activated → imported image 279, bottom-left, 25%, 40% opacity, auto-add on, backup off; waiting while Easy Watermark active, enabled after deactivation. Settings restored afterwards.
  - `debug.log`: no SEO Pro Stack or watermark entries.
- **Docker** WP 6.2 / PHP 7.4: upload marking, thumbnail left alone, re-mark from original (once), removal and mark-is-not-marked all pass with **GD** (CLI) and **Imagick** (web container, `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick`, ImageMagick 6.9.11). Media tab renders the picker and loads `media-views`; Media Library list shows row and bulk actions; `debug.log` empty.

title: GH#7: fix: Plugin Check findings in media queries (#7 P4)
body:
## Summary

Plugin Check on the `.distignore` build after #17 reported one error and four warnings in the media features. Fixed in code rather than by suppressing checks, except for a false positive on a core hook:

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php` (`cli()`): **ERROR** `WordPress.DB.PreparedSQLPlaceholders.LikeWildcardsInQuery`. `LIKE 'image/%%'` is now `LIKE %s` with `$wpdb->esc_like('image/') . '%'`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php` (`editor_classes()`): **WARNING** `NonPrefixedHooknameFound` on `apply_filters('wp_image_editors', …)`. This reads the core hook on purpose to follow WordPress's image library choice, so it gets a targeted `phpcs:ignore` with the reason.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php` (`waiting()`, `counts()`): 3× **WARNING** `PluginCheck.Security.DirectDB.UnescapedDBParameter` (from #16). The prepared `$where` fragment that was put into the queries is replaced by fixed `p.post_mime_type IN (%s, %s, %s)` placeholders. `type_sql()` is replaced by `type_args()`, which pads `source_types()` (always one to three types) by repeating the first type. Every value now goes through `prepare()`, and the `InterpolatedNotPrepared` ignores are gone.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low (query shape only; results unchanged)
- `php -l` (PHP 8 and 7.4) and `node --check`: pass.
- Plugin Check 2.1.0 on the `.distignore` build (LocalWP): **"Checks complete. No errors found."** (before: 1 error, 4 warnings).
- LocalWP WP 7.1.2: `waiting()` and the settings panel count match a direct query (types jpeg,png,webp: 23 in total, panel "23 of 23 pictures converted", `wp seoprostack convert-images --dry-run` "0 of 23 waiting"). `wp seoprostack watermark-images --dry-run` lists the same 19 pictures as before.

body:
## Summary

Links phase of #7: new Links-tab feature **Short addresses for custom post types** (`SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-remove-cpt-base.php`), off by default, replacing Remove CPT base.

- Serves items of chosen post types at `/item-name/` instead of `/type/item-name/`. Offered types: public, non-built-in, with a fixed rewrite base (bases with tags such as `%product_cat%` are not offered). Nothing happens on plain permalinks; the panel says so.
- Links: `post_type_link` drops the base, so menus, sitemaps, the editor's sample link and WooCommerce listings use the short address.
- Requests: a `request` filter looks for an item only when WordPress matched a page, post, category, attachment or 404 that does not exist, so pages, posts and categories keep their addresses. `get_page_by_path()` is called with array post types, because a string type also matches attachments (a picture named like an item made Rank Math redirect the item to the home page). Hierarchical types (`/parent/child/`), `<!--nextpage-->` pages, feeds, embeds, trackbacks and comment pages keep working.
- Old addresses keep working (no rewrite rules change, nothing to flush) and redirect 301 to the short address at `template_redirect` priority 0, keeping the query string and page number. Turning the feature off restores the old addresses.
- Name clashes: an item whose short address a published top-level page or post has keeps its old address and is not redirected. The list is stored in the autoloaded `seoprostack_cpt_base_taken` option (one small query per type), cleared on post save/delete/trash/untrash and when the feature is off; the options panel names the clashing addresses.
- Migration (settings version 5, unreleased): imports `rcptb_selected` post types; switches on if Remove CPT base is active. Waits while it is active. Removed from Free Plugins.
- Uninstall removes `seoprostack_cpt_base_taken`. README and readme.txt updated.

title: GH#7: fix: no option query per request while short CPT addresses are off (#7 Links)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #19. While Short addresses for custom post types was off (the default), `boot()` called `get_option('seoprostack_cpt_base_taken')` on every request to delete a stale list. Before WordPress 6.4, reading an option that does not exist costs a database query each time (no `notoptions` priming), so every request on every site with the feature off paid one extra query.

- `boot()` no longer reads the option. Instead `forget_taken()` is hooked to `save_post`, `deleted_post`, `trashed_post`, `untrashed_post` and `update_option_seoprostack_options` whether the feature is on or off. These fire only on writes, so a list stored while the feature was on is still cleared when posts or settings change while it is off.
- `forget_taken()` calls `delete_option()` directly.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low
- `php -l` (PHP 8.2 and 7.4): pass.
- **Docker** WP 6.2 / PHP 7.4, feature off, option absent, `SAVEQUERIES`: before, 1 of 4 queries in a WP-CLI bootstrap read `seoprostack_cpt_base_taken`; after, 0 of 3. The 29 HTTP checks from #19 pass; `debug.log` empty.
- **LocalWP** WP 7.1.2 / PHP 8.2: the 29 HTTP checks pass.

body:
## Summary

New feature on the Links tab, off by default: **Short links**, replacing Pretty Links (next plugin in the #7 replacement plan). Pretty Links is used by several of the surveyed sites.

- Short addresses on the site (such as `/go/offer/`) that redirect elsewhere with 301, 302 or 307, with nofollow (`X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, as Pretty Links does) and sponsored options, a note, categories, and click and unique-visitor counts.
- Links are a non-public post type (`sps_short_link`, menu **Short links**, `edit_pages` capability) with a category taxonomy, so the list, search, bulk actions and bin come from core. Columns: short address, target with redirect code, clicks (sortable). Search also matches address and target.
- **Front-end cost:** live links sit in one autoloaded option (`seoprostack_short_links`), checked on `do_parse_request` at priority 1. A request that is not a short link costs an array lookup and **no query** (measured: 0 queries on WP 6.2). The map is rebuilt once per request at shutdown when links change, and dropped when the feature is switched off.
- Clicks are counted after the redirect has been sent (`fastcgi_finish_request` / `litespeed_finish_request` when available) with an atomic `UPDATE … + 1`. Bots, previews, scripts and HEAD are not counted. A per-link cookie (`sps_link_<id>`, value `1`, one year, HttpOnly) marks unique visitors; no IPs or visitor details are stored.
- Editor safeguards: addresses are cleaned (full URLs, query strings, `..` and odd characters), WordPress addresses (`wp-*`, `feed`, `sitemap.xml`, …) are refused, taken addresses get `-2`, and a warning appears when a link takes over a page's address. New links get a random address with the configured prefix and the panel's defaults.
- **Pretty Links import:** `migrate()` imports its defaults for new links (redirect, nofollow, sponsored, tracking, Pro `base_slug_prefix`) and switches on when Pretty Links is active with links. Links are imported with address, target, redirect, options, name, description, date, on/off state, click and unique counts, and categories: when Pretty Links is deactivated, from **Import links** in the settings panel (20-second budget, resumable), or with `wp seoprostack short-links import`. Links already imported, deleted in Pretty Links (`deleted_at`), or whose address a short link already has are skipped, so importing again adds nothing. Pretty Links' tables and options are only read. Cloaked and other Pro redirect types become 302.
- While Pretty Links is active the feature waits (Pretty Links keeps redirecting), but links can be imported and checked beforehand.
- Filters: `seoprostack_short_link_target`, `seoprostack_short_link_count_click`.
- Free Plugins no longer lists Pretty Links. `uninstall.php` removes the map option, the links with their meta, and their categories. README.md and readme.txt (feature, privacy note for the cookie, FAQ, changelog) updated.

Not imported: Pretty Links' per-click history (referrers, IPs), keyword replacements (Pro).

- `php -l` on PHP 8.2 and 7.4: pass. **Plugin Check** 2.1.0: no errors or warnings (fixed `suppress_filters`, nonce field output and table-name queries, which now use `%i`, available from WP 6.2).

title: GH#7: feat: load plugins only where needed in wp-admin (#7 P9)
body:
## Summary

Phase 9 of #7 (wp-admin speed): new feature on the Plugins tab, off by default: **Load plugins only where needed**.

- Ticked plugins load only on their own pages, on post, term and list screens where they add boxes, fields or blocks, and where plugins that need them load. Everything else in wp-admin skips them.
- **Learned, not configured:** the first time an administrator opens a screen it loads every plugin and records which plugins register its page, post type, taxonomy, blocks and form hooks (scoped to that screen’s own post type or taxonomy). Forgotten when plugins are activated, deactivated or updated.
- **Always every plugin:** POST and other non-GET requests, links with an action or nonce, admin-ajax, REST, cron, WP-CLI, logged-out requests, the front end, Plugins/updates/settings/profile/user/widgets/menus/Customizer/Site Health/import/export screens, and SEO Pro Stack’s settings. Saving therefore never runs with plugins missing.
- **Menu stays the same:** an administrator’s full menu is copied (without counts; links back to the current screen, such as Customize return=, follow the screen shown) and skipped plugins’ entries are put back. Each person only gets back entries they could open; administrators keep entries for capabilities a skipped plugin grants itself.
- **Dependencies follow** (Requires Plugins, WooCommerce/Elementor headers and add-on names), in both directions.
- **Safe fallback:** a fatal error or a plugin deactivating itself on a filtered screen marks that screen to load every plugin, and core’s error message says to reload. A refused page reloads once with every plugin; only for administrators is the screen also marked, so other users cannot switch filtering off. Nothing is ever deactivated.
- Admin bar shows “N of M plugins” with a load-every-plugin link; ?seoprostack-load-all=1 and SEOPROSTACK_LOAD_ALL_PLUGINS are escape hatches. Plugins that change the login address or the active plugin list always load; permission plugins are marked in the list.
- Runs from a small must-use file the feature writes and removes itself (panel explains when wp-content/mu-plugins is not writable). Options, the MU file and learned data are removed on uninstall. Long plugin lists get search and select-all controls.
- README.md and readme.txt document the feature, safety rules and benchmark examples.



## Files Changed

README.md, admin/css/seoprostack-admin.css, admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php, admin/js/seoprostack-admin.js, includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php, includes/class-seoprostack.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php, readme.txt, uninstall.php

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified on three sites; no errors from the loader in debug logs.

- **WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (Docker):** php -l on all 59 PHP files under PHP 7.4.33, node --check on 3 JS files. MU file written after making mu-plugins writable; unwritable case shows the panel notice. Admin: first visit loads every plugin and learns, later visits filtered (Dashboard 1 of 4, Posts 1 of 4, New post 2 of 4, Pretty Links pages 2 of 4, Akismet page 2 of 4); menus match the full menu except the Customize return= links, which now point to the current screen. WooCommerce, Rank Math, Kadence):** Dashboard 1 of 11, Posts 2 of 11, New post 5 of 11, Rank Math and WooCommerce settings 2 of 11, product categories 3 of 11, all 200 with full menus. Test settings restored afterwards (feature off, MU file and map removed).

title: GH#7: chore: stop recommending EditorsKit in Free Plugins (#7)
body:
## Summary

Free Plugins no longer recommends EditorsKit (`block-options`). Its last release was 1.40.6 in May 2024, tested up to WordPress 6.5, and WordPress plus Kadence Blocks now cover everything it was used for.

- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: removed `block-options` from the `cms` group, with a comment saying why, in the same style as the String Locator note.
- `README.md` and `readme.txt`: changelog lines.

No SEO Pro Stack feature is needed: an audit of the EditorsKit installs on our hosting found no use that WordPress or Kadence could not take over.

## What the sites used, and what replaced it

EditorsKit was on 12 installs (17 sites, counting multisite subsites). Only visibility rules and a few inline formats did anything on the front end. They were ported, checked, and EditorsKit was then deleted from all installs.

| EditorsKit use | Replacement |
|---|---|
| Kadence Row Layout hidden from logged-in users | Row Layout `loggedIn` setting |
| Block shown only to logged-in or logged-out users | Kadence Blocks Pro conditional display (`user_logged_in`) |
| Same, on blocks without conditional display (query filters, core paragraph and group) | Wrapped in a Kadence Column with conditional display |
| Block hidden everywhere (all devices, or both login states) | WordPress Hide (`metadata.blockVisibility`, WordPress 6.9+) |
| Uppercase format on headings | Core heading letter case (`textTransform`) |
| Highlight background in a Kadence heading | Kadence highlight (`<mark class="kt-highlight">`) |
| Nofollow/sponsored link rel, underline | Already saved as plain HTML, no change needed |
| One Styles Manager style (Site Logo) | Unused stub, nothing to port |

## Verification

- `php -l admin/data/free-plugins.php`: no syntax errors. Loading the list: 88 entries, `block-options` absent. (The one duplicate, `fluent-community`, was already on `main`.)
- Sites: each changed post was backed up before and after, the port was run dry and its diffs reviewed, then applied. Each changed page was fetched logged out and logged in (as an administrator) after deleting EditorsKit and purging LiteSpeed. Every block's visibility matches the original EditorsKit settings, with no leaks.
- Home pages of all installs return 200 after removal, apart from one staging site behind its own HTTP password.

title: GH#7: fix: notices tray catches wrapped, late and script-drawn notices; clears top bars (#7)
body:
## Summary

With Hide admin notices on, some notices still showed on the page, and on screens with their own top bar the Notices button sat on top of that bar. This change catches those notices and gives the button its own row where the page has no Screen Options.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php`: notices printed by the notice hooks are marked while the page is drawn (`mark()`), including ones inside another plugin's wrapper. The selectors and early-hide CSS cover wrapped notices. Kept kinds (errors, warnings) go in the panel on screens that hide every notice themselves (WooCommerce, Rank Math), so they can still be read. The inline script moved to a file.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-notices.js` (new): tray button and panel. Takes marked notices, the ones core's `common.js` would move, and notices that scripts add before the first click or keypress. Later notices stay on the page because they answer what the person did. React or Vue notices, such as WooCommerce Analytics' scheduled-updates notice, stay hidden where they are. The panel shows a copy that passes clicks back and disappears when the original goes. On pages without Screen Options or Help, such as WooCommerce, ACF and Rank Math, the button gets its own row above the page's bar. Where a page hides Screen Options itself, it stays hidden and Notices stays.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature notes and changelog.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: separate commit. Plugin Check warned `InputNotSanitized` on `$_GET['page']` in `screen_key()` (from #22). The value was already limited by a regex allowlist. It now also goes through `sanitize_text_field()`, which leaves every allowed value unchanged.

The block editor is still out of scope. Messages about what you just did and inline notices inside page content still stay on the page.

## Verification

- `php -l` and `node --check` on changed files; PHP 7.4.33 lint of the whole plugin: pass.
- Browser check on LocalWP (WordPress 7.1.2, WooCommerce, Rank Math, ACF, Kadence Blocks, test mu-plugin printing info/error/warning/legacy/inline/action notices), 44/44 pass across 13 screens: dashboard, Posts, Plugins, SEO Pro Stack settings, Kadence Blocks home, Rank Math, ACF field groups, WooCommerce Home, Analytics, Orders, Settings, Products. On each screen:

  - no notice is left on the page;

- The same check also covered:
  - the WooCommerce React notice stays in place hidden, the panel shows a copy, and dismissing the copy dismisses the original and lowers the count;
  - the empty Orders list keeps Screen Options hidden while Notices stays;
  - a notice added by script before the first click goes into the panel; one added after a click stays on the page;
  - the settings header starts below the button;

- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (Docker, release-style copy, all 49 features on): smoke run clean, `debug.log` empty. Same browser check without WooCommerce: 16/16 pass.
- Plugin Check on the `.distignore` build: "Checks complete. No errors found." (before the loader commit: 1 warning, in the loader).

title: GH#7: fix: Kadence palette colours in screenshot borders; dark mode styling rules (#7)
body:
## Summary

Checks that the plugin's front-end block styling works with the Kadence Pro dark mode switcher, fixes one bug found, and records the requirement for future work.

- **Bug:** a border colour picked from the palette was written as `var(--wp--preset--color--theme-palette3)`. Kadence (like core) names its variables with kebab-cased slugs, `--wp--preset--color--theme-palette-3`, so the colour never applied (light or dark) and the border fell back to the link colour. `css_value()` now kebab-cases slugs with core's `_wp_to_kebab_case()` (WP 5.8+), and the editor's `cssValue()` uses the same rule, so the `borderColor` attribute and shadow presets resolve as core's style engine does. Per-side preset colours already went through the style engine and were correct.
- **Audit, no change needed:** screenshot pending box uses a translucent neutral with inherited text; captions inherit; the iFrame block border uses `currentColor`; editor-only error text is in the admin UI; the plugin toggle's admin-bar style is not themed by Kadence.
- **AGENTS.md:** new *Front-end styling and dark mode* section (how Kadence switches: body class, palette variables redefined on `<body>`, `<html>` stays light; use `currentColor`/inherit/translucent neutrals/palette variables; no `prefers-color-scheme`; no palette-derived `:root` properties; kebab-cased preset variables; iframes keep the visitor's system scheme) and Testing step 5 (simulate the switcher without Kadence Pro).



## Files Changed

## Summary

Fixes the admin bar plugin menu (Plugins tab, replaces Plugin Toggle) when **Load plugins only where needed** is on, and makes the menu easier to read.

## Summary

Load plugins only where needed no longer adds its own "N of M plugins" item to the admin bar when the Plugins menu (plugin icon) is on. The icon's tooltip also gives the count. With the Plugins menu off, the separate "N of M plugins" item stays, with only the reload link under it.

The reload (`?seoprostack-load-all=1`) now also learns the screen again. Before, it only loaded every plugin for one request and learned nothing. Now that request learns the screen's needs again and updates the post type, taxonomy and block owners, so a box, field or block that went missing comes back.

The pinned order from #36 is reversed: the Plugins menu now sits next to the account menu (rank 0) and the notices bell to its left (rank 1). The bell is hidden until its script has counted the notices, so on the outer side its appearing no longer moves the plugin icon or the account menu.

- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature text and the 0.4.0 changelog lines, including the #36 line, now describing the new order. The features are unreleased.

title: GH#7: fix: notices bell next to the account menu, Plugins menu to its left
body:
## Summary

On the right of the admin bar, the notices bell now always sits next to the account menu (“Hi, …”), with the Plugins menu to its left. Every other plugin's right-hand item goes further left, in its own order. Before, the order depended on hook priorities, so items such as “N of M plugins” or other plugins' icons could land between the bell, the Plugins menu and the account menu.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-admin-bar.php` (new): `SEOProStack_Admin_Bar::pin( $id, $rank )` registers a `top-secondary` node. On `wp_before_admin_bar_render` (priority `PHP_INT_MAX`, after every plugin has added its items) it re-adds the right-hand nodes in this order: other items, pinned items (highest rank furthest left), then WordPress's own items (`my-account`, `recovery-mode`, `search`), which keep their places. `WP_Admin_Bar` keeps nodes in the order they were added, so re-adding is how the order changes. Child items reference their parent by ID and are not touched.
- WordPress 6.6 changed how `top-secondary` is laid out: it now shows items left to right in the order they were added, where 6.2–6.5 float them right so the first added is furthest right (core changesets 58215 and 58748). The order is built for whichever version is running.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php`: pins the bell at rank 0. `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-toggle.php`: pins the Plugins menu at rank 1. Hook priorities are unchanged, so draft #35 (which adds items to the Plugins menu at priority 99) is not affected.
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: loads the new class.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: placement notes and Unreleased changelog lines.

- `php -l` on the changed PHP files: pass.

title: GH#7: fix: notices panel opens on hover, like other admin bar menus
body:
## Summary

The notices bell now behaves like the other admin bar menus. Pointing at it opens the panel, and moving the mouse away closes it. Before, the panel opened and closed only on click.

`admin/js/seoprostack-admin-notices.js`:
- With a mouse, the panel opens after 100 ms over the bell and closes 180 ms after the mouse leaves both the bell and the panel. These are the delays core's admin bar menus use (hoverIntent interval and timeout), so a quick pass over the bell does nothing and moving from the bell down into the panel keeps it open.
- Pointing does not move focus, so text you are typing elsewhere on the page is not interrupted. A mouse click on the bell (also before the delay) only opens it; it never closes a panel you are pointing at.
- Keys and taps open the panel and keep it open until Escape, the bell again or a press elsewhere, as before. Focus moves into the panel.
- The panel stays open while you type in a field inside it.
- Closing resets the hover state, because a hidden panel or bell sends no `pointerleave`. Escape while pointing closes the panel, and it stays closed until the mouse comes back.

`README.md`, `readme.txt`: behaviour notes and Unreleased changelog lines.

## Verification

- `node --check admin/js/seoprostack-admin-notices.js`: pass.
- LocalWP, WordPress 7.1.2, with a release-style copy and "Show example notices" on. A Playwright check passed 29 of 29:
  - hover opens after the delay, with `aria-expanded` and no focus change; a quick pass does not open it;
  - moving from the bell into the panel keeps it open; it is still open within the close delay and closes after moving away;
  - a click while pointing keeps it open, and moving away still closes it;
  - dismissing a notice in the panel lowers the count and keeps the panel open; moving away then closes it;
  - keyboard: Space and Enter open it with focus inside; it stays open when the mouse passes; Escape closes it and puts focus back on the bell; a click elsewhere closes it;
  - Escape while pointing closes it until the mouse comes back;
  - typing in a field inside the panel keeps it open, and a click elsewhere closes it;

body:
For #7

## Why

With many plugins active, the admin bar wraps onto a second line that covers the top of the page and its buttons. You asked for a … menu after WordPress's own items (+ New last) that holds the extra left-hand items, with tick boxes for plugins to keep on the bar.

## What

New feature **More menu in the admin bar** (Admin tab, off by default), in wp-admin and on the site:

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-bar-more.php`: just before the bar renders (`wp_before_admin_bar_render`, priority 100000), moves top-level left-hand items that WordPress didn't add under a new `seoprostack-more` node placed last. Submenus keep their own flyouts. Click or Enter/Space opens it, outside click or Escape closes it, `aria-expanded` stays in sync, and WordPress's `hover` class stays on while it is open so the highlight shows. Without JavaScript it opens on hover as usual. On screens up to 782px, WordPress hides plugin items; the menu shows them with submenus expanded and scrolls within the screen.

title: GH#7: feat: notices bell on every screen with a dot; notices of skipped plugins kept behind it
body:
For #7

## Why

The notices bell came and went between admin screens. Two causes:

1. The bell was hidden while there were no notices, and its count arrived after the icon, so the bar changed as the page loaded.
2. With **Load plugins only where needed**, a screen that skips a plugin also skips that plugin's notices. Example on the test site: Rank Math's "detected new post types" notice showed only on screens that loaded every plugin, never on the Dashboard or Posts list, where Rank Math is skipped.

## What

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php`, `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-notices.js`:

- **Bell on every screen.** It no longer hides when there are no notices. With none, the panel says "No notices."
- **Dot instead of a count.** A 7px dot (9px on phones) in the bar's text colour: white with the default colours, dark with the Light scheme. Not red. The bell never changes width, so nothing on the bar moves. Screen readers still hear "Notices (N)" from the aria-label.
- **Notices of skipped plugins are kept**, much like the menu copy that Load plugins only where needed keeps:
  - On screens that load every plugin, `capture()` wraps, in place, the `admin_notices` / `all_admin_notices` callbacks of skippable plugins. The callback key stays the same, so `remove_action()` / `has_action()` still work. `keep()` stores what each printed, per person, in the `{prefix}seoprostack_stored_notices` user option. Limits: 40 notices, 30 KB each, and only rewritten when something changes or once an hour.
  - On screens that skip plugins, `replay()` prints their kept notices on `admin_notices`. The inline `mark()` script unwraps them, so they are moved behind the bell like any other notice.
  - A kept notice goes when: its plugin stops printing it on the screen it came from; it is dismissed with the core dismiss button or a control whose class, link or words say dismiss/hide/close/later/"No thanks" (`wp_ajax_seoprostack_forget_notice`, nonce-checked; dismissals are remembered for 30 days); or after 12 hours, since links in notices carry nonces. Ordinary links such as "Learn more" do not count as dismissals.
  - Where the plugin loads, the plugin shows its own notice as usual.
- `uninstall.php`: removes the user option on every site.
- `class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: the setting description says notices still show behind the bell when Hide admin notices is on.
- README (feature section, Load plugins section, changelog) and readme.txt (description, changelog). Two older Unreleased lines that said the bell "appears only after counting" now match.

## Verification

- Probe: the bell is at x=1192 on the Dashboard (1 of 10 plugins), the Dashboard with every plugin, and the Posts list (2 of 10). Rank Math's notice was printed with every plugin, then shown as `[stored]` on the Posts list. No dot and "No notices." when empty.

- `seeded.mjs`, 6/6, with seeded kept notices: the expired one is hidden; nothing is left on the page; "Learn more" does not forget; "No thanks" forgets and removes; a notice is dropped after its screen loads every plugin without printing it.

title: GH#7: chore: combined preview on the shared test site (main plus open PRs)
body:
## Summary

The shared local test site was last-copy-wins: each session copied its own worktree, which hid every other session's unmerged work. New scripts/preview-site.sh (excluded from release builds by the existing scripts entry in .distignore and .gitattributes) builds a combined preview: it fetches origin, lists open same-repo PRs with gh, and merges each one onto origin/main in PR order with git merge-tree --write-tree and commit-tree. Nothing is checked out, no branch is written and nothing is pushed; the dangling preview commits are local only. Branches that conflict are left out and listed with the conflicting files. It exports the result with git archive, rsyncs it with the merged tree's .distignore (the same contents as a release build), and writes wp-content/seoprostack-synced-from.txt listing main, the included PRs with their commits and the skipped ones. A mkdir lock in the git common dir stops concurrent runs and takes over a lock left by a dead process or older than 10 minutes. The site path is remembered per clone in the git common dir, so it never reaches the public repo; SEOPROSTACK_PREVIEW_SITE overrides it. It refuses to copy if gh cannot list PRs, because a main-only copy would hide work in progress. It warns when the branch it is run from is missing or has unpushed commits. --dry-run reports without copying. Functions are kept under the 100-line complexity limit. AGENTS.md Testing step 2 now requires the script for the shared site, forbids rsyncing a worktree there, says to push and open a draft PR before asking the user to look, says to run it again after merging, and keeps worktree rsync for private throwaway sites.



## Files Changed

AGENTS.md, scripts/preview-site.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — shellcheck clean, and runs under macOS /bin/bash 3.2. In a scratch repo, merge-tree gave exit 0 with the tree for a clean merge and exit 1 with the tree plus conflicting file names for a conflict, as the script expects. A dry run against the shared site listed main plus PR #53. A real run into a throwaway folder copied main's latest (GH#54 Hosting needs and the #52 reset code) plus PR #53's admin-menu files, without AGENTS.md or scripts. It wrote the stamp and released the lock. A planted lock with a dead PID was taken over. With gh missing from PATH it stopped and copied nothing. Before the first run on the shared site I checked it would lose nothing: the commit already copied there (4072d5e) is an ancestor of PR #53's pushed head, the admin-menu worktree is clean and pushed, and the extra notices file was already in main. #53 merged meanwhile, so the run copied main 909b0f1. The site then returned 200 for / and wp-login.php, with no new debug.log entries. After the refactor into smaller functions, a throwaway copy was identical to the shared site's copy (diff -rq), and the remembered site path was used when no argument was given.

## Summary

Free Plugins no longer sends you to the Plugins screen, and a new **All** view sets up many recommended plugins at once.

- **Cards, in place**: Install Now → **Activate** + **Uninstall** → (activate) **Deactivate** → (deactivate) **Activate** + **Uninstall**. No page loads; each change ends by showing the state the server reports.
- **All view** (first filter link): every recommended plugin in a compact table grouped by category. Checkbox per plugin, per group and Select all; bulk **Install and activate**, **Install**, **Activate**, **Deactivate**, **Uninstall**. Runs one plugin at a time with "N of M: name" progress, a Stop button, and a "Changed / skipped / failed" summary. Bulk Uninstall deactivates active plugins first (with a confirm). A plugin listed in two groups (for example Fluent Community in CRM and LMS) stays in sync.
- Plugins that need a newer WordPress or PHP (new `incompatible` status), WordPress.org-closed plugins and network-active plugins cannot be selected, so bulk runs skip them.

## How

- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`: one `state_buttons()` renderer shared by cards, rows and AJAX replies; `plugin_state()` adds incompatible/unavailable; new `seoprostack_plugin_action` AJAX (`activate`, `deactivate`, `state`) with nonce, `install_plugins` plus `activate_plugin`/`deactivate_plugin` capability checks, and **only slugs from `admin/data/free-plugins.php`** (cannot touch SEO Pro Stack or other plugins). Respects WordPress 6.5+ plugin dependencies when deactivating. Our own activate/deactivate, because core's `activate-plugin` AJAX needs WordPress 6.5 (minimum here is 6.2) and core has no deactivate AJAX.
- Install and uninstall use core `wp.updates.installPlugin` / `deletePlugin` (WordPress 4.6+), so FTP credential prompts work; the credentials modal is printed on the tab.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin.js`: `PluginActions` (single actions) and `Bulk` (selection + sequential runner). `post()` and core calls retry **once** when a page comes back instead of JSON: a just-activated plugin (seen with the Minimal set) redirected the next `admin-ajax.php` request to its welcome screen via `admin_init`, which failed the first bulk deactivate before this fix.
- `admin/includes/class-free-plugins-manager.php`: All link, toolbar and grouped table; rows load per category (4 at a time) using the existing per-category cache.
- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin.css`: list, sticky toolbar, Uninstall button, phone layout. Colours use the existing admin variables (wp-admin only, no front-end impact).
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature text and changelog. No new options, transients or cron, so `uninstall.php` is unchanged.
- Merged `main`'s plugins from outside WordPress.org (Git Updater in GitHub builds): its card and a new All row share `external_state()`; the row has its own Install/Activate links, no checkbox, and says "Needs PHP 8.0 or later" where relevant. `curated_slugs()` leaves external slugs out, so the AJAX endpoint and bulk actions only handle WordPress.org plugins (`slug=git-updater` → 400).

title: GH#66: feat: Hosting needs: plans for low, medium and high traffic from measured numbers
body:
## Summary

Extends Hosting needs (off by default) with hosting to buy for low, medium and high traffic (10,000, 100,000 and 1,000,000 visits a month) and for the traffic measured now: PHP workers, RAM, CPU cores, object cache and kind of hosting, plus the OPcache settings and PHP memory limit that suit them all.

- **Traffic sampling:** 1 in 20 requests that reach PHP records its time and hour in `seoprostack_hosting_traffic` (not autoloaded, 7 days, `seoprostack_hosting_sample_rate` filter, 0 stops it). The p95 of page times replaces typical times once 30 are sampled.
- **Site facts:** database size, postmeta rows, products and autoloaded options from table statistics, cached hourly in the `seoprostack_hosting_facts` transient and cleared on plugin (de)activation. Page cache and shop/membership/course plugins are detected and change how much traffic reaches PHP.
- **OPcache sizing:** compiled/source ratio is measured from `opcache_get_status(true)` when readable (2.6 assumed otherwise). A full OPcache now gets a suggestion big enough for all the code that can load. Site Health Info also gives settings for the code of every installed plugin.
- **Plans:** `includes/class-seoprostack-hosting-plans.php` holds every assumption as a constant. Workers come from Little's law (burst requests per second × p95 seconds, +1, with a minimum per level). RAM covers workers, OPcache, database, system and object cache, ×1.25 for bursts, and at least 1 GB per core. CPU allows 0.7 core per busy worker. The table and Site Health say what is assumed.
- **Advice:** page cache, object cache (postmeta > 500k or products > 10k), autoloaded options over 1 MB, and PHP older than 8.2.
- Fixed the plans table on phones: core's 782 px list-table rules (WordPress 7 uses flex rows) were stacking its cells.

## Files Changed

README.md, readme.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-hosting-plans.php (new), includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php, uninstall.php

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium. Adds an option write on 1 in 20 requests. Hosting needs is off by default.
