title: GH#7: feat: Faster editor with Kadence Blocks (design library on demand)
body:
For #7

## What

New Speed feature, **Faster editor with Kadence Blocks**, off by default.

Kadence Blocks prints its whole design library (every pattern's pre-rendered HTML) into each block editor screen as `kadence_blocks_params_library` (`includes/class-kadence-blocks-editor-assets.php`, around line 437 in Kadence Blocks). With every recommended plugin active, `post-new.php` weighed about 24.5 MB, and roughly 15 MB of that was this variable.

The feature returns false from Kadence's own `kadence_blocks_preload_design_library` filter. Kadence already does this itself when Gravity Forms is active, so it is a supported path. The editor JS (`dist/blocks-rowlayout.js`, `getPatterns` and `getAIWizardData`) then fetches the library and the AI wizard settings from Kadence's REST routes the first time they are needed, and keeps them in `window`.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`: new feature, one filter, admin only.
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: registered after Delayed Google Analytics (Speed tab).
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature section and changelog.

No new options, post meta, transients or cron hooks, so `uninstall.php` is unchanged. No external service is contacted that Kadence does not already contact.

## Testing

Measured on the shared test site (85 active plugins), with a temporary mu-plugin that applied the same filter only to requests with a test query parameter:

| `post-new.php` | Size | Server time (3 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Preload on (Kadence default) | 24,434–24,532 KB | 6,875 / 4,626 / 3,395 ms |
| Preload off | 8,691 KB | 2,815 / 3,109 / 3,158 ms |

Through the feature itself on the combined preview (`scripts/preview-site.sh`, PRs #70 and #73 included), `post-new.php` was 8,788 / 8,689 / 8,697 KB (3,912 / 2,964 / 3,238 ms).

Browser check (Playwright, `post-new.php`, then **Design Library** in the editor toolbar):

| | Feature on | Feature off (Kadence default) |
|---|---|---|
| `window.kadence_blocks_params_library` at load | `undefined` | object (~15 MB inline) |
| REST requests after opening the library | `get_library … meta=info` (805 KB) + `meta=html` (14.4 MB) | `get_library … force_reload=true … meta=html` (14.4 MB) |
| Library shown | 833 patterns with previews | same |
| Console errors | identical set in both (404s and React warnings from other plugins) | |

With Kadence's default, opening the library downloads the 14.4 MB HTML again even though it was already inline, so the HTML is sent twice. With the feature on it is sent once, only to people who open the library.

- `php -l` on changed PHP files.
- `debug.log`: nothing from this change.
- Merged `origin/main` after v0.5.0; changelog lines are under Unreleased and `@since 0.5.1`.

- **Load plugins only where needed**: pages that Freemius takes over (WP Sheet Editor's welcome and setup pages) were recorded as belonging to the plugin holding the shared Freemius copy (Git Updater), so they opened blank. They now belong to the plugin Freemius works for (`plugin_for_sdk()`). The map is learned again (`MAP_VERSION` 2).
- **Organise the admin menu**: upgrade links (Upgrade, Go Pro, Unlock Pro…) and pages without a name are left out. So are entries in a new catalog `hidden` list (Freesoul's holder menu, WP Sheet Editor's Freemius opt-in prompts, an AutomatorWP advert, MasterStudy's 29 "Unlock this addon" pages; PRO Addons still lists them), and pages registered without a menu (such as setup wizards), which core never shows. Their pages still open and keep their place for the safeguards; choosing a place for one shows it again. With Complianz, Post Type Switcher, Burst, Rank Math and Sticky posts columns, the Posts Title column was 0 px wide, and columns without a width of their own (Rank Math, Page views) were 0 px too. When the main column is under a fifth of the table, or a column is squeezed out, the script gives the main column a quarter and narrows the others towards the narrowest they can be without breaking words. If space is still short, the main column gives up some of its quarter (down to 120 px) before other columns break words. Narrow columns whose content fits (checkboxes, icons) keep their width. It refits on Screen Options changes and window resizes and does nothing at phone widths, where WordPress stacks columns. Nothing is stored.

| Profile (`profile.php`) | 1.9–2.2 s, all 85 | Dashboard 0.67 s (15 of 85) |
| Edit user (`user-edit.php`) | 2.0 s, all 85 | Users list 0.31 s (15 of 85) |
| Add user (`user-new.php`) | 2.0 s, all 85 | Comments 0.31 s (15 of 85) |
| Tools (`tools.php`) | 2.1 s, all 85 | Rank Math page 0.36 s (16 of 85) |
| About screens | 1.9 s, all 85 | |

Profile, Edit user and Add user were in the never-filter list on purpose, because saving those forms without a plugin's fields can clear its values. Tools, Media › Add New and the About screens had no screen key, so they always loaded every plugin. The admin bar also showed no count on those screens, so you could not tell whether the setting was working there.

## What

`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`

Saving (POST) still loads every plugin, so any plugin that saves profile fields also loads on the form and its fields are always there. User screens also load plugins learned as changing permissions (`editable_roles`, `user_has_cap` and the like).
- `TOOLS_HOOKS` (`tool_box`) and `UPLOAD_HOOKS` (plupload and upload UI hooks), plus any `*-profile.php`, `*-user-edit.php`, `*-user-new.php`, `*-tools.php` and `*-media-new.php` hook (`load-`, `admin_head-`, `admin_footer-`…).
- `state()['reason']` says why a request loads every plugin: `always`, `learning`, `error` or `needed`.

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- Learns the new kinds through `form_plugins()`.
- On screens that load every plugin, the top of the admin bar Plugins menu says why, such as “This screen always loads all 85 plugins” or “All 85 plugins loaded while SEO Pro Stack checks this screen”. After an error it also offers “check every screen again”.

Settings screens (`options-*.php`), widgets and menus still load every plugin: `options.php` sets a registered setting to null when its field is not posted, so learning them safely needs more than hooks.

title: GH#7: perf: SEO Pro Stack settings load only the plugins they need
body:
## What

With **Load plugins only where needed** on, SEO Pro Stack's own settings page (Settings › SEO Pro Stack) used to load every active plugin, so every tab paid for all of them. On the test site with 85 active plugins that was 2.2–4.5 s per tab and a 4.8 MB page, of which our own markup was about 38 KB; the rest was other plugins' scripts (one font list alone was 526 KB).

The page is now an ordinary learned screen. Alongside SEO Pro Stack it loads only:

- the plugins that register post types, taxonomies or widgets (the settings offer those as choices);
- plugins that change permissions (role choices);
- plugins that use SEO Pro Stack's own `seoprostack_*` hooks (extra tabs or settings);
- plugins that hook the page itself, as for any plugin page.

## Safety

- Saving a setting goes through admin-ajax, which always loads every plugin, so values are checked against the full lists.
- On a screen that loads fewer plugins, a `multi` field also shows saved choices that are not offered right now, so saving the field never drops a choice belonging to a skipped plugin.
- SEO Pro Stack now reads the stored active plugin list (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::stored_active_plugins()` / `::is_active()`) wherever it shows or decides what is active: replaced-plugin checks, the Plugin loading list itself (otherwise saving it would untick skipped plugins), Free Plugins and link cards, Plugin sizes, Hosting needs, More menu sources, migrations and Git Updater detection.
- Tidy the dashboard no longer overwrites its list of seen dashboard widgets on a Dashboard that skipped plugins (it used to drop their widgets from the choices).
- Map format 3: every screen is learned once more after updating.

title: GH#7: feat: skip admin tools on the site with Load plugins only where needed
body:
## What

**Load plugins only where needed** now also covers the site itself, with a new list, **Plugins to skip on the site**, and **Also skip them for people who are logged in** (off by default). It replaces what most of our sites use Freesoul Deactivate Plugins Pro for on the front end ("Frontend everywhere" and "Unlogged"); FDP's per post type, search and URL rules are not covered, so FDP stays on the Free Plugins list.

- Ticked plugins are skipped on page views: GET or HEAD for the site's `index.php`, not the REST API, whose query arguments are only search, page numbers and campaign tags (`s`, `paged`, `page`, `cpage`, `p`, `page_id`, `utm_*`, `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`…). Any other argument may be a link a plugin acts on (FluentCRM unsubscribe, downloads, magic login, `wc-ajax`, MainWP), so it loads every plugin, as do logins, form posts, cron, AJAX, REST, XML-RPC and WP-CLI.
- **Learned, not guessed.** Once per set of active plugins, the first page view loads every plugin and notes, for each plugin, what it registered: shortcodes, blocks, widgets and public content types; hooks that change pages, addresses or output; login checks; email; the admin bar; and core (pluggable) functions it replaced. The list shows this next to each plugin ("adds to pages", "nothing seen on the site"…), plus "Freesoul Deactivate Plugins skips it on the site" when FDP's lists include it (read only).
- **Always load:** plugins that change logins or the plugin list (`login_url`, `determine_current_user`, `option_active_plugins`…) or replace a pluggable function; a ticked plugin that a loading plugin needs (`Requires Plugins`, WooCommerce/Elementor headers, add-on names).

## Safety

- Nothing is deactivated (`keep_active` as in wp-admin).
- New for every filtered request (wp-admin too): rewrite rules made with fewer plugins are never saved; a flush empties them, and the next full request rebuilds them.
- A fatal error or a plugin trying to deactivate itself on a filtered page makes the site load every plugin, and the settings say which page and plugin, until the list is saved again.
- One request learns at a time (a short lock); `?seoprostack-load-all=1` loads every plugin, and for administrators learns the site again.
- New options `seoprostack_plugin_front` (autoloaded, small) and `seoprostack_plugin_front_lock`, both removed on uninstall and forgotten with the rest of what was learned.

## Verification

On the shared preview site (85 active plugins, Kadence, WooCommerce, Tutor, Rank Math and others):

- **Learning:** one logged-out page view learned the site: 3 plugins always load (Tutor and WooCommerce on `determine_current_user`, FluentSMTP replaces `wp_mail`), 12 dependency links (WooCommerce extensions), 15 plugins with nothing seen. `pre_get_*` hooks are now matched by name (`pre_get_posts`, `pre_get_document_title`…), so cron-only hooks such as `pre_get_ready_cron_jobs` no longer count as page output.
- **Same output:** with those 15 admin tools ticked (update-related plugins left out), 14 logged-out URLs (home, posts, page, event directory, checkout redirect, shop, courses, events, category, search, 404, feed, sitemap redirect, robots.txt) gave the same status and **0 differing lines** compared with `?seoprostack-load-all=1`.
- **Skipping happens:** an in-process front request reports `mode=filter skipped=15 loaded=70`; logged in with "Also skip them…" on, the Plugins menu says "70 of 85 plugins loaded on this page", with one reload that checks the site again (no "check every screen" link on the site).
- **Guards:** POST, `?add-to-cart=12` and `/wp-json/` load every plugin; `?s=test&utm_source=x&paged=2` and the feed skip.
- **Fallback:** a fatal error on a filtered page showed core's error with "SEO Pro Stack loaded fewer plugins on this page. Reload it: the site now loads every plugin."; the next request loaded all 85; the settings named the page and time; saving the list cleared it and skipping resumed.
- **Speed:** with only these light admin tools ticked, the home page median (11 runs) was 1.01 s vs 1.05 s with every plugin. The gain depends on what a site ticks, so the docs make no speed claim.
- `php -l` clean on PHP 7.4 (Docker `php:7.4-cli`) and 8.5. `readme.txt` is 9,514 bytes.

title: GH#7: fix: admin menu opens on plugins' post type lists; lean loading recovers from Query Monitor fatals
body:
## What

Two fixes found while checking every admin submenu link on the test site (85 active plugins), after the report that Kadence submenu entries don't open the left menu.

### 1. Organise the admin menu: the menu doesn't open on post type lists shown in another plugin's menu

Kadence Blocks registers Forms, Navigations and Headers with `show_in_menu => 'kadence-blocks'`. On `edit.php?post_type=kadence_header`, core passes `edit.php?post_type=kadence_header` to the `parent_file` filter and finds the real parent (`kadence-blocks`) only afterwards in `get_admin_page_parent()`. `build_menu()` only treats an entry as current when its slug equals `$parent_file`, so the Administrators menu stayed closed and no entry was marked.

Fix (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`, `organise()`): if `$parent_file` is not a top-level entry and the matched entry (`current_entry()`) stays in its own menu, use that entry's menu (`from`) as `$parent_file` before building the Administrators and Developers menus. New helper `is_top()`.

### 2. Load plugins only where needed: screens that failed under Query Monitor kept failing

Admin Columns' settings (`options-general.php?page=codepress-admin-columns`) failed on every visit: Admin Columns calls `class_exists(OrderUtil::class)`, some loaded plugin's autoloader still finds WooCommerce's class file while WooCommerce is skipped, and `OrderUtil::custom_orders_table_usage_is_enabled()` calls the missing `wc_get_container()`. The loader should mark such a screen to load every plugin after one failure, but Query Monitor's exception handler shows the error and calls `exit` (`collectors/php_errors.php`, `output_fatal()`). So WordPress's `wp_php_error_message` never runs and `error_get_last()` is empty at shutdown.

Fix (`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`, `on_shutdown()`): a 500 status at shutdown on a filtered screen also marks the screen. This works whichever handler printed the page. It can only make a screen load more plugins, never fewer.

## Not changed (outside SEO Pro Stack)

- WP Sheet Editor's editor pages (`admin.php?page=vgse-bulk-edit-*`) answer "Spreadsheet not enabled" even with every plugin loaded. `Freemius::_prepare_admin_menu` (priority 999999999) removes the page from `$submenu`, so core can't find its parent and refuses it.
- Hash-routed app pages (FluentCRM, Fluent Support, Bit apps, Ninja Tables…) always mark their first entry; core does the same.
- TranslatePress redirects to its opt-in page under a hidden parent; core doesn't open a menu there either.

### 3. Add New screens of those post types marked the wrong entry

On `post-new.php?post_type=kadence_header`, core sets `$submenu_file` to the menu's own slug when there is no Add New entry, which marked Kadence's Settings page (`admin.php?page=kadence-blocks`). `build_menu()` now ignores that fallback on post type screens, so `mark_post_type_list()` marks Headers.

## Verification (combined preview, 85 active plugins)

- `php -l` on both files.
- `edit.php?post_type=kadence_header|kadence_form|kadence_navigation`: Administrators opens, Kadence › Headers/Forms/Navigations marked (before: no menu open).
- `post-new.php?post_type=kadence_header`: Headers marked (before: Settings). `post-new.php` (Posts › Add Post) and `post-new.php?post_type=acf-field-group` (Developers › SCF › Field Groups) unchanged.
- Admin Columns' settings: first visit fails (Query Monitor's page), second visit loads every plugin and opens Administrators › Settings › Admin Columns (before: failed on every visit).
- Script that opens all 368 submenu links: 118 → 109 flagged, no new entries. The rest are the "Not changed" cases above, full-screen editors (Customiser, YellowPencil, Woo email customiser), plugins redirecting to their own onboarding (Lasso, MasterStudy, WooCommerce) and label counts.

title: GH#7: fix: admin screens no longer jump as they load
body:
## What

Two admin screens moved after they drew, found while checking the reported gap and jump under the admin bar (test site, 85 active plugins). Layout shifts were recorded in Chromium with a `layout-shift` PerformanceObserver.

### 1. Hide admin notices: empty boxes that a script fills later

MasterStudy LMS (`_core/libraries/announcement/item-announcements.php`) prints `<div data-mount="stm-item-announcements-notice">` on `all_admin_notices` on every screen and enqueues `https://stylemixthemes.com/item-announcements/js/app.js`. Once that loads, a Vue app puts an empty `<div class="announcements-notices">` with `margin-top: 8px` in the box. On SEO Pro Stack's settings, `.sps-wrap` moved from y=32 to y=40 about 1.9 s into the load (shift 0.0048), leaving an 8px gap under the admin bar. Blocking the stylemixthemes.com script in the browser removed the shift, which confirms the cause.

The marking script ran when the box was still empty, so it was neither moved nor hidden.

Fix:
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php` `mark()`: an empty element (no child elements, no text) printed straight above the page is marked `data-sps-notice="wait"`. It is hidden with the other notices while the page loads.
- The marking script also watches `#wpbody-content`'s own children while a box waits: Vue 2 replaces the element it mounts on (insert the new one, then remove the old one, in one batch), so the new element is marked `wait` before the next paint and passed on with a `sps-notice-wait` event.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-notices.js` `wait()`: keeps a waiting box hidden (`sps-notice-away`) while it is empty, or while what it holds was already taken to the panel. When a script fills it with a notice or banner (notice classes, or class/id words such as "notice" or "announcement", as in the marking script), it goes behind the bell (a copy, if Vue or React owns it). Anything else (no notice words, or a dialog) is shown where it is.
- `render()` no longer puts an empty copy of a script-owned notice in the panel, so an empty box never shows the dot.

### 2. Tidy the dashboard: empty columns took 250px once core's script ran

With rearranging off, Tidy the dashboard leaves the side column empty. Core's `postbox.js` marks empty columns `.empty-container` when the page is ready, and core's `dashboard.css` gives them `height: 250px`. The lock CSS reset `min-height` and the border, but not `height` or the newer `outline`, and was printed in the footer. Container 3 moved from y=114 to y=352 (shift 0.0475).

Fix (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-dashboard-layout.php`): the style moves to `admin_head` (`lock_style()`) and sets `height: 0; outline: 0` and the column's own `margin: 0 8px 20px` (core's empty style uses `margin: 4px`, which moved the next column up 12px). The drag-stopping script stays in the footer.

## Not changed (outside SEO Pro Stack)

- Pages opened in the classic editor on the test site because of a test-only must-use file left over from earlier checks (`sps-test-classic.php`). It has been removed from the test site.
- The post editor no longer opened full screen for one admin because FluentCRM's email editor (`assets/guten-editor/index.js`) turns off `fullscreenMode` in the shared `core/edit-post` preferences, which are saved per person. It is reset on the test site; FluentCRM will turn it off again whenever its email editor is opened.
- MasterStudy LMS also loads its announcements script, its styles and `stylemixthemes.com/api/announcements/…json` from the browser on every admin screen where it loads. SEO Pro Stack does not block them.

## Verification

- `php -l` (PHP 8.5 and 7.4) on both PHP files, `node --check` on the script.
- Combined preview (Chromium 1440×900, logged-in admin, `layout-shift` observer):
  - SEO Pro Stack settings: before, `.sps-wrap` 32→40 (0.0048) and an 8px gap under the admin bar; after, no shift in the page, `.sps-wrap` at y=32, MasterStudy's replaced box marked `wait` with `display: none`, bell panel with 12 notices and the dot.
  - Dashboard: before, container 3 114→352 (0.0475); first fix 114→102 (0.0015); after, no shift in the page.
  - Left: one 0.0002 shift in the admin bar on every screen (items widen by a few pixels as a font loads), not from this change.
- `readme.txt` stays under 10 KB.

title: GH#7: feat: Quiet Freemius prompts
body:
## What

New feature, off by default: **Quiet Freemius prompts** (Admin tab, `freemius_quiet`), in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-freemius-quiet.php`.

Plugins that bundle the Freemius SDK (WP Sheet Editor and its add-ons, Git Updater) each add an opt-in notice on every admin screen, Opt In / Upgrade / Add-Ons links on the Plugins screen, trial and affiliate offers, a redirect to the opt-in page on activation, and a deactivation survey modal printed in full on the Plugins screen for every such plugin.

## Why not unload Freemius

The plugins call the SDK directly (licence checks, menu building, `*_fs()->can_use_premium_code()` and the like), so stopping it from loading would fatal or break them. This feature removes the prompts only:

- Freemius's own per-plugin filters (`fs_{tag}_{affix}` via `$fs->add_filter()`): `redirect_on_activation`, `show_deactivation_feedback_form`, `show_trial`, `show_affiliate_program_notice`, `is_submenu_visible` (pricing, addons, affiliation; also gates the Upgrade and Add-Ons row links) and `show_admin_notice` (`connect_account`, `promotion` type, and `update-nag` unless the plugin is premium-only).
- After Freemius's `admin_init` (priority 10), removes its `admin_footer` deactivation dialog for plugins that are not registered (no subscription to cancel) and its opt-out dialog for plugins that are not opted in, and drops the `opt-in-or-opt-out {slug}` row link for those.

Nothing is stored: no plugin is opted in or out, and switching the setting off brings every prompt back. Kept: licence activation, Account, Contact Us, Support, licence and payment notices, Opt Out for opted-in plugins, and the opt-in screen a plugin shows in place of its own page until "Skip" is chosen once.

See the PR comments for before/after measurements on the preview site.

title: GH#7: feat: Dashboard and Menus load only the plugins they need
body:
## What

Two more screens learn what they need with **Load plugins only where needed**.

### Dashboard

The Dashboard skipped every ticked plugin, so their boxes (WooCommerce reviews and setup, Fluent Forms, Fluent Support, FluentSMTP, Burst, Debug Log Manager) disappeared. It now learns which plugins own the boxes still in `wp_meta_boxes['dashboard']` at `admin_footer`, after **Hide dashboard widgets** and **Tidy the dashboard** have removed theirs, and loads only those. Hiding a box with either feature also stops its plugin loading there.

### Appearance › Menus

`nav-menus.php` was in `NEVER`. It now has the screen kind `menus`, learned from:

- plugins on `MENU_HOOKS` (`wp_nav_menu_item_custom_fields`, `wp_edit_nav_menu_walker`, `wp_setup_nav_menu_item`, `wp_update_nav_menu_item` and other menu filters and save hooks, `nav_menu_items_{type}`) and `*-nav-menus.php` hooks. Saving loads every plugin, so a plugin that saves item fields must show them, as with profile fields;
- owners of meta boxes on the `nav-menus` screen;
- owners of post types and taxonomies with `show_in_nav_menus`, and of objects already in a menu (`_menu_item_object`), so no item shows as "Invalid".

Menu locations have no owner to learn. The learned list is stored as `menu_locations`; if a filtered request is missing one (a skipped plugin adds it), `check_menu_locations()` on `load-nav-menus.php` sets the screen to every plugin and reloads it. Otherwise saving would take the menu out of a location that was not shown.

### Widgets: stays full

`widgets.php` keeps loading every plugin, now with the reason in `NEVER`: opening it runs `retrieve_widgets()` (classic screen directly, block screen through its preloaded `/wp/v2/sidebars` request), which removes unregistered widgets and sidebars from `sidebars_widgets` and saves the result.

### Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `dashboard_plugins()`, `menu_plugins()`, `learn()` stores `menu_locations`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `MENU_HOOKS`, `menus` kind, `check_menu_locations()`, `MAP_VERSION` 3 → 4 (every site learns again once).

title: GH#89: feat: Ask before licence checks (once now, once a day or never)
body:
## What

New, off by default: **Ask before licence checks** (Plugins tab). Premium plugins' and themes' licence checks wait for the site owner's say, per plugin and server:

- **Allow once now**: the next check goes through (within the hour; five minutes once it starts, for checks made of several calls), then the owner is asked again.
- **Once a day**: the first check each day goes through; the plugin gets that same answer for the rest of the day, so pages do not wait for the maker's server. A failed check is retried after an hour.
- **Never**: no check is made.

Until a choice is made, nothing is sent and the plugin gets `http_request_failed` (as if the server could not be reached). Administrators are asked in a dialog on the next admin screen; **Ask me tomorrow** hides it for a day. The Plugins screen has a **Licence checks** view link and a row link per plugin to see and change the choices.

Never held: WordPress's update checks, update details and downloads (by call stack and by address), WordPress.org, the site itself, and calls from WordPress or SEO Pro Stack. Runs at `pre_http_request` priority 100, so requests already answered or blocked by another plugin are left alone.

Also adds the owner-control / performance-first rule to `AGENTS.md` → Code rules, as asked in #89.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-licence-calls.php`: the feature (detection, holding, daily answer cache, choices, Plugins screen links, dialog).
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: registered in `$core_features`.
- `uninstall.php`: removes `seoprostack_licence_calls`, `seoprostack_lc_*` transients (with the other `seoprostack_*` transients) and `seoprostack_licence_later` user meta.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (10,229 bytes, under 10 KB), `AGENTS.md`.

## Storage and performance

- One option, not autoloaded, written only when something changes (new entry, choice, first held, a call made); "last seen" at most once a minute, so held checks do not write on every page.
- Request forms (which can hold licence keys) are never stored; a hash of the call keys the kept answer. Kept answers are dropped per plugin when its choice changes.

## Verification

Throwaway WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 site (Docker) with a stand-in premium plugin that checks its licence on every admin screen and during the update check, against a stand-in licence server that logs each hit:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Feature off | check reaches the server |
| On, no choice | held, dialog shown, 0 hits |
| Once a day | 1 hit, then the same answer reused on later screens (0 more hits), 1 kept answer |
| Never | held |
| Update check while Never | reaches the server |
| Allow once now | checks go through; after the window, held and asked again |
| Ask me tomorrow | dialog hidden; Plugins link still opens it |
| `debug.log` | empty |

- `php -l` on every changed PHP file (PHP 8 and 7.4).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: 0 errors, 0 warnings on both zips (no `plugin_updater_detected`).
- Dialog screenshots at 1280×800 and 390×780: fits, no console errors.

Not yet tested with a real premium plugin's licence server; worth checking how one behaves with its checks held before relying on Never.

Resolves #89

title: GH#90: feat: Disable Bloat parity: tidy admin, WooCommerce and login screens, simpler editor, WordPress extras, lighter WooCommerce pages
body:
## What

Six new features, off by default, that do most of Disable Bloat's job. While Disable Bloat (free or PRO) is active they import its switches once and wait, as other replacing features do:

| Feature | Tab | What it removes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tidy admin screens | Admin | "Thank you for creating with WordPress" footer, the core update notice for people who cannot update, optionally the file editors (`map_meta_cap`) |
| Tidy WooCommerce admin | Admin | Marketplace suggestions, Extensions menu, WooCommerce.com connect notices, "Get the app" in new order emails (WooCommerce's own filters) |
| Tidy the login screen | Admin | Logo links to the site with the site's name, WordPress logo hidden, optional language menu |
| Simpler block editor | Content | Welcome guides and block directory; optionally core and Pattern Directory patterns, template editor (classic themes) and fullscreen mode |
| Remove WordPress extras | Speed | Emoji script, version tag, RSD/WLW links, shortlink, comment reply where unused; optionally Dashicons, jQuery Migrate, comment autolinks, feed links, feeds |
| Lighter WooCommerce pages | Speed | WooCommerce scripts and styles, cart fragments and Stripe product-page buttons outside shop pages and pages with WooCommerce blocks or shortcodes |

It also imports Disable Bloat's W logo (Hide admin bar items), Dashboard boxes and widgets (Dashboard and sidebar widgets). All mappings live in `SEOProStack_Disable_Bloat::MAP`. Settings version 6.

Disable Bloat does more than this (Heartbeat, XML-RPC, REST API, resource hints, revisions, auto-updates, third-party plugin switches). So the Plugins screen does not simply say it can go. A new `seoprostack_replaced_plugin_extras` filter lets it name the switches that are on and not covered: "...takes over once you deactivate it, except for these, which SEO Pro Stack does not do: Heartbeat, Disable XML-RPC". Pro Plugins no longer lists Disable Bloat PRO.

This is the first step for #90: Lighter WooCommerce pages dequeues WooCommerce's assets on non-shop pages. Skipping WooCommerce's PHP page by page (the aim of #90) is still to do.

## Decisions

- Welcome guides and fullscreen mode are per-person editor preferences. A client script raced core on WordPress 6.2, which loads saved preferences asynchronously and overwrote the change on a first visit. These choices now filter the `persisted_preferences` user meta read (`get_user_metadata`), so editors open with them off, with no script and nothing stored.
- The file editors are refused through `map_meta_cap` rather than by defining `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT`, so switching the choice off brings them back and Plugin Check has nothing to flag.
- Disable Bloat's "Remove DNS prefetch" removes all resource hints. That is broader than emoji, so it is not mapped; it is listed as not covered.
- Order attribution (`wc-order-attribution`) is left on every page: it records the landing page.

## Files

- New: `includes/class-seoprostack-disable-bloat.php` (map, import helpers, coverage check), `includes/features/class-seoprostack-{admin-tidy,woo-tidy,login-screen,editor-tidy,wp-extras,woo-light}.php`.
- Changed: `includes/class-seoprostack.php` (registration), `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php` (DB_VERSION 6, docblock), `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-bar-hide.php` and `class-seoprostack-widget-control.php` (imports), `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php` (partial-coverage lines), `admin/data/pro-plugins.php`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (9.6 KB).
- No new options, meta, transients or cron.

## Verification

- `php -l` on all changed files (local PHP and `php:7.4-cli`). `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors. `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: WordPress.org zip 0 errors and 0 warnings; the GitHub zip has only the expected updater findings.
- Throwaway site (WordPress 7.1.2, WooCommerce 11.1.2, Kadence, Disable Bloat 4.0.0 from WordPress.org): seeded 14 Disable Bloat switches plus PRO's Dashboard list, deleted `seoprostack_options` and `seoprostack_db_version`, activated. Every mapped switch was imported (`db=6`) and `uncovered()` returned Heartbeat and XML-RPC. The Plugins-screen notice showed the partial line with a Deactivate link.
- After deactivating Disable Bloat, a plain page had no WooCommerce scripts or styles, emoji or shortlink. The block page (`woocommerce/product-new`) and the product page kept `woocommerce`, `wc-add-to-cart` and the rest. The login logo links home. The Dashboard hid the WooCommerce Status, Welcome and Events boxes and the W logo. The Extensions menu entry is removed when chosen. The post editor has no block directory or footer text. Settings → Speed renders the new cards.
- WordPress 6.2 with PHP 7.4 (`wordpress:php7.4-apache`), all six features on with every choice: front end, login, post editor and settings return 200. Feeds return 301 to home, and the theme editor returns 403 with its menu links gone. In Playwright, the editor opened with the welcome guide and fullscreen off, with no console errors, on both 6.2 and 7.1 with fresh preferences.
- `debug.log` stayed empty on both sites.
- Not checked: the Kadence dark mode (no front-end styles added) and a real Stripe gateway (the filter is Stripe's own).

title: GH#123: fix: fitted admin menu fills the open menu, same width on every screen, names fit
body:
## Summary

Fixes "Fit the menu to its names" (Organise the admin menu, from #120, unreleased, on by default).

- **No strip beside the open menu.** Core keeps `#adminmenu .wp-submenu` at 160 px, so the open menu's in-place list stayed 160 px inside the wider sidebar. The gap showed the sidebar background or the current entry's highlight. In `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`, the in-place list now has `width: auto` (≥ 961 px, sidebar expanded).
- **Names fit.** `fit()` measured with `scrollWidth`. That leaves out the padding after the text and never reports less than the current width, so "Debug Log Manager" and "Scheduled Actions" still wrapped. It now measures the text with a Range and adds the padding (`room()` in `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`). RTL is handled.
- **Same width on every screen.** Every menu's entries count, open or not, with third-level lists at their in-place indent (38 px). They are shown for the measurement, like folded sections. Before, the width depended on which menu was open. The script checks again on `load` and only ever widens, in case styles printed later make names longer.
- **Hanging indent.** In the Administrators and Developers menus, the entry icon sits in the link's padding (absolute, logical properties), so a name that still wraps past 280 px lines up under its first line.
- README updated. The changelog line for this unreleased feature still holds.

Resolves #123

## Verification

Throwaway sites, latest WordPress + WooCommerce, LiteSpeed Cache, Debug Log Manager, WP Crontrol, and so on; WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4.

- Before: Tools → Scheduled Actions measured 165 px for the sidebar and 160 px for the list (5 px strip), and Debug Log Manager and Scheduled Actions wrapped. Posts measured 164 px.
- After: 184 px for the sidebar and the open list on Scheduled Actions, Posts and LiteSpeed Cache, the same on 3 reloads each and on WP 6.2. The widest entry is "Export Personal Data" (third level). No names wrap and there is no strip. The LiteSpeed in-place list and the hover flyouts (second and third level) look right. At 900 px the sidebar collapses as before, and the block editor is unchanged in full screen. No page errors.
- `node --check admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` passes.

Burst 3.7.2 registers `Admin::create_js_file()` on `burst_after_saved_fields` (`includes/Admin/class-admin.php:80`). Its `App::rest_api_fields_set()` fires that hook after saving any field (`includes/Admin/App/class-app.php:2396`). `create_js_file()` unconditionally writes a temporary tracking script and moves it into place (`includes/Admin/class-admin.php:627-629`).

A real authenticated HTTP save of **only** `dismiss_non_error_notices=true` succeeded and replaced the generated JavaScript file (inode changed). Empty presets are rejected by `includes/class-seoprostack-presets.php:103-105`, so a notes-only Burst preset cannot satisfy the required lifecycle. One-time notice dismissal state and site-specific report recipients are also unsuitable shared preferences.

Required brief-owner decision: explicitly permit admin-only preferences whose normal save handler incidentally rebuilds otherwise unrelated JavaScript, or revise the acceptance criteria to allow a documented no-preset verdict for Burst. Neither authorization exists in #102, #7, PR #96 or AGENTS.md. The smallest recovery is a brief update; no production save hooks should be bypassed or expanded without it.

title: GH#144: fix: plugins' fixed bars follow the fitted admin menu
body:
Resolves #144

## What

With **Fit the menu to its names** on, other plugins' fixed headers, footers, notices and panels that were laid out for WordPress's usual 160px menu now move over or narrow by the extra width, so the wider menu no longer covers them (for example Fluent Support's setup footer).

## How

Universal detection instead of a per-plugin list (`admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`, `follow()` / `place()` / `watch()`):

- Checks elements with `position: fixed` (and `absolute` positioned on `<body>`) once the page is ready, then added elements and elements whose `class`/`style` changes (MutationObserver, batched every 50ms; big changed subtrees beyond 300 elements only check the changed element).
- Starts under the wider menu (160px up to the fitted width), not centred → `sps-fit-start` (from `left`) or `sps-fit-margin` (from `margin-left`), keeping its own offset in `--sps-fit-start` / `--sps-fit-margin`.
- Spans the whole window with 160px+ start padding → `sps-fit-pad` (Freemius `.fs-modal`).
- Now runs off the far side by the extra width (`width: calc(100% - 160px)`) → `sps-fit-width` with `--sps-fit-gap`, `box-sizing: border-box`.
- Skips the admin menu and toolbar, elements a script positions inline (`left`, `right`, `inset`, `transform`, `translate`: dropdowns, popovers) and centred dialogs.
- Re-checks a followed element when its own class or style changes, so drawers that slide away are not pinned. Transitions are paused while it moves.
- Right-to-left aware (logical properties; `body.rtl` measured from the right).

`admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css` applies the classes only at 961px+ with the menu expanded (`body.sps-menu-fit:not(.folded)`), so collapsing the menu or a narrow window gives back the plugin's own layout.

Docs: `README.md` feature section and changelog, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (still under 10 KB).

## Verification

See PR comments for the test-site evidence.

title: fix: shared preview keeps PRs whose only conflicts are changelog lines
body:
## What

`scripts/preview-site.sh` now includes a PR in the shared preview when its only conflicts are in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` or `README.md`. For the preview those files are merged with git's union merge (both sides' lines kept, through a temporary `core.attributesFile`), and the stamp says so, for example:

```
#141 feature/... ba55fb2 (draft; both sides' lines kept in changelog.txt README.md readme.txt) ...
```

Conflicts in any other file still leave the PR out, as before. Real merges and `.gitattributes` are unchanged.

## Why

Every PR adds lines at the top of the same changelog lists. After each merge to `main`, every other open PR conflicts there, so the next preview run by any session drops them all. On 2026-10-02 this hid #141 three times in about ten minutes (after the merges of #148 and #153) while the owner was reviewing it, and also dropped #149, #150, #153 and #154 at various points. Posts use core `menu_order`; terms use term meta. Moves swap only the places the moved rows hold, so one page or a filtered list leaves the rest alone. Queries that set no order follow it; searches and column sorts do not. Imports SCPO's types, taxonomies and `term_order` (read only). WooCommerce-sorted taxonomies are left to WooCommerce.
- **Term tools** (`class-seoprostack-term-tools.php`, replaces Term Management Tools): bulk Merge into, Move to taxonomy (refused on a slug clash), Set parent (refused for loops). Old archive addresses of merged and moved terms 301 to the term that took over when they would otherwise 404.

body:
Resolves #171. For #7.

## What changed

- **Word documents in the editor** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-word-import.php`, `admin/js/seoprostack-word-import.js`, Content tab, off by default, replaces Mammoth .docx converter): drop or paste a `.docx` file into the block editor, or choose **Word document** in the editor's Options menu. A short-lived `seoprostack/word-document` block (a `files` transform at priority 5, before core's File block; not in the inserter, saves nothing) sends the file to `POST seoprostack/v1/word-document` and replaces itself with `wp.blocks.rawHandler()` blocks from the returned HTML. Plain ES5, no build step, no 600 KB library.
- Server conversion with `ZipArchive` and DOM: headings (Heading 1–6, Title, outline levels, following `basedOn`), bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, sub/superscript, links (external relationships only, `http(s)`/`mailto`/`tel`), line breaks, nested bulleted and numbered lists from `numbering.xml` (one list across nested levels with their own numbering), quotes (Quote and Block Text styles), tables (header rows, `gridSpan`), pictures with alt text and Caption-style captions, tracked insertions and content controls. XML parts with a DOCTYPE are refused and parsed with `LIBXML_NONET`; parts over 50 MB, documents over 30 MB (or the upload limit) are refused.
- Pictures: checked with `wp_get_image_mime()` (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), sideloaded with `media_handle_sideload()`, attached to the post, named after their alt text or the document, alt text stored; up to 100 per document, the rest counted and reported in a snackbar.
- Permissions: `upload_files`, plus `edit_post` for the given post (`edit_posts` without one); core's REST cookie nonce. Without `ZipArchive` the editor shows a message to ask the host for PHP's zip extension and the route returns 501.
- Settings version 11 switches it on while Mammoth is active (Mammoth has no settings). `admin/data/free-plugins.php` drops `mammoth-docx-converter`, with a comment. No new options or meta, so nothing to add to `uninstall.php`.

title: GH#189: fix: More menu rows hold their own floated icons
body:
Resolves #189

## What

Items in the More menu (…) in the admin bar no longer shift right under a taller icon (Rank Math SEO under AutomatorWP, Query Monitor under Social Posts).

## Why

Core and plugins float bar icons (`.ab-icon`, `.ab-item:before`) left. On the bar each item is one line, so that never matters; in the menu a row can be shorter than its icon, and the float pushes the next row's content right by the icon's width.

## How

One rule in `SEOProStack_Admin_Bar_More::assets()`: each moved item's `.ab-item` gets a clearfix (`:after{content:"";display:table;clear:both}`), so every row holds its own floats. It covers any plugin's floated icon with no per-plugin rules, and it works for both block and flex rows (TranslatePress). No plugin on the test site styles `.ab-item::after`.

Changelog lines in `README.md`, `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (10,207 bytes, under 10 KB).

## Verification

- `php -l includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-bar-more.php`: no syntax errors.
- Shared test site, Chromium, `/wp-admin/edit.php`, … open, measuring where each row's text starts. Before: Query Monitor at 36px (pushed by Social Posts' icon). With the rule: 10px, the row's own padding. Other rows did not move. The preview site is checked again after `scripts/preview-site.sh` includes this branch.

title: GH#188: fix: no strip beside the full screen editor with the fitted admin menu
body:
## Summary

With **Fit the menu to its names** on, the block editor in full screen mode (menu hidden) could show an empty strip down the left, as wide as the fitted menu.

- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`: every fitted-menu rule (menu width, `#wpcontent`/`#wpfooter` margin, `.sps-fit-*` bars) now also needs `:not(.is-fullscreen-mode)`. Before, `#wpcontent` kept the wider margin in full screen (it beat core's `margin-left: 0` on source order), and a bar marked `sps-fit-start` overrode core's `left: 0 !important` on the editor frame.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`:
  - new `shown()` (not collapsed, wide window, not `is-fullscreen-mode`, menu has boxes) used by `fit()` and `wide()`.
  - `place()` never marks `.interface-interface-skeleton`, which the stylesheet places.
  - `watchShown()` fits the menu when it shows again. The editor page opens with `is-fullscreen-mode` set in PHP, so the menu used to be measured while hidden and stayed at 160px with names wrapping after the editor left full screen.
- Changelog lines in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (kept under 10 KB); feature text in `README.md`.

Resolves #188

## Verification

Throwaway WordPress 7.1.2 site (Docker), with a long menu name so the menu fits to 264px, Playwright at 1400px:

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Opened in full screen, then full screen off | menu 160, names wrap | menu 264, editor at 264 |
| Normal, then full screen on | `#wpcontent` margin 264 | margin 0, editor at 0 |
| Editor frame with a stale `sps-fit-start` in full screen | n/a | editor at 0 |
| Fixed plugin bar at `left: 160px` | n/a | 264 with menu shown, back to its own 160 in full screen |

Dashboard and Fluent Forms screens: menu still 264, content beside it. `node --check` passes. On the shared preview site (read-only, full screen preference put back), the editor frame starts at 0 in full screen.

I couldn't reproduce the exact strip from the report in headless Chromium or WebKit. The fix covers each way the offset reaches full screen.

title: fix: preview script runs origin/main's copy when a worktree's is out of date
body:
## Why

At 21:03 a session ran `scripts/preview-site.sh` from an old worktree (`chore/release-0.8.0`). Its copy of the script dates from before `fd3cacb` (changelog-only conflicts no longer keep a PR out), so it skipped both open PRs (#187, #192) and put plain `main` on the shared test site, one minute after a correct run. The owner then saw the old sticky star and spacing and asked whether it was a cache issue.

## What

`scripts/preview-site.sh` now fetches, then compares its own file with `origin/main:scripts/preview-site.sh`. If they differ, it runs `origin/main`'s copy (from a temp file, which that copy deletes when it starts) with the same `--dry-run` and site arguments, and says so on stderr. `SEOPROSTACK_PREVIEW_OWN=1` runs the checkout's own copy, for trying a change to the script itself. `--help` does not fetch.

Worktrees made before this merges still have the old script, but every worktree that includes this change will run main's copy from then on.

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/preview-site.sh`: clean.
- `--help` prints the whole header (the `usage()` line range moved by two lines).
- From this branch (copy differs from main): `--dry-run` printed the notice and main's copy produced the report with #187 and #192 included.
- `SEOPROSTACK_PREVIEW_OWN=1 ... --dry-run`: ran this copy, same report, no notice.
- Before this merges, main's copy has no clean-up step, so the dry run left one temp file; it was removed by hand. After merge, main's copy deletes it.

title: fix: preview script knows a squash-merged branch is in the preview
body:
## Why

After #192 was squash-merged, `scripts/preview-site.sh` run from its worktree said "Your branch feature/pinned-pages-list-speed is not in the preview: push it and open a draft PR", although its work was in `main`. `branch_note()` merges the branch into the preview and compares trees, but the preview's changelogs also hold other open PRs' lines (union merge), so that merge conflicted in `changelog.txt`, `README.md` and `readme.txt` and the check failed.

## What

`branch_note()` now merges with the same union attributes `merge_pr()` uses, and treats the branch as included when the merged tree differs from the preview only in `DOC_FILES`.

- `shellcheck scripts/preview-site.sh`: clean.
- `SEOPROSTACK_PREVIEW_OWN=1 ... --dry-run` from the squash-merged `feature/pinned-pages-list-speed` worktree: no note (before: the false note).

body:
## What

Contributors are writers, not commenters: WordPress gives them the editor in wp-admin to write posts and submit them for review, so blocking wp-admin would stop them working. Commenters and reviewers are subscribers (or WooCommerce customers), which **Block dashboard access** already covers.

What contributors (and authors) saw was the problem: many plugins open their pages to anyone who can log in or write. On the test site a contributor saw AI Engine's settings and Playground, Media File Renamer, FluentCommunity, WooCommerce Home, WP Sheet Editor, Social Posts and Tools. Those pages ask only for `read` or `edit_posts`.

New sub-setting of **Organise the admin menu**, on by default: **Writers see only writing** (`admin_menu_writers`).

- Hidden from the menu and refused with a 403: plugin pages whose capability is one every writer has (`read`, `edit_posts`, `upload_files`, `level_0`…). Tools is hidden too (nothing of WordPress's own for writers).
- Kept: WordPress screens (Dashboard, Posts and post types they can edit, Media, Comments, Profile), and plugin pages that ask for a capability a plugin gave the role on purpose.

title: GH#173: feat: Brand icons
body:
## What

**Brand icons** (Content tab, off by default; replaces Popular Brand Icons – Simple Icons, whose bundled set dates from 2022):

- **Brand icon** block: search by name (placeholder, or Icon in the sidebar), brand colour or text colour (Styles), size, optional link (new tab), screen-reader name.
- 3,806 icons: Simple Icons 16.33.0 (3,463, CC0) plus 343 Font Awesome Free 7.3.1 brand icons (CC BY 4.0) for brands Simple Icons does not have, many removed at their owners' request (LinkedIn, Microsoft, Slack, AWS).
- Near-black and near-white brand colours (GitHub, X, Apple) use the text colour, so they stay visible in Kadence dark mode. Same luminance rule in PHP and JS.
- Front end: SVG inlined on the server. No icon font, no script or stylesheet, no request to another site.
- Editor: `GET seoprostack/v1/brand-icons` (`edit_posts`), 60 results per page, exact match first, then starts-with, then aliases. The whole set is never sent to the browser.
- Compatibility: `[simple_icon name color size class title_tag]` and `#name#` menu titles, registered only once the old plugin is inactive. Names match with or without spaces, dots and capitals; 154 aliases follow renames (`twitter` → X, `nuxtdotjs` → nuxt). Brands no longer in either set render nothing.
- Colour and size values are checked against a strict pattern before they go into `style` (no `url()` or `;`). Path data and viewBox are checked when read.

## Storage: 64 shard files, not 3,806 SVGs

The first version shipped one SVG per icon: 3,806 files, 3.9 MB zip. Every install and update copies every file, which is slow on hosts that update over FTP. Icon shapes are now in `assets/brand-icons/shapes-{0..63}.json` (about 80 KB each). `index.json` (title, colour, source, shard) says which file holds an icon. A page reads only the shards it needs, once per request.

- Zip: **2.9 MB, 254 files** (761 KB before this feature; 3.9 MB / 3,996 files with one SVG per icon).
- 20 icons render in 1.5–4 ms. Plugin Check runs in 96 s instead of 263 s.
- `LICENSE.txt` names both sources and licences. Each shard holding a Font Awesome icon repeats Font Awesome's attribution under `"//"`.
- `scripts/update-brand-icons.sh` (Node 18+, contacts registry.npmjs.org only) rebuilds everything from the newest npm releases. Run it before a release.

## Migration and replacement

- Settings version 13: switches on while `simple-icons` is active (it has no settings to import).
- `simple-icons` removed from Free Plugins with a comment. `README.md` Features table and Credits rows (Popular Brand Icons, Simple Icons, Font Awesome; GitHub links checked with `gh api`). `php scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write`: 44 plugins.
- No options, meta, transients or cron of its own, so `uninstall.php` is unchanged.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-brand-icons.php` (new), registered in `includes/class-seoprostack.php`
- `blocks/brand-icon/` (hand-written, no build)
- `scripts/update-brand-icons.{sh,js}`, generated `assets/brand-icons/` (index, 64 shards, LICENSE)
- `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php` (DB_VERSION 13), `admin/data/free-plugins.php`
- `README.md` (feature, table, credits, count, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (10,211 bytes)

## Verification

- `php -l` / `node --check` on changed files.
- Server checks (WP-CLI, 29) on WP 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3 and WP 6.2 / PHP 7.4, all pass: name/alias lookup, path traversal (`../index`) rejected, shortcode options, unsafe colour/size ignored, menu titles, block with link, missing icon renders nothing, REST ranking and `edit_posts` check, **all 3,806 icons render from their shard and all 154 aliases resolve**.
- Browser on both versions: picker shows icons before typing, search and choose, attributes stored, no editor or front-end console errors, no icon or block asset requested on the front end, text-colour icon and GitHub follow simulated Kadence dark mode.
- Real Popular Brand Icons – Simple Icons 2.8.4: with the plugin active, the feature switches on at DB version 13 and its shortcode stays the old plugin's; after deactivation, ours takes over.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors (warnings are existing release-time items). `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors, no new warnings.

Resolves #173

title: GH#202: chore: CI and quality checks on every pull request
body:
## What

Every pull request and push to `main` is now checked in GitHub Actions, and each check runs the same way locally. Workflow and commands: `DEVELOPMENT.md`.

| Job | Runs | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lint (PHP 7.4) | every push | PHP 7.4 syntax, `node --check`, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS (WordPress Coding Standards, security sniffs, PHPCompatibilityWP 7.4+, minimum WP 6.2), PHPStan level 5 |
| Release build | ready PRs, `main` | `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`, both zips built, `scripts/plugin-check.sh` on both; zips and reports kept 7 days as an artifact |
| Smoke test | ready PRs, `main` | new `scripts/smoke-test.sh` on WP 6.2 / PHP 7.4 and latest WP / PHP 8.3 |

The smoke test installs the GitHub zip on a throwaway Docker WordPress, logs in, and loads 11 public and 18 admin pages, first with default settings and then with all 69 on/off features switched on (all except maintenance mode). It also runs due cron events, uninstalls the plugin, and fails on any 5xx, critical error page, `debug.log` line, or leftover `seoprostack` option or cron hook. A canary notice proves `debug.log` works, so an empty log means something.

Also:
- `composer.json` / `composer.lock` (development tools only; lock now committed so CI is reproducible). `.distignore` and the preflight's dev-file guard keep tooling, `vendor/` and `.github/` out of both zips.
- Actions pinned to commit SHAs with `persist-credentials: false`, `contents: read`, and concurrency cancelling. No `|| true` on any check. Dependabot groups weekly updates for Actions and Composer.
- Draft PRs run only lint, to save private-repo minutes.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` rewritten (it described `v0.2.3-stable` branches); `TESTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` point to the new checks; README changelog line.

## Code fixes found by the tools
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `pre_update_option_active_plugins` registered with 2 accepted args for a 1-arg callback; `WP_INSTALLING` constant replaced with `wp_installing()`; `state()` docblock lists `front_revision`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`: `catalog()` docblock lists `hidden`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-post-reactions.php`: `$extra` documented as the string it is.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-old-slugs.php`: explicit `$single = false`.
- A handful of `phpcs:ignore` comments, each with a reason (intended `urlencode()`, large queries, local `file_get_contents()`, Kadence's hook names, assignment in condition).

## PHPStan baseline
48 existing findings are in `phpstan-baseline.neon`. Most come from the WordPress 7.x stubs being stricter than WordPress (custom `wp_hash()` schemes, `wp_register_script()` with no file, `method_exists()` checks kept for WP 6.2). New findings fail; the baseline only shrinks (`composer baseline`).

## Verification (local)
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all six checks pass (after rebasing on `main`, including Brand icons).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors; 5 warnings, all existing release-time items. Both zips: "no development files".
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: GitHub zip 0 errors (only the expected updater findings), WordPress.org zip 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` and `--php 8.3` (WP 7.1.2): passed; every page 200 except the deliberate 404; no PHP messages; nothing left after uninstall.

Nothing is tagged, published or uploaded.

Resolves #202

title: GH#208: feat: Brand icons in Kadence Blocks icon pickers
body:
## What

Brand icons (#173) in every Kadence Blocks icon picker, as a **Brand icons** category next to Line Icons and Solid Icons.

- **Editor** (`admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-brand-icons.js`): adds the set through Kadence's `kadence.icon_options` (name => `{vB, cD}`) and `kadence.icon_options_names` (category => names) `wp.hooks` filters. Names are `sps_{slug}`. Icons the site already uses are printed with the page, so blocks draw at once; `index.json` and the `shapes-*.json` files load in the background as static, versioned files that the browser caches (about 2.2 MB gzip, once). Loaded only in the block editor, with Kadence Blocks active and Brand icons on.
- **Front end** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-brand-icons.php`): Kadence draws icons on the server from one list (`kadence_svg_icons`), built the first time a request draws an icon. title: GH#152: fix: fitted admin menu the same width on every screen
body:
## What

**Fit the menu to its names** gave the sidebar different widths on different screens, so the menu moved sideways (203–219 px on the shared test site).

Measured on that site (Chrome, 1440×900), there were two causes:

1. **Padding depended on where the entry was.** "HTTP Requests Manager" (third level) has 14/16 px padding in a menu that opens to the side and 12/12 px in the open menu, so it needed 201 px on WP-Optimize and 205 px elsewhere. `room()` in `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` now measures the text where it is, but always adds the in-place padding: 12 px before (38 px for third-level and icon entries), and 12 px after (24 px for entries with a chevron). Top-level names are unchanged.
2. **Plugins change entries per screen.** AutomatorWP's "Try BBForms!" entry has a "New" badge that is only styled where its CSS loads (text 108 px on most screens, 161–167 px on edit.php and Plugins), and Tutor LMS's screen loads a font that widens text by about 3 px. No measurement on one screen can know about another. So the widest width the menu has needed is remembered per person in the `spsmw` user setting (the `wp-settings` cookie, as folding already does). It is keyed by `width_key()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`: an 8-character hash of the stored active plugins (read from `wp_load_alloptions()`, so Load plugins only where needed does not change it per screen), the user's language and the SEO Pro Stack version. Activating or deactivating a plugin, or updating, starts over.

## Verification

Shared test site, via `scripts/preview-site.sh` (this PR plus `main`, #216 and #217), with the stored width cleared first:

- First pass: index, edit and WP-Optimize are all 203 px (they were 207/207/203 before). Tutor settings and Fluent Support are 206. Plugins and post-new are 219 (the badge's CSS).
- Second pass over all seven screens: **219 px on every one**. No entry in the open menu or a top-level name wraps.
- WP-Optimize's header and Fluent Support's navbar start at 219 px, level with the menu (#144 behaviour kept).
- No new debug-log lines. The `regeneratorRuntime is not defined` page error on plugins.php comes from other plugins' scripts (Code Snippets, Image Copytrack and others), not SEO Pro Stack.
- `node --check`, `scripts/lint.sh` (PHPCS, PHPStan) pass.

Docs: `README.md` (Fit the menu to its names, changelog), `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (9,944 bytes after merging `main` with #216). The `readme.txt` line for #208's Kadence pickers, dropped there for size, is back.

Resolves #152

New, off by default: **Restrict content** (Content tab). Membership, payments and sign-up stay with the plugins that already do them (Fluent Forms registration, FluentCRM, FluentCart, WooCommerce): they give people a role, and the role decides what they see.

- **Who sees this** on posts, pages and public custom post types (meta box): everyone, logged-in, logged-out, only chosen roles, or logged-in except chosen roles.

- Content Control compatibility: its `contentControls` block rules (login status and roles; hiding on phones, tablets or desktops) and the `[content_control]` shortcode keep working. Its restrictions for chosen posts, chosen terms and posts in chosen terms are converted once. Restrictions it cannot convert (whole site, post types, AND conditions) are listed on the settings card. Its settings are never changed.
- New filters `seoprostack_can_see_content` and `seoprostack_block_visible`. Settings version 14. Uninstall removes the post and term rules.

Not covered from Content Control Pro: scheduled blocks, WooCommerce/EDD rules, content previews and custom login pages.

title: GH#213: feat: pictures converted again after quality changes, rules check, whole-library watermarks
body:
## What

Pictures are converted again after quality changes, with optional quality by picture size; the WebP and AVIF panel checks that browsers really get the copies; Watermark pictures can work on the whole Media Library in the background.

Resolves #213

## Why

- **Quality settings had no effect.** `WP_Image_Editor::get_output_format()` calls `set_quality()` with no value when the format changes on save, which resets it to WordPress's default (86 for WebP, 82 for AVIF). On the test site, WebP quality 90, 50 and 20 all gave the same 44,148-byte file.
- Changing a quality only affected pictures converted afterwards.
- On LiteSpeed, new `.htaccess` rules can sit unread until the server restarts, so browsers get originals and nothing says so.
- Watermarks could only be changed by selecting pictures page by page, and a bulk action stopped after 20 seconds.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
  - Applies the quality through `wp_editor_set_quality` for that one save.
  - Records the quality each format was made with in `_seoprostack_nextgen` and puts a picture back in the queue when that changes. Copies from 0.10.0 and earlier have no record and are made again once.
  - New `nextgen_smart` setting, off by default: +15 below 200 px, −10 from 800, −20 from 2,000 on the longest side.
  - Rules check: a request for a converted picture with an AVIF/WebP `Accept` header. The answer is cached in `seoprostack_nextgen_check` (a week, or five minutes after a failure), with LiteSpeed-specific or Apache-module advice.
  - Unique temporary file names and a batch lock.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`
  - Whole-library background batches: Mark every picture, Mark again with these settings, Remove every watermark.
  - Job in option `seoprostack_watermark_job`, hook `seoprostack_watermark_batch`; it walks pictures in ID order.
  - Live progress, Stop, and a lock.
  - Bulk actions queue what does not fit in 20 seconds.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php`: new `more_time()`. WP-Cron ran both 20-second batches in one request and hit a 30-second `max_execution_time` fatal in Imagick. It now restarts the limit with `set_time_limit()` where allowed; otherwise it stops early, counting CPU time.
- `uninstall.php`: removes the watermark job and hook. The lock and check transients go with the existing `seoprostack_` transient cleanup.
- README, `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (9,901 bytes) updated under a new Unreleased heading above 0.10.0.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker site (WordPress 7.1.2, PHP 8.3, Imagick), not the shared preview:

- **Quality**: WebP 80 to 50 re-queued 3 of 3 pictures, and sizes dropped (130,278 to 93,018; 36,528 to 25,498; 5,784 to 4,128 bytes). AVIF was untouched.
- **Quality by picture size**: WebP 65/50/30 and AVIF 75/60/40 at 150/700/2,400 px, from a base of 50/60. A record with no quality data was made again.
- **Rules check**: a copy came back with the rules in place. With `.htaccess` removed, the original came back and the LiteSpeed or Apache advice showed.
- **Watermark batches** (`wp eval-file`): add, again, remove and stop worked; a second start was refused while one ran; a bulk-action queue refused a different operation.
- **Watermark UI** (Playwright, 49 pictures): Mark every picture went 0, then 36, then done (48 marked, 1 left alone). Stop then hid and the buttons came back without a reload. No console errors.
- **Time limit**: both batches in one request with `max_execution_time=30`, with and without `set_time_limit` disabled. Requests took 13 to 20 s wall time and 16 to 20 s CPU, and shut down cleanly. Before the fix this was a fatal error. `debug.log` stayed empty.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passed. `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors; its warnings are the Unreleased sections and the existing v0.10.0 tag.

Not checked: a real LiteSpeed server restart, and PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 at runtime (only CI's syntax and compatibility checks).

title: GH#243: feat: WP-Optimize page cache preset off LiteSpeed; Free Plugins note
body:
Resolves #243

## Summary

- **Free Plugins** lists WP-Optimize on every site again, with a note under it (new `seoprostack_free_plugin_note` filter, rendered in cards and rows by `SEOProStack_Plugin_Manager::note()`): on a LiteSpeed server, that this site does not need it; elsewhere, that it is there for its page cache and its preset turns that on.
- **Preset conditions** can start with `!` (`!litespeed_server`), in `SEOProStack_Presets::condition()`.
- **WP-Optimize preset** turns `wpo_cache_config.enable_page_caching` on where the site is not on a LiteSpeed server, with WP-Optimize's own defaults for the rest (24 hours, not for logged-in people). Nothing that SEO Pro Stack already does (images, database cleanup) or that writes `.htaccess` (Gzip, browser caching).
- **`SEOProStack_WP_Optimize`** (new, `includes/class-seoprostack-wp-optimize.php`) runs after Apply, Reset and Undo (`seoprostack_plugin_preset_changed`), like the LiteSpeed Cache one: it saves through `WP_Optimize_Cache_Commands::save_cache_settings()`, which writes or removes `advanced-cache.php`, the `WP_CACHE` line and its config, and purges. That code acts only when its stored switch changes, so the switch is first set from the files.
- **OPcache**: WP-Optimize rewrites `wp-config.php` without telling OPcache, so with `opcache.revalidate_freq=2` (the Docker image default; often 60 on hosts) an Undo straight after a Reset still saw `WP_CACHE` on and skipped writing it back. The helper calls `opcache_invalidate()` on `wp-config.php` after saving (skipped where `opcache.restrict_api` does not allow it).
- Docs: README (presets table, `!` conditions, LiteSpeed hosting, hook, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (40 bytes left).

## Verification

Fresh throwaway site (`wordpress` Apache image, PHP 8.3, WP-Optimize 4.7.0, OPcache on, not LiteSpeed):

- `wp seoprostack presets diff wp-optimize` before: only the admin-bar setting and page cache false → true.
- **Apply preset** link from the Plugins screen (logged-in request): `advanced-cache.php` and `define('WP_CACHE', true); // WP-Optimize Cache` written; second page request `WPO-Cache-Status: cached`; diff says settings match.
- Reset then Undo from the Plugins screen, back to back, three rounds: each Reset removes the `WP_CACHE` line and `advanced-cache.php` (no cache header); each Undo restores both and pages are `cached`. Before the OPcache fix, Undo left `WP_CACHE` out.
- Same through `wp seoprostack presets reset|undo wp-optimize`.
- Free Plugins note filter returns the non-LiteSpeed note for `wp-optimize` and nothing for other slugs.
- No PHP warnings or notices in Apache's log from these requests.
- `scripts/lint.sh` all passed; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` 0 errors (warnings are release-time ones already on `main`).

Not checked on a LiteSpeed server: there the preset leaves `wpo_cache_config` out (condition), so the helper does not run.

title: GH#242: refactor: shared GitHub updater, newest copy on a site runs
body:
For #242 (phase 3: shared GitHub updater engine).

## What

- New `includes/github-updater/`: the update engine moved out of the SEO Pro Stack feature into a shared, versioned updater (`WPAllStars_GitHub_Updater`). It is the same in every plugin made from the starter apart from the text domain and `@package`.
  - `load.php` registers this copy's version (`1.0.0`) when the plugin loads; on `plugins_loaded` (priority 1) only the newest registered copy loads, once, and serves every installed plugin with a `GitHub Plugin URI` header.
  - It decides on `init` (20) whether to run: `wpallstars_github_updater_enabled` (default: off while Git Updater is active). Other filters: `wpallstars_github_updater_early`, `wpallstars_github_plugins` and `wpallstars_github_token` (default `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN`). Cache: `wpallstars_github_releases`.
- `SEOProStack_Github_Updates` keeps its settings (on/off, Early updates, waits for Git Updater, Git Updater error-cache fix) and drives the engine only through those filters, because another plugin's copy may be the one that runs. `SEOPROSTACK_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `seoprostack_github_token` and `seoprostack_github_plugins` still work.
- `SEOProStack::load()` requires `includes/github-updater/load.php` when present. `.distignore-wporg` leaves the folder out of the WordPress.org build. `uninstall.php` removes the new and old caches. PHPCS accepts the `wpallstars` prefix.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: BSD awk cannot take a value with newlines through `-v`, so the list of updater paths broke once it had two lines (the updater errors were counted again). It now goes through the environment. Plugin Check's prefix warnings in the updater files are reported as expected in the GitHub zip, like the updater errors.
- Docs: README (feature, hooks, Updates and releases, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, `RELEASING.md`. No `readme.txt` line: the updater is not in the WordPress.org build.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors (warnings are the usual Unreleased / slug / existing-tag ones). GitHub zip has `includes/github-updater`; WordPress.org zip has neither updater path, no updater headers, no update code.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors on either zip; 2 updater errors and 8 prefix warnings expected in the GitHub zip; the 6 remaining warnings (database cleanup) are the same in the WordPress.org zip.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3, defaults and every feature on): passed.
- Two plugins on a disposable site (SEO Pro Stack GitHub zip + a demo plugin with its own copy; GitHub and WordPress.org faked, requests logged):
  - same version: SEO Pro Stack's copy loads, 1 update hook, both plugins offered 9.9.9 with their release assets, 6 GitHub requests; a second check makes 0 (cache).
  - demo carries 1.0.1: the demo copy loads; demo carries 0.9.0: SEO Pro Stack's copy loads. Always 1 update hook.
  - tokens: none → empty; `SEOPROSTACK_GITHUB_TOKEN` → used; with `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN` too → the shared one wins.
  - Updates from GitHub off → 0 update hooks, neither plugin listed, 0 requests.
  - SEO Pro Stack inactive → the demo copy serves both.
  - `uninstall_plugin()` removes `wpallstars_github_releases` and `seoprostack_github_releases` (the demo copy fills the cache again at the next update check, as it should).

title: fix: page learning keeps every script and style handle; release 0.11.2
body:
## Summary

Fix found in the preview site's debug log while checking the 0.11.1 update, then release 0.11.2.

**Bug:** `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::page_needs()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`) builds `$handles` with `array_unique()`, which keeps the original keys, then walks it with `for ($i = 0; $i < count($handles); $i++)` while appending dependencies. Gaps from removed duplicates meant:

- `Undefined array key N` warnings and `Using null as an array offset` deprecations (preview log, 03-Oct-2026 02:16 UTC, `learn_front` → `page_needs`, lines 1260–1261);
- handles stored at keys at or above `count()` were never examined, so a plugin whose scripts or styles a page still used could be left out of that page's `needs` and skipped by **Learn which plugins each page needs**.

**Fix:** `array_values(array_unique(...))`, so the loop sees every handle. It is the only loop of this kind in `includes/`.

**Release:** `Version:`/`SEOPROSTACK_VERSION` 0.11.2, `Stable tag: 0.11.2`, changelog in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- Preview site (every recommended plugin, page learning on): deployed the fix, ran `forget_front()`, fetched 4 uncached public pages as a visitor. 4 pages learned (12–13 needed plugins each), with no SEO Pro Stack log lines since; before the fix, the same path logged the warnings above.

title: GH#261: fix: private GitHub updates where GPLVault Updater resets every download
body:
## What

- Syncs the shared GitHub updater from the starter (wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#261, commit 38fe7a6) with `scripts/sync-core.sh`. Before downloading, it swaps a private repository's API address for GitHub's signed, short-lived download address on `upgrader_package_options`, so WordPress downloads it itself. `private_download()` stays as a fallback; both use `signed_address()`.
- Changelogs (`README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`): adds an Unreleased section with the fix. GH#256's affiliate-links line moves there too: it was merged after the `v0.11.2` tag (`compare v0.11.2...059e56d` = 1 commit), so 0.11.2 never had it.

## Why

GPLVault Updater returns `false` from `upgrader_pre_download` for every package at priority 999999999. That threw away the file the updater had downloaded, and WordPress fetched the API address without the token. GitHub answered 404, so private updates fail wherever GPLVault is active (10 of 17 Hostinger installs). The 7 installs without it updated to 0.11.2 normally. Trace: #261.

## Verification

- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` before the sync: only this file differed from the starter (1 of 44).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. `readme.txt` is 9712 bytes.
- Live, on a site with GPLVault Updater 5.3.9 active: this exact file (byte-identical) in place of the 0.11.0 one. The cron-context automatic update downloaded from `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, updated 0.11.0 → 0.11.2 ("Plugin updated successfully") and kept the plugin active. Without it, the same run failed with "Download failed. Not Found".

## Rollout

Sites with GPLVault active that run a version without this fix cannot auto-update past it. They need the first release with the fix installed once by hand; later updates then arrive by themselves.

Resolves #261

title: GH#230: learn and undo large unused autoloaded settings
body:
## Summary

Off-by-default, single-site Speed feature, **Load large settings only where they are used**. A removable must-use sampler learns which autoloaded settings of 10 KB or more logged-out site pages read. After at least 3 days, 30 sampled visitor pages and 10 sampled admin screens, it turns autoload off for the large settings that site pages never read. Values are never changed, collected or deleted. - Merged `origin/main` (0.12.8 and later). Doc conflicts resolved, keeping both sides; readme.txt is 10,238 of 10,240 bytes after small wording trims.

title: fix: Agency option lists no longer stop pages when a Fluent plugin's tables are missing
body:
## What

After installing 0.11.3 on the wpallstars.com network, the front pages of `builder`, `test2`, `test3` and `test4.wpallstars.com` returned 500 with a critical error.

Cause (stack trace from a CLI render of `http://test2.wpallstars.com/`):

`SEOProStack_Settings::maybe_migrate()` → `sanitize_all()` → `sanitize_value()` → `options_for()` → `SEOProStack_Agency_Orders::form_options()` → `FluentForm\App\Models\Form::...->get()` → `QueryException: Table 'wp_20_fluentform_forms' doesn't exist`.

Fluent Forms is network-active, but on those sites it was never set up, so its tables are missing and its query builder throws. 0.11.3 raised the settings DB version, so every site ran the upgrade on its first request. The upgrade threw before saving, so it ran again on every request.

## Fix

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-agency-orders.php`: `form_options()`, `board_options()` and `space_options()` go through a new `add_rows()` helper that catches `\Throwable` and returns the list built so far. All the fields that use them are `'open' => true`, so stored form, board and space IDs are kept when the list is empty (`SEOProStack_Settings::sanitize_value()`, select and multi cases).

Changelog: an Unreleased entry in `README.md` and `changelog.txt`. `readme.txt` has 47 bytes left, so its line is added when the release rewrites that section.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Live: this file was copied over the 0.11.3 copy on the wpallstars.com network (the original is backed up on the server). `builder`, `test2`, `test3` and `test4` now return 200, and `seoprostack_db_version` is 18 on each, the same as the main site, so the upgrade finished there.

## Follow-up

`SEOProStack_Settings::options_for()` is a starter core file. Guarding every option callback there would stop any feature's list from taking a site down. That change belongs in the starter first.

## What

Syncs the shared GitHub updater from the starter (wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#264, merge `51ccabc`): its requests to GitHub never follow redirects, whatever other plugins set. Updater copy 1.0.1.
