title: fix: Load plugins only where needed skips plugins again on updated sites; full effect when switched on
body:
## What

Load plugins only where needed did nothing on sites updated to 0.11.3 or 0.11.4. This fixes the cause, repairs those sites (DB v19), and gives the feature its full effect as soon as it is switched on.

## Why

`SEOProStack_Settings::sanitize_all()` stores every setting, defaults included, so every site had `plugin_loading_only => []` and `plugin_loading_front => []`. The 0.11.3 migrations took those empty lists as choices:

- `migrate()` put every active plugin into **Always load these plugins** (`plugin_loading_always`), so wp-admin skipped nothing.
- `migrate_front()`, on the site's first learn, put every plugin it skips automatically into **Always load these plugins on the site** (`plugin_loading_pages_keep`), so the site skipped nothing.

Seen on all 17 Hostinger installs (32 sites): `plugin_loading_always` held every active plugin; on client-a.example (the only site with the feature on) 10 of the 11 automatic site skips were in the site bypass list.

## Change

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`:

- Migrations keep only non-empty lists (real choices). A new site marks the site-wide migration done, so nothing ticked before its first learn is turned into bypasses.
- DB v19: an always-load list that holds every active plugin is cleared. Where the site-wide migration ran with an empty ticked list, plugins it skips automatically leave the site bypass list. Page learning is switched on where the feature is off.
- **Learn which plugins each page needs** defaults on. It does nothing until the parent feature is on.
- For visitors (no login cookie, so no admin bar), plugins whose only site footprint is the admin bar are skipped automatically too. The Plugins to skip on the site list says so. Logged-in people still get every plugin unless **Also skip them for people who are logged in** is on, and then these plugins load.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: docs and Unreleased entries.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- client-a.example (feature on): the three files on top of 0.11.4 (setup with only `DB_VERSION = 19`), options backed up first. The migration ran to db 19: `plugin_loading_always` 60 → 0, site bypass 12 → 1 (Readabler, which adds to pages). The site relearned with 9 plugins skipped for visitors. Front pages and 7 admin screens return 200 with no errors; new log lines are the existing Action Scheduler "Commands out of sync" and a Really Simple SSL scan query, both logged before the change.
- The other 31 sites (feature off): the same changes applied through `SEOProStack_Settings::set()`, options backed up first. The always-load lists are now empty and page learning is on. When this release arrives, v19 finds nothing more to change.

The Theme tab showed a broken Kadence screenshot (alt text and broken-image icon) on live sites.

## Why

title: fix: replaced plugins' Deactivate link and Plugins tab Activate/Deactivate save through Freesoul Deactivate Plugins
body:
## Problem

On sites with Freesoul Deactivate Plugins (FDP), two actions did nothing:

1. A replaced plugin's **Deactivate …** link (for example "Deactivate Disable Bloat PRO" under Remove WordPress extras) reloads the page and leaves the plugin active.
2. On the Plugins tab, in-place **Activate** / **Deactivate** report success, but the plugin's state does not change.

## Root cause

FDP's mu-plugin (`eos_dp_return_all_plugins()` on `pre_update_option_active_plugins`) replaces every `active_plugins` save with the full list it read when the page loaded. The only exception is core's own Plugins screen actions (`$_REQUEST['action']` is `activate`/`deactivate`/… and `plugin` is set). Our admin-post and admin-ajax actions have other names, so the save was dropped without any error.

## Fix

- `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php` (core file, synced from the starter with `scripts/sync-core.sh`): new `SEOProStack_Replaced_Plugins::save_plugin_state()` and `stored_plugins()`. After core's activate/deactivate hooks run, it checks the stored list with the `active_plugins` read/write filters paused. If the change is missing, it saves only that change. The deactivate link uses them.
- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`: the Plugins tab's Activate and Deactivate call `save_plugin_state()` after core's call.
- Changelog lines in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (10167 bytes, under the limit).

Starter PR: wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding (same branch name).

## Verification

Hostinger preview site (FDP + Burst REST optimizer mu-plugins active), real HTTP requests with an admin cookie:

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Deactivate Disable Bloat PRO link | 302 `seoprostack-deactivated=1`, still active | 302, inactive, count 32 → 31 |
| Plugins tab Activate fluent-booking | `success`, status `inactive` | `success`, active, count 32 → 33 |
| Plugins tab Deactivate fluent-booking | n/a | `success`, inactive, count back to 32 |

`phpcs`, `phpstan` clean; `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` reports all 44 core files match the starter. All temporary test files have been removed from the server, and the preview site's plugin states are back to how they were.

body:
## What

Two more fixes under **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`), on by default:

- **Freesoul Deactivate Plugins 2.6.9 + PRO 1.3.0.0.** Before this fix, deactivating one plugin left the other active. PRO's own deactivation hook is registered for the wrong file, so it never runs. Freesoul's must-use file (`mu-plugins/eos-deactivate-plugins.php`) was left behind on networks, and on single sites whenever Freesoul's own code did not run. A leftover file keeps skipping plugins by Freesoul's saved rules and shows an error on every admin screen. Now:
  - Deactivating either plugin deactivates both in the same scope: this site or the network. This works from the Plugins screen, the admin bar and WP-CLI. Saves go past Freesoul's guard through `SEOProStack_Replaced_Plugins::save_plugin_state()`.
  - Once neither plugin is active anywhere (network-active or active on any site, up to 1,000 sites), the must-use file is deleted if its header says it is Freesoul's. Opening the Plugins screen also cleans up a file left from before.
- **Readabler 2.0.18** (Merkulove "Unity" code). On every Plugins screen load, it asks its server for product information with a 60 s timeout, even with a cached answer from the last day. If that request fails, it adds an `admin_notices` closure that throws, and the Plugins screen fails with "There has been a critical error". Now the `load-plugins.php` request is skipped while the cached answer exists, and the throwing closure is removed at `admin_notices` priority 0. Readabler still logs the failure itself.

## Why

- The owner asked whether deactivating Freesoul through SEO Pro Stack should take out both plugins and the must-use file.
- The Readabler crash was found in the 0.11.5 rollout health check. On a production site the Plugins screen returned 500 every time. The shutdown error was `Uncaught Exception: Readabler: Can't get plugin info. User has blocked requests through HTTP. (HTTP Requests Manager plugin …)` from `EnvatoItem.php:170`, and the PHP logs show the same exception daily since 23 Sep.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan). `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`: exit 0.
- Readabler: this class was placed on the affected site, with the original file backed up. The Plugins screen then returned 200 with no critical error on both sites (4 of 4 loads). The only remaining shutdown notice was a Tutor Pro deprecation.
- Freesoul: a disposable Docker run (WordPress 7.1.2, PHP 8.3, Freesoul 2.6.9 + PRO 1.3.0.0, a build of this branch) passed every case with an empty `debug.log`:
  1. WP-CLI deactivates the free plugin: 0 active, file removed.

title: fix: Pro add-ons and their base plugin load together with Load plugins only where needed
body:
For #303

## Problem

With **Load plugins only where needed** on, some wp-admin screens skipped a base plugin while its Pro add-on still loaded. Each Pro add-on then showed its "requires the base plugin" notice there (seen behind the megaphone): FluentBooking Pro, FluentBoards Pro ("please configure"), Fluent Support Pro, FluentForm PRO.

The owner wants these pairs **both or neither**. GH#303 (60dbeb7, merged while this PR was open) makes paid add-ons follow their parent by folder suffix plus three aliases. That is one-way: with both ticked, the base loads on its own screens without the add-on, so Pro features are missing there. Add-ons whose folder is not a suffix of the base and not in the alias list stay unlinked.

## Fix

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` → `dependencies()` (merged with GH#303's suffix list and aliases):

- **Name match** as well: a plugin whose name (without tagline) is another active plugin's name plus Pro/Premium/Add-On/Pack needs it (`FluentCRM Pro` → `FluentCRM - Marketing Automation For WordPress`, `Fluent Forms Pro Add On Pack` → `Fluent Forms`). Covers add-ons beyond the alias list.
- **Both ways**: the base also needs its paid add-on, so the existing loops in `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::plugins_for_screen()` and `front_skipped()` load the pair together or skip both. Plugins on the keep list keep loading, and their pair loads with them.
- New `plain_name()` helper compares names as lower-case letters and digits.

`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `MAP_VERSION` 9 → 10 (sites that already learned with GH#303's one-way links learn again) and `FRONT_VERSION` 4 → 5 (the site's stored dependencies were never refreshed). Docs: README (Dependencies follow, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs` (both files), `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: clean.
- Ran `dependencies()` against plugin headers (real Fluent Forms / Pro headers from a test site, others matching shipped names): every Fluent base ↔ Pro pair (Booking, Boards, Support, Forms, CRM/`fluentcampaign-pro`) and Elementor ↔ Elementor Pro linked both ways; SEO Pro Stack (name contains "Pro") and Akismet got no links.

title: fix: Tutor LMS gets its order, cart and coupon tables on every site of a network
body:
## What

This adds a fix for Tutor LMS 4.1.0 to **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`). Fixes for other plugins is on by default.

Tutor names its nine foreign keys the same on every site, for example `fk_tutor_order_item_order_id`. InnoDB constraint names must be unique per database. On a network, or on sites sharing a database, only the first site gets `tutor_ordermeta`, `tutor_order_items`, `tutor_order_itemmeta`, `tutor_coupon_applications`, `tutor_coupon_usages`, `tutor_carts` and `tutor_cart_items`. On the other sites:
- Tutor's installer fails quietly with errno 121.
- `Upgrader::upgrade_to_3_8_0()` then fails on every `admin_init` with errno 150, "Foreign key constraint is incorrectly formed", because `tutor_order_items` is missing.
- The cart and coupon tables reference `{prefix}users`, which subsites don't have.

The fix has two parts:
- **`dbdelta_create_queries`:** for this site's `tutor_` tables, a constraint name that another table already uses gets this site's table prefix. `{prefix}users` becomes `$wpdb->users`. On the first site Tutor's own names are kept.
- **`admin_init` at priority 5, before Tutor's upgrader:** where `tutor_version` is set but `tutor_order_items` is missing, it runs Tutor's own `create_database()`. If the table is still missing afterwards, a `seoprostack_tutor_tables_retry` transient waits a day before the next try. Uninstall already removes `seoprostack_` transients.

## Why

The owner's network (wpallstars.com) had six subsites missing these tables, and each logged 80–100 error lines per health-check run. Those sites were repaired by hand. This change keeps it from happening again, there or anywhere else.

title: GH#324: fix: Tutor LMS Pro and Comment Goblin no longer slow every admin screen
body:
## What

Two more fixes in **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`). Fixes for other plugins is on by default.

- **Tutor LMS Pro 4.0.9:** `updater/update.php` adds a `current_screen` closure that runs `delete_site_transient('update_plugins'); wp_update_plugins();` on every Plugins screen load. Every plugin's update and licence hooks then run each time. On wpallstars.com those were Hostinger's update-check, Kadence and StellarWP licence validation, and Freesoul's `licensor/product/active` POST. **Ask before licence checks** rightly leaves calls inside `wp_update_plugins` alone. `tutor_pro_no_forced_check()` (on `current_screen` at priority 0) removes closures whose scope class is `TutorPRO\ThemeumUpdater\Update`. WordPress's own `load-plugins.php` check, at most once an hour, stays.
- **Comment Goblin 1.2.0:** `include/update.php` asks `CG_API_BASE . 'plugin-details'` on every read of `update_plugins`, and caches only successful answers. commentgoblin.com currently serves a `*.ingress-daribow.ewp.live` certificate, so each read waits for a failure of about 0.3 s, and reads happen many times per admin screen.
  - `cg_note_failure()` (on `http_api_debug`) records a failed or empty answer in the `seoprostack_comment_goblin_failed` site transient, for 12 hours.
  - `cg_skip_failed()` (on `pre_http_request`) answers with an `http_request_failed` `WP_Error` while that transient exists. Comment Goblin's own error handling already treats that as "no update".
  - `uninstall.php` deletes the transient.

## Why

Admin screens on the wpallstars.com network took 12–17 s. A profile of the main site's Plugins screen measured 15.8 s wall time against 2.5 s of CPU, with about 13 s spent in outgoing requests: 25 failed Comment Goblin requests (about 7.5 s) plus the forced update and licence checks.

Resolves #324

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan). `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` passed. `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` found 0 errors; the warnings are about Unreleased sections and the version, as expected before a release. `readme.txt` is at 10,114 bytes.
- A disposable Docker test ran on WordPress 7.1.2 with PHP 8.3, Tutor 4.1.0, Tutor LMS Pro 4.0.9, Comment Goblin 1.2.0 (the real commentgoblin.com, which is failing), and a build of this branch. A must-use logger recorded each outgoing request. All cases passed:
  1. Control with the fix off: two Plugins loads and one dashboard took 4.09 s, 3.98 s and 2.60 s. They made 2 WordPress.org update checks (forced by Tutor Pro) and 27 Comment Goblin requests, all failing.
  2. Fix on: the same loads took 0.47 s, 0.06 s and 0.04 s, with 0 update checks and 1 Comment Goblin request. The failure was kept.
  3. Fix on, with `last_checked` set two hours back: WordPress's own Plugins screen check still runs exactly once over two loads.
  4. Fix on, after the failure window is cleared: Comment Goblin asks its server once more, then not again.
- WordPress 7.1 returns `pre_http_request` answers without `http_api_debug`, so the fix's own answers never extend the 12-hour window.

title: fix: LiteSpeed no longer stops Action Scheduler and cron runs partway (#336)
body:
## What

**Fixes for other plugins** now writes a block at the top of the site's `.htaccess`, on LiteSpeed servers only (`# BEGIN SEO Pro Stack background requests`). It sets LiteSpeed's `noabort` variable for two requests:
- `wp-cron.php`;
- `admin-ajax.php?action=as_async_request_queue_runner`, Action Scheduler's async runner.

The block is removed when the fix is turned off or the plugin is deactivated. On a network, the main site's switch decides, because the sites share one `.htaccess`.

Files:
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: `noabort_rules()`, `noabort_maybe_sync()` (`admin_init`; also runs when switched off), `noabort_write()`, `deactivate()`.
- `uninstall.php`: deletes `seoprostack_noabort_rules`.
- README (feature, Uninstall, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Why

Resolves #336.

Action Scheduler and WordPress cron each start in a request their caller does not wait for. LiteSpeed stops PHP when that caller hangs up. On client-a.example this caused:
- 89 actions in 30 days marked failed after 300 s "in-progress";
- 1,125 `Commands out of sync` lines at shutdown, from a query stopped in the middle.

Evidence, on Hostinger's LiteSpeed server:
- The temporary probe caught a stopped run: `POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=as_async_request_queue_runner`. It was fine at `action_scheduler_before_process_queue`, and its last query was `reset_timeouts`. Its next check came at `shutdown`, with error 2014 (`Commands out of sync`).
- A test script with the client timing out at 0.1 s or 1 s:

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Plain | Stopped at the hang-up |
| `ignore_user_abort(true)` first thing, no output | Stopped at the hang-up |
| `ignore_user_abort(true)` and output every second | Ran to the end |
| `SetEnv noabort 1` or `RewriteRule … [E=noabort:1]` in `.htaccess` | Ran to the end |

- The exact `RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} (^|&)action=as_async_request_queue_runner(&|$)` rule set `$_SERVER['noabort'] = '1'` for that action only.

Why the top of the file: multisite's WordPress block ends rule processing for existing files (`-f [OR] -d` → `^ - [L]`). `insert_with_markers()` can only append a new block, so the block is written directly with `LOCK_EX`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passed, including phpcs and PHPStan.
- `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` found 0 errors; `readme.txt` is 41 bytes under its limit.
- On the preview site: block written, idempotent, removed when switched off and on deactivation (results in a PR comment).

title: fix: short CPT addresses work for post types registered without a query var
body:
## Problem

On a live site with **Short addresses for custom post types** on for a post type registered with `query_var => false`, every item's link dropped the base (`/item/`), the old address redirected there (301), but the short address returned 404. So every listing linked from the directory page was unreachable.

Cause: `SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base::resolve()` returned early when the post type had no query var (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-remove-cpt-base.php`), while `short_link()` and `redirect_old()` still ran.

## Fix

- `resolve()`: for types without a query var, query the item the way WordPress's own rewrite tags for such types do (`wp-includes/class-wp-post-type.php`: `post_type=<type>&pagename=` for hierarchical, `&name=` otherwise).
- `redirect_old()`: no longer unsets `$args[false]` (key `0`) for such types; also drops `pagename`.
- Changelog entries in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`.

## Verification

Patched file deployed to the affected site (after backing up the 0.12.0 file, identical to `main`), LiteSpeed cache purged:

- All 30 published items of the post type: 200 at their short address, correct title.
- `/property-service/uec/` → 301 → `/uec/`.
- Pages, posts and nested pages (`/directory/`, `/about/`, `/services/trade-partner-services/`, a post): 200.
- Unknown address: still 404.

title: fix: Kadence Pro no longer causes Failed opening warnings; release 0.12.3
body:
## What

**Fixes for other plugins** now cleans Kadence Pro 1.2.5's Composer class map, so other plugins' shared libraries load without PHP warnings.

## Why

Kadence Pro 1.2.5 moved its libraries (PSR interfaces, StellarWP Uplink, DI52, LiquidWeb Harbor) into `vendor-prefixed/` but kept the old names in `vendor/composer/autoload_classmap.php`: 348 of its 354 entries point at files it does not ship. Composer prepends its autoloader, so when another plugin that ships one of those libraries asks for a class, Kadence Pro's loader tries first and PHP warns:

```
Warning: include(.../kadence-pro/vendor/composer/../psr/container/src/ContainerInterface.php): Failed to open stream: No such file or directory
```

Seen on a production site running AI Engine Pro, Kadence Conversions, WP Content Crawler and WP Mailster (all ship `psr/container`). Kadence Pro 1.2.5 is the latest copy we have, and every copy is the same.

## How

- `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::early()` runs from `SEOProStack_Setup::init()` as SEO Pro Stack loads (features boot on `init`, which can be too late). It reads the switch from the stored option, not `SEOProStack_Settings::get()`, because building the schema translates labels before `init`.
- It finds Kadence Pro's loader through `ClassLoader::getRegisteredLoaders()` (Composer 2; a Composer 1 copy throws `Error` and the fix stays off) and drops class-map entries whose folder is missing (one `is_dir()` per folder, 122). Composer has no API for removing entries, so a closure bound to the loader unsets them.
- If Kadence Pro loads after SEO Pro Stack (SEO Pro Stack active for the whole network, Kadence Pro on one site only), `plugin_loaded`/`network_plugin_loaded` run it once Kadence Pro's file has loaded.
- Kadence Pro's 6 real entries and its files are left alone.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, phpcs, phpstan).
- On the affected site with all plugins loaded (WP-CLI `eval-file`, same steps): requesting a class from the broken map gave 2 warnings before; after cleaning (0.46 ms, 122 folders, 348 dropped, 6 kept), 0 warnings, and `Psr\Container\NotFoundExceptionInterface` still loads from the plugin that ships it.

- With the branch build installed on a test site (Kadence Pro 1.2.5 active): requesting four classes from the broken map gave 354 entries and 14 warnings before the change; with it, 6 entries and 0 warnings, and the 2 classes other plugins ship still load. Switching **Fixes for other plugins** off brings back 354 entries and 14 warnings; on again, 6 and 0. No notices from SEO Pro Stack, such as translations loading too early.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Release 0.12.2

This PR also releases 0.12.2 (owner's request): version in `seoprostack.php` and `readme.txt`, and the changelogs. #343 (MainWP Child footer) merged after the 0.12.1 tag but put its changelog line under 0.12.1; that line moves to 0.12.2, where it ships.

title: GH#285: perf: LiteSpeed Cache preset leaves CSS and JS Minify off
body:
## What

The LiteSpeed Cache preset (`presets/litespeed-cache.json`) now sets CSS Minify and JS Minify **off**. Before this change it turned them on.

## Why

Without Combine, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 loads, minifies and rewrites every CSS and JS file again on every page that misses the page cache (`LiteSpeed\Optimize::_build_single_hash_url()`, `src/optimize.cls.php` ~line 797, has no check for an existing file). Hostinger A/B test, straight to origin, median of 6:

| Page | Minify on | Minify off |
|---|---|---|
| client-a.example post | 1.98 s | 0.99 s |
| client-a.example home | 2.47 s | 1.29 s |
| wpallstars.com home | 1.07 s | 0.82 s |
| client-c.example post | 1.33 s | 1.03 s |

Combine avoids the repeat work but breaks pages more often, so it stays off as well. Compression and HTTP/2 already make the files small. Cached pages are unaffected. Full findings: #285.

## Notes added

- Preset `notes` and each Minify setting's `description` in the Apply preset dialog say why the setting is off and what turning it on costs.
- README → LiteSpeed hosting has a "Why Minify is off" bullet with the numbers, and the Features row is updated.
- AGENTS.md records the owner's decision. It also says to time pages straight to the origin, because requests from the Hostinger server through Cloudflare are held to 2.2 s.
- Changelog lines are added in README.md, changelog.txt and readme.txt.

## Verification

- `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` exits 0, and the preset JSON parses.
- Live check: on the Hostinger installs, Minify was turned off through LiteSpeed's own `Conf::update_confs()`. Afterwards the client-a.example post took 0.87 s median uncached (it was 1.98 s), and the cached home page took 0.09 s.

Resolves #285

title: GH#355: feat: pin from an ACF/SCF true/false field; Kadence loops count pins within pages
body:
## What

Pinned posts for any post type (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-sticky-posts.php`):

1. **Pin from a true/false field** (`sticky_posts_fields`, new, off by default). Lists the top-level ACF / Secure Custom Fields true/false fields of the pinnable types (`type|field_name`). Shows while ACF, ACF Pro or SCF is active.
   - Field → pin: `added_post_meta`, `updated_post_meta`, `deleted_post_meta` on a linked field pin or unpin the item. This covers the editor, REST, WP-CLI and imports.
   - Pin → field: core `post_stuck` / `post_unstuck` (pin column, Quick Edit, `stick_post()`) set the field with `update_field()` by field key, so ACF keeps its `_field` reference.
   - Choosing a field (`update_option_seoprostack_options`) pins and unpins the items of its type to match the field, with one `sticky_posts` write (`match_fields()`).
   - A static flag stops the two directions answering each other.
   - In the editor, **Pin to the top** is hidden for linked types: the ACF box would otherwise save the old field value and undo a pin made in the sidebar.
2. **Kadence query loops count pinned items within pages.** Until now pinned items were added on top of page 1, so page 1 held `perPage + pins`. With 73 pins that is 123 items. Now:
   - `kadence_query_vars()` gets the loop's matching pinned IDs in its order (same vars, `fields => ids`, no paging).
   - It takes this page's slice from Kadence's offset (`perPage × (page − 1) + loop offset`) and starts the rest query that many places earlier. `paged` is set to 1, because `offset` 0 counts as none in WP_Query.
   - `lift()` puts the slice in front and trims the rest to the room left.
   - A `found_posts` filter adds the pin count, so Kadence's result count and page count are right. They were short by the number of pins.
   - Inherited loops (no page size) keep the old behaviour: all pins on page 1.

Resolves #355

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs and phpstan all pass.
- **Kadence, real data, read-only.** On client-a.example (Kadence Blocks Pro 2.8.20, loop 13462: awards, A–Z, 50 per page), I loaded this class under another name for one WP-CLI process and swapped it in for the 0.12.3 one. A `pre_option_sticky_posts` filter used the 73 Featured Listing awards as pins, so nothing was written. Results across all pages of Kadence's REST route:
  - Pages 1–10 have 50, 50, …, 22 items.
  - Featured awards fill page 1 and the first 23 places of page 2.
  - 472 items, 472 distinct.
  - The first 73 are exactly the featured awards A–Z. The other 399 are exactly the non-featured awards A–Z.
  - `found_posts` and Kadence's `foundPosts` are 472 (0.12.3 reports 466), and `maxNumPages` is 10.

- **`presets/seo-by-rank-math.json`**: `console_caching_control` = `365` (Rank Math keeps twice this, 730 days). A new, generic `limits` section (`includes/class-seoprostack-presets.php`, `limit()`) runs the plugin's own filter (`rank_math/analytics/max_days_allowed`, default 90) and lowers the value to the site's limit, adding to the dialog description: "The plugin allows at most 90 on this site (such as by its plan), so the preset sets 90 instead of 365."

title: GH#345: feat: Hosting needs finds the site's CDN and suggests one when there is none
body:
## Summary

Hosting needs now finds the CDN in front of the site and suggests one when there is none, instead of SEO Pro Stack running its own image CDN (owner's decision, PR #344).

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`:
- `cdn()`: request headers a CDN passes to the site (`CF-Ray` → Cloudflare, `X-Sucuri-ClientIP` → Sucuri), then `cdn_plugin()`, then the cached `cdn_probe`.
- `cdn_plugin()`: LiteSpeed Cache `litespeed.conf.cdn-quic` (QUIC.cloud) or `litespeed.conf.cdn` (CDN mapping); Cloudflare plugin signed in (`cloudflare_cached_domain_name`, no key read); Bunny CDN (`bunnycdn_cdn_hostname` with `bunnycdn_cdn_status` > 0, as `BunnyCDN\Config\Cdn`); CDN Enabler (`cdn_enabler['cdn_hostname']`); Jetpack `photon` / `photon-cdn` modules.
- `cdn_probe()`: one `wp_remote_head(home_url('/'))` (5 s, no redirects), cached in the hourly facts transient. A failed request is `unknown`, never "no CDN".
- Advice (`recommended`, only when `none`): QUIC.cloud through LiteSpeed Cache on a LiteSpeed server, Cloudflare's free plan elsewhere. Site Health Info gains a **CDN** field (provider / None found / Unknown).
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json` notes: QUIC.cloud's CDN needs the site linked to a QUIC.cloud account, which a preset cannot do.

### Headers, each confirmed

- Cloudflare: `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray` (statically.io and client-a.example responses); request `HTTP_CF_RAY` (Sucuri plugin's `base.lib.php`).
- Bunny CDN: `server: BunnyCDN-…`, `cdn-pullzone`, `cdn-requestid` (bunny.net response).
- Fastly: `fastly-restarts`, `x-served-by: cache-…` (fastly.com response).
- CDN77: `server: CDN77-Turbo`, `x-77-pop`, `x-77-cache` (cdn77.com response).
- QUIC.cloud: `x-qc-cache` (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 `src/core.cls.php`, its QUIC.cloud cache header).
- Sucuri: request `HTTP_X_SUCURI_CLIENTIP` (Sucuri Security plugin, `isBehindFirewall`).
- Left out, not confirmed: CloudFront (`x-amz-cf-id`), `x-sucuri-id`, `x-qc-pop`.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker site (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3), home page answer faked with a must-use `pre_http_request` filter:

| Case | State | Site Health field | Advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| real loopback (cannot reach itself in Docker) | unknown | Unknown | no |
| none | none | None found | yes |
| cloudflare / bunny / fastly / cdn77 / qc | found | Cloudflare / Bunny CDN / Fastly / CDN77 / QUIC.cloud | no |
| `WP_Error` | unknown | Unknown | no |

Plugins (with the "none" answer): LiteSpeed CDN mapping → "A CDN set up in LiteSpeed Cache"; `cdn-quic` → QUIC.cloud; Bunny disabled → none, enabled → Bunny CDN; CDN Enabler hostname → found; `HTTP_CF_RAY` → Cloudflare; `HTTP_X_SUCURI_CLIENTIP` → Sucuri. Debug log empty.

Production check (read-only, client-a.example behind Cloudflare): the same `wp_remote_head(home_url('/'))` returns `200 server=cloudflare cf-ray=…-LHR`.

`scripts/lint.sh`: all passed. `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed, no PHP messages.

Resolves #345

title: GH#277: feat: block web access to log and backup files, and name exposed ones in Site Health
body:
## Summary

A new choice in **Turn off unused remote access**, "Block web access to log and backup files", and an always-on Site Health test that names such files anyone can download.

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hardening.php`:
- `item_options()`: new `files` choice, off by default like the others.
- `files_rules()`: one `FilesMatch` for `^(error_log|php_errorlog|wp-config.+\.php)$|\.(log|sql|sql\.gz|bak)$` with `Require all denied` (the rule from the issue, plus `.bak` and wp-config copies). `wp-config.+\.php` leaves the real `wp-config.php` alone without a lookahead.
- `files_maybe_sync()` (admin_init, main site only, one site option read when nothing changed): writes a marked block (`# BEGIN SEO Pro Stack log and backup files`) at the **top** of the site's `.htaccess`, as `noabort_write()` in Plugin fixes does. A folder's own `.htaccess` gets one only when wp-content or uploads is outside the site's folder, because rules cover the folders below them. Retries while a file can't be written. The server type is in the hash, so a site moved between Nginx and Apache syncs again.
- Follows `switched_on()`, not `enabled()`: the feature waits for Hostinger Tools / Disable Bloat, and neither of them blocks these files (Hostinger sites are where this was found).
- Nginx: `nginx_rules()` shown in the options. Other servers that don't read `.htaccess`: a note to ask the host. Unwritable: the block to add by hand.
- `deactivate()` removes the block (on multisite: network-wide, or from the main site). `uninstall.php` removes it too if deactivation couldn't write the file, plus the option.
- Site Health async test `seoprostack-exposed-files` (always on, advice only): files with matching names and a size above 0 bytes in the top level of the site's folder, ABSPATH, wp-content (so `debug.log`) and uploads. Largest first, one `HEAD` each, at most 10, cached a day in a transient. Files that answer 200 are listed as `recommended` under Security, with name and size (never contents) and a link to the choice. `.php` copies are blocked but **not requested**, because requesting a PHP file runs it. If every request fails, the result is "could not be checked", not "none found".
- Files are never deleted or moved.

#345's CDN probe and this test both use core's `https_local_ssl_verify` filter for requests to the site itself.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker site (Apache, WordPress latest, PHP 8.3); a test-only must-use plugin sends the site's requests to itself to Apache inside the container:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `uploads/test_abc.log`, root `error_log`, `backup.sql.gz` created; feature off | `curl` 200 for each; Site Health AJAX (`health-check-seoprostack-exposed-files`): `recommended`, "Log or backup files can be downloaded by anyone", lists all three with sizes; an empty `.log` is skipped; the wp-config copy is not requested |
| Same, loopback unreachable | `good`, "Log and backup files could not be checked" (3 checked, 3 failed) |
| Choice on, admin screen loaded | Block at the top of `/var/www/html/.htaccess`, once; panel: "blocked by rules in /var/www/html/.htaccess"; `.log`, `error_log`, `.sql.gz`, `.bak` and `wp-config-before-x.php` give 403; image, `robots.txt`, sitemap, admin-ajax, home and `wp-login.php` give 200; Site Health now `good` |
| Choice off | Block gone, files 200 again, option deleted |
| Nginx (globals simulated) | Block removed, status `nginx`, panel shows the `location` rule |
| Rule on real Nginx (`nginx:alpine`, `nginx -t` OK) | 403 for `error_log`, `uploads/a.log`, `b.sql.gz`, `c.bak`, `wp-config-old.php`; real `wp-config.php` reaches the PHP location; `pic.png`, `robots.txt`, `my_error_log.txt` 200 |
| Back to Apache | Re-synced on its own (server type in the hash) |
| Deactivate | Block removed, option gone |
| Deactivate with `.htaccess` read-only, then `wp plugin uninstall --skip-delete` | Block kept at deactivation; uninstall removed it, plus the option and transient |

Debug log empty. `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed. `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed, no PHP messages.

Resolves #277

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-cleanup.php`:

- **Checked as cron runs them** (`cron_observe()`, at `shutdown` of a web cron request, at most hourly, while the switch is on): each task with no callback is noted with when it was first and last seen without one. A task seen with a callback starts over. WP-CLI requests never check, because Hostinger's Monarx agent adds `mnx_*` tasks from `auto_prepend_file` on web requests only (as the issue warns).
- **Sites whose cron runs from WP-CLI** (`cron_ask()`): an admin screen sends a non-blocking request to `wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron=seoprostack-check` when no check ran for 12 hours (at most hourly), as `spawn_cron()` does. I read core's `wp-cron.php` (WordPress latest): a GET lock value that matches no lock makes it `return` before running anything, after loading WordPress with `DOING_CRON` (every plugin loaded).
- **Candidates** (`cron_candidates()`): no callback on checks at least 7 days apart, the last check under 2 days old, and no callback in the request doing the removal. **Never removed** (`cron_protected()`):
  - core tasks (`wp_*` plus `delete_expired_transients`, `recovery_mode_clean_expired_keys`, `upgrader_scheduled_cleanup`, `importer_scheduled_cleanup`, `publish_future_post`, `do_pings`), `mnx_*` and `seoprostack_*`;
  - tasks put back;
  - tasks of installed plugins, active or not: the name starts with a plugin's folder, main file or text domain, or with their first part;
  - tasks whose name's first part other code in the request uses (`cron_live()`).
- Removal: `wp_unschedule_hook()`. The events are kept exactly as stored (time, key, schedule, interval, args) in a non-autoloaded option. **Put back** writes them back through `_get_cron_array()` / `_set_cron_array()`, so a task whose custom schedule no longer exists comes back unchanged, and keeps them from then on.
- Panel: tasks waiting to go, with the recommended plugin each most likely came from (`admin/data/free-plugins.php` slugs), the last check, and the last removal with **Put back**. `wp seoprostack clean-database --dry-run` lists the tasks.
- Not in the default items. Uninstall removes the two new options.

### Why the protections go beyond folder names

On the throwaway site the first version would have removed the tasks of two installed plugins:
- **Rank Math** (active, folder `seo-by-rank-math`): its disabled modules leave `rank_math/...` tasks with no callback, and the folder doesn't match. Its main file `rank-math.php` does, and so does the live-namespace rule while any `rank_*` hook has code.
- **LiteSpeed Cache** (inactive): its tasks are `litespeed_task_*`, not `litespeed_cache_*`. The folder's first part (`litespeed_`) matches.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker site (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3; Rank Math, Burst, FluentSMTP, weDocs active; Akismet and LiteSpeed Cache inactive):

- Test tasks: `sps_test_orphan` (hourly, no callback); `sps_test_custom` (schedule `sps_gone`, interval 600, args `[5]`, written straight into the cron array); `mnx_ten_minutes_test`; `akismet_test_cleanup`; `litespeed_test_task`.
- `curl wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron=seoprostack-check`: 200. The check recorded the tasks with no callback. Overdue `wp_scheduled_delete` (cron is off on this site) was **not run**: next run unchanged.
- First sightings backdated 8 days. `--dry-run` lists only `sps_test_custom` and `sps_test_orphan` (not core, `mnx_*`, Akismet, LiteSpeed or Rank Math).
- Run: both removed and gone from `wp cron event list`. Recorded as stored, including `sps_gone` / 600 / `[5]`.
- Panel (admin): "Scheduled tasks last checked …" and "Removed …: sps_test_custom, sps_test_orphan." **Put back** through the form (admin-post, nonce): 302 back. Both tasks return at their original times, `sps_test_custom` with `sps_gone`, 600 and `[5]`. They are on the keep list and the next dry run finds 0.
- WP-CLI cron path: last check set 13 h back, then an admin screen load. The check ran in the background (4 s before) and the "asked" transient was set.
- Guess: `antispam_bee_daily_cleanup` (Antispam Bee not installed), backdated, then the panel shows "`antispam_bee_daily_cleanup` (probably antispam-bee)".
- Default items: `transients,trash,spam,auto_drafts,orphaned_meta`.
- Debug log empty.

`scripts/lint.sh`: all passed. `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed, no PHP messages. Plugin Check and preflight run in CI.

Not done: the issue's side note that Hosting needs could name the missing Monarx schedule. It's optional, and the site already fixed it with a must-use plugin.

Resolves #278

title: GH#279: feat: name options saved on every page view, keep known licence timestamps, keep page learning through record writes
body:
## Summary

The three parts of #279: Hosting needs names options saved on most page views; Ask before licence checks keeps known licence timestamps; plugin-loading stops restarting its page learning on such writes.

New `includes/class-seoprostack-option-writes.php` (`SEOProStack_Option_Writes`), with no other SEO Pro Stack dependencies so it can load early:

- **Known licence options** (`KNOWN`, one line each, from the guard that fixed the Hostinger site): Complianz Pro `cmplz_transients` → `cmplz_license_status`, Really Simple Security Pro `rsssl_transients` → `rsssl_pro_license_status`, Fluent Forms Pro `_ff_fluentform_pro_license_status_checking`, Tutor LMS Pro `tutor_license_info`, WP-Optimize Premium `wp-optimize-premium_updater_options`. A `pre_update_option_{name}` filter returns the stored value only when:
  - the stored state is valid (`valid` or `activated`);
  - the stored expiry, where there is one, is at least a week away;
  - the new value equals the stored one without the timestamp field.

  For the "transients" arrays only the licence entry is put back, so other entries still save. This is stricter than the site's guard, which put the licence entry back even when its state changed.
- **Counting**: on 1 in 20 page views (GET, not admin, cron or CLI), `updated_option`/`added_option` are counted per option with the plugin, must-use plugin or theme from the backtrace. Transients are skipped.

**Why early loading matters**: Fluent Forms Pro (as patched) saves its option while its file loads, and plugins load in folder order, so `fluentformpro` runs before `seoprostack`. The guard on the live site worked because it was a must-use plugin. `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::start()` (the must-use file of Load plugins only where needed, which the owner's sites use) now loads the helper and starts counting and keeping when Hosting needs or Ask before licence checks is on. Without that file both start when SEO Pro Stack loads. README says what that misses. I didn't make the must-use file serve these two features on its own. That would change its lifecycle (written and removed with Load plugins only where needed); a follow-up can do it if wanted.

**Hosting needs** (`class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`):
- At `shutdown` (before its own writes), a counted site page view adds to `seoprostack_hosting_writes`: per day, the pages counted and, for each option, the pages that saved it and its source. Not autoloaded, 7 days, at most 50 options a day.
- `frequent_writes()`: options saved on more than half the page views counted, once 20 are counted.
- Advice (`recommended`): "These settings are saved again on almost every page view, which slows pages and clears the object cache: …", each with its plugin name and share. If a known licence option is listed and Ask before licence checks is off, the advice says to turn it on. There's also a Site Health Info line.
- Counts start again on plugin deactivation or update, and when Ask before licence checks is switched. Uninstall removes the option.

**Plugin-loading** (`front_option_changed()` → new `record_write()`). I checked: every `updated_option`/`added_option`/`deleted_option` except a short list called `forget_front()`, which writes a new `seoprostack_plugin_front_revision`. So a plugin saving an option on every request restarted page learning on every request. That includes SEO Pro Stack's own Hosting needs records (`seoprostack_hosting_traffic` on 1 in 20 requests, the day's memory peak).

I didn't take the issue's suggestion to derive the revision from the plugin list and versions only: that would drop the documented rule that stored-setting changes invalidate decisions. Writes that keep a record leave decisions alone:
- SEO Pro Stack's own `seoprostack_*` records (`seoprostack_options` still invalidates);
- the known licence options, and options Hosting needs found saved on most page views;
- writes on cron and on GET requests outside wp-admin, AJAX, REST and WP-CLI.

Writes from wp-admin, AJAX, REST, WP-CLI and form posts still invalidate.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker site (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3). Test plugin `aaa-sps-writes` saves on include, before SEO Pro Stack: `sps_test_licence` (unknown), a Complianz-like `cmplz_transients`, a Fluent-like object. `zzz-sps-writes` saves Tutor-like and WP-Optimize-like options on `init`. A must-use logger records each real `updated_option`.

| Run (page views) | Writes logged |
|---|---|
| Features off (3) | all 5 options, 3 times each |
| Ask before licence checks on, no must-use file (5) | `sps_test_licence`, `cmplz_transients`, Fluent: 5 each; Tutor and WP-Optimize: 0 |
| + Load plugins only where needed (must-use file) (5) | `sps_test_licence` only |
| Stored Complianz state `invalid` (3) | `cmplz_transients` 3 (saved as usual) |
| Stored Complianz expiry 2 days, set by SQL (3) | `cmplz_transients` once (`/?sps=1`, renewed to 30 days), then kept |

- Seeding the expiry through `update_option()` was refused while the stored licence was valid for 30 days, as intended, so the seed used SQL.
- Detection: 600 views counted 41, then 300 + 400 more counted 29 after deleting the option. Result: `sps_test_licence` share 1, source `plugin:aaa-sps-writes`. The advice: "These settings are saved again on almost every page view, which slows pages and clears the object cache: sps_test_licence (AAA SPS write test (loads before SEO Pro Stack), 100% of page views)." Site Health Info shows the same; below 20 views it says "Not known yet (13 of 20 page views counted)". The known options weren't listed: they were never written.
- Hint: with Ask before licence checks off, seeded counts (`cmplz_transients` 24 of 25, another option 5 of 25) gave the advice with "Turn on Ask before licence checks …" and left out the 5-of-25 option. Switching the setting (`seoprostack_setting_saved`) deleted the counts.
- Front revision: `777b1961-…` before and after 600 page views with 600 option writes, and after an admin screen. `wp option update blogdescription …` changed it (`e7b56975-…`), as a real setting should.
- Debug log empty.

`scripts/lint.sh`: all passed. `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed, no PHP messages. Plugin Check and preflight run in CI.

Resolves #279

Runtime evidence carried over from #307, for byte-identical preset and adapter code:

- Reapplying makes no outgoing requests.

- When the native save is locked, the earlier redirect is put back and the undo copy is kept.

title: GH#293: feat: Code Snippets test in Site Health names slow, unused and replaceable snippets
body:
## Summary

New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-snippets-audit.php` (`SEOProStack_Snippets_Audit`, registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`). It adds a **Code Snippets** test to Tools → Site Health while Code Snippets or Code Snippets Pro is active:

- always on, advice only, with no setting, like the log-files test in `SEOProStack_Hardening`;
- an async test with an `async_direct_test` and an AJAX handler;
- detection: an active plugin folder starting `code-snippets` plus Code Snippets' table, so it doesn't rely on the plugin's classes being loaded.

It reads `{prefix}snippets` (and `{base_prefix}ms_snippets` on multisite), at most 500 rows each, and never changes a snippet. Each finding links to the snippet's edit screen, built as Code Snippets 3.10's `get_menu_url()` builds it, including its `code_snippets_compact_menu` filter. The test names an active snippet that is:

- **front-end styles, head scripts or footer scripts**: Pro serves these through a separate uncached request on every page. Admin styles do the same on every admin screen.
- **a content snippet nothing uses**: its ID isn't in a `[code_snippet id|snippet_id=N]` shortcode or a `wp:code-snippets/*` block with `"snippet_id":N`. Searched: post content in any status except trash and auto-draft (revisions excluded), the Text, Custom HTML and block widgets, and theme mods. The advice says to check page builders first, because their data isn't searched.
- **code an SEO Pro Stack setting does** (`REPLACES`, each pattern set must all match). It links to the setting using its schema label and tab:
  - `kadence_blocks_pro_query_loop_query_vars` with sticky → Pinned posts for any post type;
  - `rank_math_focus_keyword` → Rank Math defaults;
  - `created_…` with `wp_update_term()` → Term tools;
  - `get_field_objects()` with `wp_update_post()` → Custom fields to content;
  - Kadence query classes with scroll calls → Kadence query filters scroll to results.
- **saving the post again from `save_post`**: `wp_update_post()` inside a `save_post` hook, unless the code also has `remove_action`, `remove_filter`, `did_action` or a `static` flag.

It also names Code Snippets' own samples (their description contains "This is a sample snippet.") and inactive snippets whose `modified` (GMT) is over 180 days old.

I verified the schema, scopes, sample text, shortcode attributes, edit-menu slugs and GMT `modified` against Code Snippets 3.10.2's source. CSS and JS snippets are a Pro-only type (`get_is_pro()`), and I had no Pro copy. That check uses the stored scope; the request it describes is the one seen on the client site in the issue.

Not done: the issue's optional "Export to a must-use plugin" action. It's optional, and it would be the first feature here that writes PHP files.

## Verification

Throwaway site (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3), Code Snippets 3.10.2 with its 4 samples. Fixture snippets, set up with `$wpdb->insert()`:

- active footer JS and active admin CSS;
- three active content snippets: one used in a published post (`[code_snippet id="8" format]`), one in a draft's `code-snippets/content` block, one used only in a trashed post;
- inactive snippets: one modified 2025-01-01, one modified now;
- active Rank Math, term-slug, unguarded `save_post` and guarded (`remove_action`) `save_post` snippets.

`SEOProStack_Snippets_Audit::test()` returned `recommended`, "11 code snippets slow pages or are not needed". It named:

- the footer JS and admin CSS;
- the content snippet used only in trash;
- the Rank Math snippet (link to Rank Math defaults, `tab=links`) and the term-slug snippet (link to Term tools, `tab=content`);
- the unguarded `save_post` snippet;
- the 4 samples and the 2025 inactive snippet.

It didn't name the shortcode-used or block-used content snippets, the recent inactive snippet or the guarded `save_post` snippet.

Also checked on that site:

- The edit link for snippet 7, opened logged in, shows "T293 unused content".
- With Code Snippets deactivated, `site_status_tests` has no `seoprostack-snippets` test; reactivated, it's back.
- The debug log stayed empty.

Checks:

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors. The warnings are the expected release-only ones.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed, after merging main (#295).

Resolves #293

title: feat: Developer admins, choose who can change plugins, themes, admins and site settings
body:
## What

New **Developer admins** feature (Admin tab, off by default). Choose which administrators are developers; other administrators (client admins) can be stopped from:

- installing, deleting or editing plugin and theme code (`code`, default)
- switching plugins on or off or changing the theme (`activate`, default)
- making administrators or editing developers (`admins`, default)
- changing the site addresses and administration email (`site`, default)
- changing permalinks or search engine visibility (`search`, default)
- running updates (`updates`, optional)
- adding unfiltered HTML (`html`, optional)

SEO Pro Stack's settings, admin bar star and Plugins row are developer-only, so nobody else can switch the limits off or deactivate the plugin.

## No lockout

- Switching it on ticks only the person switching it on.
- The person saving is always kept on the list (tested: unticking yourself re-adds you).
- When no ticked person is still an administrator, every administrator counts as a developer (tested by demoting `dev` to Editor with WP-CLI).
- On multisite, developers are super admins.

## Moved from Organise the admin menu

Client safeguards and the developer list move out of Organise the admin menu, so they work without the organised menu. `is_developer()` there and in the dashboard layout now delegates to `SEOProStack_Developers`; **Preview the admin as › Client administrator** still shows the limits. Settings version 22 migrates `admin_menu_safeguards` / `admin_menu_developers` to `developers` / `developers_users` / `developers_limits` (`code`, `admins`): same behaviour, same developers (tested on a seeded v21 site).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-developers.php` (new)
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-dashboard-layout.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` (registration, `DB_VERSION` 22)
- `admin/data/admin-menu.php`, `admin/data/dashboard.php`

title: GH#387: fix: object cache warning names the cause and offers a working address
body:
## Summary

Hosting needs now says why LiteSpeed Cache's object cache is not working: PHP not loading the memcached/redis extension (Hostinger's hPanel switch only enables it for some PHP versions), its drop-in missing or replaced, or no server at the configured host and port. When another local server answers (Hostinger's Memcached listens only on ::1), the warning has a nonce-protected 'Use Memcached at [::1]:11211' link for administrators (network administrators when LiteSpeed Cache is network-active). The link re-checks the server, saves only kind/host/port through LiteSpeed Cache's own Conf code (which rewrites its drop-in settings file), empties the cache at the new address as LiteSpeed Cache does on reconnect, and re-runs the check. LiteSpeed settings are read from network options when it is network-active. A missing-extension result is rechecked as soon as the extension loads.



## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php

The first build saved but stayed unreachable because the old cache held stale litespeed.conf values; fixed by flushing via the PHP extension (LiteSpeed's own Object_Cache refuses after LITESPEED_OC_FAILURE). (2) kind set to Redis on ::1 -> cause=server, Memcached offered; click -> kind Memcached, state=working. title: GH#390: fix: Remove CPT base never redirects when no chosen post type is registered
body:
## Summary

`SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base::redirect_old()` passed `self::types()` to `is_singular()`. When the plugin that registers the chosen post types isn't loaded on a request, `types()` is `[]`, and `is_singular( array() )` is true for any item. The CPT archive URL then resolves to the static front page, and the method 301s it to the home page, which browsers keep caching after the site recovers.

- Returns early when `types()` is empty.
- Defence in depth: it redirects only when the queried item's `post_type` is one of the chosen types.
- `resolve()` already returns early on an empty list, and `short_link()` uses `in_array()`, so neither has the problem.
- Changelog: Unreleased Fix entry in `README.md` and `changelog.txt`.

Resolves #390

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (front-end redirects); verified with runtime reproduction.
- Throwaway WordPress in Docker (MariaDB 11, `wordpress:cli`): pretty permalinks, a static front page, a must-use plugin that registers `directory` (`has_archive`) unless `GH390_OFF` is set, item `item-1`, and Remove CPT base on for `directory`. Each request ran in-process (`REQUEST_URI`, `wp()`, then `redirect_old()`), with `wp_redirect` captured.

| Request | `main` (daf50a7) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/directory/`, type registered | archive, no redirect | archive, no redirect |
| `/directory/item-1/`, type registered | 301 → `/item-1/` | 301 → `/item-1/` |
| `/directory/`, type **not** registered (`types=[]`, front page queried) | **301 → `/`** | no redirect |

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.

title: GH#392: chore: align own docs and code with WP Plugin Starter 1.0.9; forget site pages once per request
body:
## Summary

Brings SEO Pro Stack's own files (the ones `scripts/sync-core.sh` does not touch) up to the standards WP Plugin Starter set in 1.0.1 to 1.0.9, and fixes two performance gaps the `STANDARDS.md` → Performance audit found. The full per-release review is on #392.

Resolves #392

## Changes, each with the starter rule it follows

| Change | Rule |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` shortened to a map (86 lines): replaced-plugin steps moved to new `docs/replaced-plugins.md`, the LiteSpeed Cache preset decision (#285) to `docs/presets.md`, live-site timing to `TESTING.md`; a rule `STANDARDS.md` already holds dropped | 1.0.2 / 1.0.7 `STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs |
| `TESTING.md` rewritten: only checks the scripts cannot do (visual, live hosting, other plugins, multisite); the manual "Performance Testing" checklist and CI notes the smoke test now covers removed; checklists for features that no longer exist (Sync Guard, the Multisite category) removed | 1.0.9 smoke test with query checks |
| `STABILITY.md` and `ROADMAP.md` removed: last accurate at 0.3.0, nothing links to them; `changelog.txt` and GitHub issues replace them | Agent docs: no stale or duplicate docs |
| `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`: `[[ ]]` tests | 1.0.5 shell style |
| `scripts/count_files_by_extension.zsh` removed: an early unused shell snippet, referenced nowhere, not in the starter | Structure |
| `forget_front()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`): forgets what Load plugins only where needed learned for site pages once at the first change in a request, and once more at `shutdown` if more changes followed, instead of at every change | 1.0.9 Performance: no repeated writes |
| `SEOProStack_Setup::prime_admin_options()`: ten small, non-autoloaded options every admin screen reads are loaded with one `wp_prime_option_caches()` query (WordPress 6.4+; older versions keep separate reads) | 1.0.9 Performance: options, WordPress first |
| `changelog.txt` and `README.md` → Changelog entries; README also gets the #391 entries it was missing | — |

No core file changes: `scripts/sync-core.sh --check --from <starter>` says all 51 core files match starter `58b5bc5`.

## Measurements

`scripts/smoke-test.sh`, WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3, 10,001 posts and 30,002 meta rows. `own` = queries from SEO Pro Stack's code.

| request | before: own queries | after: own queries |
|---|---|---|
| admin screens, default settings | 5 | 1 |
| admin screens, every feature on (82) | 15 | 8 |
| first admin screen after switching every feature on | 314 (116.6 ms) | 210 (96.1 ms) |
| `seoprostack_plugin_front_revision` writes in that request | ~45 | 1–2 |
| `seoprostack_plugin_front_lock` lookups, whole run | 38 | 5 |
| visitor pages | 0 (default) / 2–7 (all on) | unchanged |

On WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 the option reads are unchanged (no `wp_prime_option_caches()`); the `forget_front()` change applies.

The 210 left on the first screen are one-off set-up when the features are first switched on: the three starter short links (posts, meta, terms), next-gen image rules and the plugin map.

## Audit findings with no change needed

- **Front end:** every feature's public CSS/JS/output is gated on that feature and printed inline; nothing loads when a feature is off. Visitor pages run 0 of SEO Pro Stack's queries with the default settings.
- **Remote requests:** none on a page view. `cron_ask()` runs from an admin screen at most every 12 hours with a transient lock and does not block; Next-gen rule check from its settings tab; Hardening file check from Site Health and weekly cron; Hosting needs' CDN probe at most hourly (`facts()` transient); Really Simple Security check only on a preset action; Screenshots and link health in cron.
- **Own tables:** `seoprostack_links` (PK `post_id,url_hash`, key `target_id`), `seoprostack_link_health` (key `checked_at`), `seoprostack_link_clicks` (PK `post_id,url_hash,day`, key `day`) cover every lookup, join and delete. The click report sorts by an aggregate (`ORDER BY events`), which no index can serve; it is admin-only, limited to 90 days and click counting is off by default (owner's choice).
- **Option writes on page views:** Hosting needs writes its memory peak only when a request beats the day's peak, and its timing sample for 1 in 20 requests (not autoloaded). No other own writes on visitor pages in either smoke round.
- **Admin data files** (`admin/data/*.php`, about 155 KB): data is inside functions called only on their tabs; under opcache only the definitions load.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WP 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: both passed, `queries: ok` in the default and every-feature-on rounds, canary found, no PHP messages, clean uninstall.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker`: 0 errors; `AGENTS.md is 86 lines and names every doc in docs/`. Warnings are the usual pre-release ones (Unreleased section, WordPress.org slug, existing tag).
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check`: all 51 core files match.

title: GH#395: fix: PHPStan level-7 findings, security-relevant files first (281 to 162)
body:
## Summary

First PR for #395, security-relevant files first. The level-7 probe (the config in #395: `phpstan.neon.dist` plus the four `missingType.*` ignores) goes from **281 to 162** findings. `phpstan.neon.dist` stays at level 5 (starter core file).

Real fixes (runtime behaviour on edge cases):

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-svg-uploads.php`: a failed `file_get_contents()` returns "could not be read" instead of passing `false` to `clean()`; a failed XPath query in `use_is_bounded()` rejects the SVG (fails closed); a failed `preg_split()` of the viewBox returns no dimensions.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`: `after_generate()` and `remove()` stop when the attachment has no file, so a restore can never copy into `/<file>` from an empty folder path (`record_current()` already checked this, but in a separate call).
- `includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-watermark-gd.php`: failed `wp_imagecreatetruecolor()` or `imagecolorallocatealpha()` returns a `WP_Error` instead of passing `false` on.
- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`: only `stdClass` results from `plugins_api()` become cards (what core returns for `plugin_information`); `ob_get_clean()` results are cast to string.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-agency-dashboard.php`: `mysql2date()` and `get_permalink()` false results are cast before escaping; `method_exists()` on a booking checks `is_object()` first.
- Shortcodes (`magic-login`, `agency-dashboard`): `(array) $atts`, since WordPress passes `''` when there are no attributes.

Type fixes (no runtime change):

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-magic-login.php`: `verify()` returns the verified `WP_User` (or `WP_Error`) instead of `true`, and both callers use it, so the user is known to be a `WP_User` after the check.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-agency-orders.php`, `class-seoprostack-agency-dashboard.php`: Fluent Forms, Fluent Boards and Fluent Support objects are typed as their real model classes (`\FluentForm\App\Models\Submission`, `Form`, `\FluentBoards\App\Models\Task`, `\FluentSupport\App\Models\Agent`) instead of `object`. Those plugins are not installed for analysis, which `phpstan-plugin.neon` already covers, so no stubs or ignores are added.
- Option lists keyed by ID (`course_options()`, `page_options()`, `get_category_labels()`): return types now say `array<int|string,string>`, since PHP makes numeric keys integers.
- `class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`: `editor_classes()` returns `list<class-string<...>>`, so `call_user_func()` and `->load()` are checked.

Left for later PRs: 149 findings in other files. The 13 in `class-seoprostack-watermark-gd.php` are PHP 7.4 signature noise (`resource` vs PHP 8's `GdImage`); they need an ignore with that reason when the level is raised, and an ignore now would fail level 5 as unmatched.

## Files Changed

admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-agency-dashboard.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-agency-orders.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-magic-login.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-svg-uploads.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php, includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-watermark-gd.php

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical (login code)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — the real magic-login HTTP flow on disposable WordPress sites in Docker, with this branch's plugin folder mounted, on **WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3** and **WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4**: 11 passed, 0 failed on each.
  1. Request form has its nonce.
  2. Requesting a link for an editor answers "Check your email".
  3. The emailed link is captured (`pre_wp_mail`).
  4. The confirm page (`render_confirm()`) shows the editor's uid.
  5. A wrong token is refused.
  6. The confirm POST (`handle_confirm()`) sets `wordpress_logged_in`.
  7. It redirects to `/wp-admin/`.
  8. `profile.php` shows the editor logged in.
  9. Reusing the link is refused.
  10. `[wpmll_form]` with no attributes renders.
  11. `debug.log` stays empty.
- Static checks: `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passed (level 5). Level-7 probe 281 → 162, with magic login, SVG uploads, agency orders, agency dashboard, plugin manager and watermark images at 0.

title: GH#395: fix: PHPStan level-7 findings batch 2 — false returns, WP_Error guards, array query vars (162 to 79)
body:
## Summary

Second PR for #395. The level-7 probe (the config in #395: `phpstan.neon.dist` plus the four `missingType.*` ignores) goes from **162 to 79** findings. `phpstan.neon.dist` stays at level 5 (starter core file).

Real fixes (runtime behaviour on edge cases):

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` (Load plugins only where needed): `?name[]=x` or `?pagename[]=x` no longer reach `front_post_by_path()` as an array; the request is treated as unknown, so every plugin loads. `?taxonomy[]=x` is no longer compared as a taxonomy name.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-term-tools.php`: merge with an empty taxonomy returns `failed` instead of looking terms up in `''`; `get_terms()` / `get_term_children()` `WP_Error` results are skipped instead of iterated; the bulk-action list checks `get_taxonomy()` before `->public`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-delay-scripts.php`: a page with no `</body>` is returned unchanged (before, `substr($html, 0, false)` dropped the page and printed only the loader).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-notices.php`: a failed XPath query no longer calls `->item()` / `->length` on `false`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-gone-urls.php`: a malformed URL (`http:///broken`) or home URL is ignored instead of reading `host` from `false`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: a day with no hourly data no longer calls `max([])` (a `ValueError` on PHP 8).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: a plugin name that is not valid UTF-8 keeps its whole name (new `before_tagline()`), instead of `preg_split()` returning `false` and `[0]` reading from it.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-word-import.php`: a PCRE limit keeps the text untrimmed instead of reading `$m[2]` from an empty match.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-auto-upload.php`: an imported image with no URL returns a `WP_Error` instead of `false`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-replace-media.php`: keeps the known path if `get_attached_file()` returns `false`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-sticky-posts.php`: `get_taxonomy()` false is checked; sticky-post merge asks for `'fields' => 'all'` so a query var can't turn it into IDs.
- `preg_split()` results in settings lists (admin menu moves, delay scripts, gone URLs, image loading, preload pages, screenshots, brand icons, term legacy shortcodes) fall back to `array()`.
- Shortcodes (`simple_icon`, the four favourites shortcodes): `(array) $atts`, since WordPress passes `''` when there are no attributes.

SonarCloud follow-up: the two term-legacy class lists use a new `classes()` helper (no nested ternary); restrict content's term grouping moved to `terms_by_taxonomy()` (cognitive complexity back under 15); the two Next-gen images `md5()` lines that the casts touched carry `// NOSONAR` with the reason (a fingerprint to notice changed settings, not security), as the GitHub updater already does.

Type fixes (no runtime change): `(string)` casts of `wp_json_encode()`, `size_format()`, `get_permalink()`, `wp_parse_url()`, `wp_date()`, `strtok()` and `get_post_mime_type()` results before escaping or hashing; `(int)` for `get_post_thumbnail_id()`, `end($steps)` and `strrpos()`; header values from `wp_remote_retrieve_header()` that may be arrays; hand order reads its rows in one loop instead of `array_combine()` (typed `array|false` on PHP 7.4).

Left for later PRs: 79 findings. The 13 in `includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-watermark-gd.php` are PHP 7.4 signature noise (`resource` vs `GdImage`), as noted in #400. The rest are spread thinly (8 Spectra blocks, 7 link index, 6 GitHub updater core file, 5 starters).

## Files Changed

includes/class-seoprostack-hosting-plans.php, includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php, includes/class-seoprostack-term-legacy.php, uninstall.php, and 33 files in includes/features/ (admin-bar-more, admin-menu, admin-notices, auto-upload, brand-icons, delay-scripts, duplicate-posts, field-content, gone-urls, hand-order, hardening, hosting-needs, image-loading, kadence-library, linking, nextgen-images, old-slugs, plugin-loading, plugin-sizes, post-reactions, post-versions, preload-pages, preview-links, replace-media, resize-uploads, restrict-content, screenshots, sticky-posts, term-displays, term-tools, wikipedia-previews, word-import).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (many small guards across features; Load plugins only where needed runs on every request)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on disposable WordPress sites in Docker with this branch's plugin folder mounted, on **WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3** and **WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4**.
  - `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passed on both: every page 200 (or the expected 404) with default settings and with all 82 features on, query checks ok, uninstall clean, `debug.log` empty.
  - A `wp eval-file` check with all features on, 19 passed, 0 failed on both: term merge (returns `merged:2`, moves the child, re-files the post, empty taxonomy fails cleanly), term move to tags (takes the child), hand order (saves Three, One, Two and numbers every page 1…n), delay scripts (holds back a matching script and adds the loader; leaves a fragment with no `</body>` unchanged), admin notices parser (finds 2 visible notices, nested; empty output), gone URLs normaliser (home URL, other host, malformed URL), term legacy `classes()` (splits, drops empties), restrict content `terms_by_taxonomy()` (groups a category and a tag; unknown term gives none).
  - Front-end requests with array query vars (`?name[]=x`, `?pagename[]=x`) answer 200 with an empty `debug.log`. `?taxonomy[]=category&term=x` answers 500 on WordPress 7.1.2 and 404 on 6.2 **with and without** SEO Pro Stack active: that is core's `WP_Tax_Query`, not this plugin.
- Static checks: `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passed (level 5). Level-7 probe 162 → 79.

body:

title: GH#417: fix: page learning recognises Kadence block settings, block widgets and editor-only inner blocks
body:
Resolves #417

## What

Load plugins only where needed treated most Kadence Blocks content as unrecognised, so those pages loaded every plugin and their page kinds were learned as needing every plugin.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` `content_needs()`: block comments are removed before looking for shortcodes (core runs `do_blocks` at priority 9, before `do_shortcode` at 11, and escapes `--` in attributes, so `<!-- wp:… -->` never holds a shortcode). A block missing from the learned registry belongs to the owners of its namespace's registered blocks (new `namespace_owners()`); a namespace with no registered block, or with an unknown owner, is still unknown.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` `page_needs()`: block, text and Custom HTML widgets are read by their own text instead of `wp_json_encode()` of the option, which wrote `kadence/…` as `kadence\/…`.
- `README.md` (Public pages only, changelog) and `changelog.txt`.

Unknown blocks and shortcodes still load every plugin; nothing else changes.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Read-only probe on the live Hostinger sites: old and new `content_needs()` side by side on each site's real content, with the blocks and shortcodes map SEO Pro Stack stored when it learned there:
  - Site A: synced patterns and widgets went from unknown (every plugin) to 5 plugins (Kadence Blocks, Kadence Blocks Pro, WooCommerce, Fluent Forms, SEO Pro Stack); posts recognised 208 → 266 of 300.
  - Site B: posts recognised 20 → 28 of 38.
  - Left unknown, as intended: indirect synced-pattern references in post content, shortcode-like text that is not a registered shortcode (`[71`), and a block from a plugin that is not active.

## Found alongside, not in this PR

On multisite, network-activated plugins always load (documented) and their blocks are not attributed to them, so content using their blocks is unknown on those sites. That needs a design decision and is filed separately for #226.

title: GH#425: fix: page learning ignores script/style code and unknown pages do not set their kind
body:
## Summary

Page learning in **Load plugins only where needed** had two problems (#425):

1. `content_needs()` read bracket text inside `<script>` and `<style>` bodies (Custom HTML blocks: `items[0]`, `data['on']`, `a[href]`) and footnote marks such as `[1]` as shortcodes. Unregistered names made the page's content "unknown", so it loaded every plugin.
2. When a page with unknown content was the first of its kind to be learned, `page_needs()` stored every active plugin as that kind's needs, so every page of the kind (all posts, say) loaded every plugin.

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`
  - New `SHORTCODE_NAME` constant (the existing pattern, now shared).
  - `content_needs()` takes out script and style bodies; inside them only **registered** shortcode names count. Elsewhere, an unregistered name counts as unknown only if it looks like a shortcode tag (`/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*$/`), so `[1]` and `[elem.name]` no longer do. Registered shortcodes keep working everywhere.
  - `start_front()`: an unlearned page kind is learned only from a page whose own content is known; a page with unknown content loads every plugin without taking the learning lock.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `page_needs()` returns `false` for unknown own content, and `learn_front()` then does not store the kind.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: "no pro version" → "no paid version" (owner's request).
- `changelog.txt`, `README.md`: Unreleased entries.

## Verification

- `composer lint`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- I called `content_needs()` directly outside WordPress (it is a pure function) with these cases:

| Content | Result |
|---|---|
| `<script>` with `items[0]`, `data['on']`, `elem[elem.name]` | `[]` (known) |
| `<style>` with `a[href]`, `input[type=text]` | `[]` |
| `[1]` and `[116]` footnote marks | `[]` |
| registered `[contact-form-7 ...]` inside a script | contact-form-7 |
| registered `[contact-form-7 ...]` in text | contact-form-7 |
| unregistered `[not_registered_tag]` in text | unknown (loads everything, as before) |

Resolves #425

title: GH#437: fix: Hostinger Monarx cron tasks no longer log invalid_schedule errors on every CLI cron run
body:
## Summary

Hostinger's Monarx security agent (the `monarxprotect` PHP extension) registers its `mnx_ten_minutes` schedule only on web requests. Where hPanel cron jobs run `wp-cron.php` from the command line (`DISABLE_WP_CRON`), every due run of `mnx_versions_cron_event` failed to reschedule and logged `Cron reschedule event error for hook: mnx_versions_cron_event, Error code: invalid_schedule` (5,095 lines in one account's `~/error_log` on 2026-10-04), then WordPress dropped the task until the next web visit.

**Fixes for other plugins** now registers, on cron and WP-CLI requests only, a missing schedule of a host's task (`SEOProStack_Database_Cleanup::HOST_CRON`, `mnx_`) with the interval stored with the task. The task stays scheduled; its code is absent from the command line, so nothing runs, as before. Other tasks with a missing schedule (removed plugins) are still dropped.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: `host_cron_schedules()` on `cron_schedules` (priority `PHP_INT_MAX`, only missing schedules, one cron-array scan per site per request), `is_host_task()`, header comment and setting description.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-cleanup.php`: `HOST_CRON` comment: Monarx is a PHP extension, not `auto_prepend_file`.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: Fixes for other plugins entry, the same correction, Unreleased.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS (one scoped `WordPress.WP.CronInterval.ChangeDetected` ignore: the interval is the host's own, read from its stored task) and PHPStan: clean.
- On a Hostinger dev site, after one web visit (Monarx scheduled `mnx_versions_cron_event`):
  - released 0.14.1 file: `wp cron schedule list` had no `mnx_ten_minutes`; the event showed as "Non-repeating";
  - patched file: `mnx_ten_minutes,600` listed; `wp cron event run mnx_versions_cron_event` succeeded and the event was rescheduled 10 minutes later ("10 minutes"); a plain `php` load with `DOING_CRON` registers the schedule; a load without it does not; no new error log lines;
  - released file put back afterwards.

Resolves #437
