title: GH#429: feat: count terms and comments in the background
body:
## Summary

Resolves #429.

- Add **Count terms and comments in the background**, off by default on Server, using the Heartbeat settings schema and database-cleanup scheduling/panel patterns.
- Preserve original taxonomy callbacks, including WooCommerce's; queue comments through WordPress's pre-count filter.
- Schedule one event about five minutes ahead, process at most 500 IDs, and provide capability/nonce-protected **Recount now**.
- Keep pending IDs durable until successful generation-aware acknowledgement. Concurrent writes to an in-flight ID survive; interrupted runs retry. Serialize runners and persistence-failure synchronous recounts with a site-specific connection-owned database lock.
- Flush one batch when disabled, finish any remainder through cron without deferring new changes, and remove the option/hook on uninstall.
- Preserve the concurrently merged Faster page counts feature when integrating current `main`.

## Files Changed

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php`: new feature.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`: feature registration.
- `uninstall.php`: queue and cron cleanup.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`: setting, delay and controls; compact WordPress.org listing stays under 10 KB.

## Runtime Testing

**Risk:** High (manual action and persistent queue). **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4.33 site, with WooCommerce 8.1.1.

| Acceptance criterion | Verified evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Server setting, off by default, with delay explained | Schema/default verified; README and listing updated. |
| No per-term count queries while enabled; correct scheduled counts | 1,000 tag assignments: zero term COUNT queries enabled; scheduled hook restored count to 1,000. Actual `wp cron event run seoprostack_deferred_counts` also passed. |
| Comments and manual recount | First approved comment remained at zero until recount; count then became one. Administrator manual handler drained the queue; missing capability and invalid nonce were rejected. |
| Custom taxonomy and WooCommerce callbacks | Late taxonomy callback restored and called. WooCommerce category counts and native `product_count_product_cat` term meta were correct, including moving a product to draft. |
| Disable flush and uninstall cleanup | Disable recounted queued terms, cleared a finished hook, drained remaining comment work and added no new disabled work. Actual uninstall code removed the queue option and scheduled hook. |
| Durable, bounded processing | A 600-post comment queue left 100 after a 500-ID batch. A throwing callback retained its ID and retry event. A second WP-CLI process updating the same ID during recount survived acknowledgement and drained on the next run. Queue autoload was `no`. |

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all six checks passed, including PHPCS and PHPStan level 7. Repeated after integrating current main.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker`: zero errors. Expected warnings concern Unreleased entries, the existing version tag, and WordPress.org submission naming; no publication requested.
- Standard debug log: zero mentions of `class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php`. Initial fixture retries produced an expected temporary eval-script error for duplicate test data, not a feature error.
- Disposable Docker resources removed after verification. No test infrastructure or fixtures added to the repository.

## Remote gate handoff

- Current implementation head: `ab9849480a3eebd5014bb49c287dab28b4e991ef`, pushed and non-draft, conflict-free after integrating the parallel Server feature.
- Remote lint, CodeQL, SonarCloud and Socket checks passed in the readiness snapshot. Release/Plugin Check and both smoke checks were still running; review was pending.
- Qlty's external status is an error because the project is out of minutes, not a reported target-code finding. No quota, billing or gate configuration was changed.
- The gated merge attempt on the repaired head returned: required checks pending; no repair action eligible. Pulse/webhook automation owns continued check and merge monitoring. The verified merge-summary comment is present.

## Timing

Same 1,000 published posts, assigning one tag through `wp_set_object_terms()`, with `SAVEQUERIES` enabled on the same disposable Docker site:

| Mode | Elapsed | Per-term COUNT queries |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Immediate counting | 17.964 s | 1,000 |
| Background counting | 9.032 s | 0 |

49.7% lower request elapsed time in this run; later recount time is excluded. This is shared-host timing evidence, not a universal throughput guarantee.

## Decisions

- Always queue the first approved comment; setting and README explicitly state that it can lag.
- Retain processing generations instead of deleting before recount, preventing interrupted workers from discarding work while staying within one non-autoloaded option and one cron hook.
- Disable performs one bounded batch immediately and schedules any remainder. Missing taxonomy plugins retain their work until available again.
- No release or publication requested.

title: GH#476: fix: page learning: a stale object-cache copy no longer stops the site saving what it learns
body:
## Summary

On sites with a persistent object cache, a reset of page learning could leave a stale copy of `seoprostack_plugin_front` cached under the option's own key. WordPress's `delete_option()` removes an autoloaded option from `alloptions` only, so `get_option()` kept returning the old map and `update_option()` then updated a row that no longer existed: nothing the site learned was saved, and every visitor page loaded every plugin until the cache dropped the entry. Found by the post-1.3.0 #226 re-survey (one site: 75 skips with 1.2.0, 0 with 1.3.0; the stale entry outlived the row by over an hour).

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: new `drop_option()` (delete the option and its own cache entry) and `save_option()` (drop the own cache entry, then `update_option()`), with the core behaviour explained.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `forget()` and `forget_front_now()` drop `FRONT`, `MAP` and `MENU` with `drop_option()`; the learned-map writes (`front` learning, `setting_saved()`, admin `MAP`) use `save_option()`; `forget_front_now()` reads the map without a stale copy before keeping a recorded failure. A site that is already stuck recovers on the plugin update (`forget()`) or its next learning request.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan): all passed.
- PHPStan: no errors. PHPCS on both changed files: clean.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: passed (WordPress 7.1.2, PHP 8.3; default and every-feature runs; uninstall; no debug.log messages).
- After release: on the affected site, `seoprostack_plugin_front` is saved after a visitor page view and `front_current()` is true; the #226 survey shows skips there again.

Resolves #476
Ref #226

title: GH#463: Preserve HandyPlugins Magic Login block forms
body:
## Summary

Resolves #463. Preserves HandyPlugins’ `magic-login/login-block` in pages and synced patterns after Magic Login is deactivated or deleted.

- Registers a rendering-only dynamic fallback, without editor assets, only when Magic Login is inactive and the block is unregistered.
- Reuses the existing login-link form; with Magic login links off, uses WordPress’s password form.
- Maps saved title, description, login label, button text, redirect and logged-in visibility. Escapes saved text and validates redirects through the existing same-site path.
- Adds the partial replacement and maker credit, documents unsupported AJAX/Pro behaviour, updates both Unreleased changelogs and regenerates the replacement count/download sizes (54 plugins).

### Files changed

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-magic-login.php`
- `README.md`
- `docs/replaced-plugins.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS and PHPStan all pass.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: passed WordPress 7.1.2/PHP 8.3 with 10,000 seeded posts, default settings, all features on, query checks, debug-log checks and uninstall cleanup.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed the minimum supported runtime.
- `php scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write` and `--check`: passed.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified on a separate disposable WordPress 6.2/PHP 8.3 site with Magic Login 2.8.1 installed and active: its renderer remained untouched. Created a published block page and a published synced pattern referenced by another page; then deactivated and deleted Magic Login. Both pages rendered through WordPress’s native `do_blocks()` with saved text and labels in password and login-link modes. Verified logged-in hiding/logout, hostile title and login-label escaping in both modes, external redirect rejection and no editor scripts. Native page-learning registration/content inspection identified SEO Pro Stack as owner for both direct and synced content, rather than returning unknown content. WP-CLI bypasses front-request loader setup, so that isolated inspection initialized the loader’s active-plugin state from WordPress’s stored active list.

Direct HTTP to the separate throwaway site was denied by the worker network policy; no retry or bypass was attempted. The feature checks used WordPress’s native rendering and learning paths via WP-CLI, not a browser assertion about the Plugins screen. The repository’s existing smoke script separately passed its HTTP and log checks.

## Review

Independent static review found an unescaped saved login label in WordPress’s password-form sink. Fixed with `esc_html()` and verified malicious login labels in both modes. No authentication, token handling or rate-limit behaviour was changed.

## Source and decisions

Verified the maker’s repository: https://github.com/HandyPlugins/magic-login. It has no `block.json`; the authoritative server schema is in `includes/block.php`. AJAX submission, hide-after-submit behaviour, plugin redirection rules and Pro features remain explicitly unsupported. No settings migration or new storage is introduced.

title: GH#481: fix: page learning: forget what was learned when SEO Pro Stack's version changes
body:
## Summary

Load plugins only where needed now forgets what was learned (site pages and admin screens) when SEO Pro Stack's own version changes, however it was updated. Before, forgetting ran only on `upgrader_process_complete`, which WP-CLI with `--skip-plugins`, deploys, uploads and Git pulls never run, so decisions learned by older code outlived the fixes in 1.3.0 and 1.3.1.

Found in the post-1.3.1 #226 checks: two sites still had every page kind learned under 1.2.0, each needing every active plugin, so they skipped nothing.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: new `LEARNED_BY` option (`seoprostack_plugin_learned_by`, autoloaded). At the start of `boot()` (before the option-change hooks are added), a version different from `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION` calls `forget()` with the cause `seoprostack_updated` (key: the new version), then saves the version. Up-to-date sites pay one autoloaded read.

title: GH#493: fix: page learning: shortcodes and blocks left by a removed plugin no longer load every plugin
body:
## What

Page learning no longer treats shortcodes or blocks left by a removed plugin in site-wide content (widgets, template parts, posts listed on archives and search) as unknown. Before this change, one such name made the page kind, or every page kind for a widget, load every plugin.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` → `content_needs()`: with `$front['live']`, only registered shortcode names are read as shortcodes, the same rule as in script and style bodies. Names that are registered but have an unknown owner still return `false`.
- `namespace_owners()`: with `live`, a block namespace with no registered block needs no plugin; unregistered blocks show their saved markup. A namespace with an unknown owner still returns `false`.
- Plugins that turn such text or markup into output through `the_*`, `widget_*` or `render_block*` filters are already kept as page hooks (`FRONT_PAGE_PREFIXES`).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` → `page_needs()`: sets `live` for the site-wide texts it checks. It runs at `shutdown` after `wp_footer` on a request that loaded every plugin, so `$shortcode_tags` holds every registration. A name still unregistered had no handler, and WordPress showed it as text; loading fewer plugins cannot add a handler.
- The post's own content and `start_front()`, which runs before plugins load, keep the stricter check.
- README.md and changelog.txt: Unreleased entries.

## Evidence

- In the #226 1.3.3 survey, site E skipped 0 plugin loads (FDP skipped 49). Every learned page kind said "page kind loads every plugin (content not recognised)".
- A read-only pre-check on site E with the deployed `content_needs()` covered 33 widget texts and template parts. Only one Text widget is unknown, and it holds an unregistered shortcode. With unregistered names escaped, as `live` does, 0 are unknown, and the site-wide content needs only Kadence Blocks and WooCommerce.
- Site D, category archives: 0 plugins skipped. A read-only check of its top three categories found 2 of 7–8 listed posts unknown, because they hold `kevinbatdorf/code-block-pro` blocks and Code Block Pro is not installed. With unregistered namespaces dropped, as `live` does, 0 are unknown.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: passed (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3), with no PHP messages.

Resolves #493
Ref #226

title: GH#495: fix: page learning: items at short addresses are learned and skip plugins
body:
## What

Page learning now gives a page kind to items served by **Short addresses for custom post types** (`/item/` instead of `/type/item/`), so they are learned and skip plugins like other singles of their type. Readabler's `readabler_cron_hook_timestamp` is now a record.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` → `front_context()`: before plugins load, saved rewrite rules read `/item/` as a page rule whose page does not exist, so the request had no kind and used only the site-wide choices. The first such page path is remembered; when no other rule matches and the learned routes list short types, `front_short_item()` looks the item up among those types, only after the page and post lookups miss, as `SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base::resolve()` does. Items of two types at one address, or an ambiguous or over-budget lookup, return no kind (site-wide choices).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` → `front_routes()`: saves `short_types` from `SEOProStack_Remove_Cpt_Base::types()` when that feature is on. Changing its settings is a stored-setting change, so pages learn again.
- `RECORD_OPTIONS`: adds `readabler_cron_hook_timestamp`, which Readabler saves as it loads and which showed up in one site's reset record.
- README (Short addresses, Unreleased) and changelog.

## Why

The 1.3.3 survey for #226 found one site's directory entries at short addresses with "page kind not learned yet": SEO Pro Stack skipped no plugins there, where Freesoul Deactivate Plugins skipped several.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passed. PHPStan caught a possible array `pagename` from `parse_str()`; only a string is remembered now.
- Read-only probe on the affected site (`wp --skip-plugins --skip-themes eval-file`, branch loader under another class name, short types supplied in memory only):
  - with short types: item → `single:<type>`, its paged address → `single:<type>`, a post → `single:post`, a page → `single:page`, a missing slug → no kind.
  - without short types (current behaviour): item and paged item → no kind; posts and pages unchanged.

Resolves #495
For #226

- Consolidates shortcode/block registration into one `init` callback: the feature has **20 methods**, down from the flagged 21.
- Builds the string and boolean attribute schemas from their defaults instead of repeated literal declarations, addressing the reported new-code duplication.
- Replaces the flagged nested redirect ternary with a separate redirect assignment and conditional.
- Corrects cherry-pick placement of the changelog entry: it remains Unreleased, not incorrectly under the intervening 1.3.1 release.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-magic-login.php`

## Accumulated CI evidence

title: GH#497: fix: page learning: pages with leftover shortcodes or blocks in their own content learn and skip plugins
body:
## What

A page whose own content holds shortcodes or blocks that no plugin registers (an old theme's `[one_third]`, a removed plugin's blocks) now learns once and then skips plugins. Before, it loaded every plugin on every visit, and a front page like that never let its kind be learned.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`
  - `start_front()`: when a page's own content is unknown before plugins load (kind new or already learned), the request loads every plugin as before. It now also learns if the content would be known with the names absent from the learned maps treated as unregistered (`content_needs()` with `'live' => true`). Content with a registered name of unknown owner still loads every plugin without learning.
  - `content_needs()`: with `'collect'`, notes the unregistered shortcode names and the blocks whose namespace has no registered block that a live check lets pass (`take_unlisted()`). Before plugins load, names in the learned `'inert'` list need no plugin; any other unknown name still returns `false`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
  - `page_needs()`: the queried post's own content is checked with this request's registrations (`live`, `collect`) instead of the strict check.
  - `learn_front()`: saves `inert` (new `front_inert()`). A kind learned already adds this page's needs to its own instead of replacing them, except when an administrator asks to learn again. The `blocks` and `shortcodes` maps keep earlier learns' entries while the map is current, so a name any learn saw registered never becomes a leftover; `front_inert()` drops a name once it is registered, or once its block namespace has a registered block. Up to 200 of each.
- README (Public pages only, Unreleased) and changelog.

## Why

Found by the 1.3.3 survey for #226: on one site, the front page holds seven shortcodes from an old theme, none registered with every plugin loaded, so `front` was never learned. On another, posts with blocks left by a removed code block plugin loaded every plugin.

## Risk

A plugin that registers a shortcode only on some requests could have a name saved as a leftover when a learn ran where it was not registered. Then a page using it with that plugin skipped would show the shortcode as text. Limits:
- Only names in a learning page's own content qualify, and only if still unregistered after that page rendered with every plugin.
- Leftovers are saved per page kind (`kinds[kind]['inert']`) and count only on pages of that kind. So a plugin that registers a shortcode only for its own post type, or only on pages, still loads there; its type registration also keeps it on its own singles.
- Any learn that sees the name registered, now or earlier for the same plugin set, removes it. Plugin, content and setting changes start learning over.

What remains: a plugin that registers a shortcode only on some posts of one kind, not by type, and not on the post that learned the kind. Closing that needs one full learn per post, which is a per-address write that page learning avoids by design. The owner accepted this approach before implementation.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passed.
- Read-only probe (`wp eval-file` with plugins loaded, branch loader under another class name, nothing written):
  - Site with old theme shortcodes, front page: saved map → `false`; learning gate → `[]`; live learn → `[]` with leftovers `slideshow, button, clearfade, tabgroup, tab, one_third, one_third_last`; before plugins load with leftovers → `[]`. Controls: `[fluentform]` → `fluentform/fluentform.php`; `[no_such_sps497]` → `false`.
  - Site with leftover code block plugin blocks, a post: saved map → `false`; live learn → `kadence-blocks` with leftover block `kevinbatdorf/code-block-pro`; before plugins load with leftovers → `kadence-blocks` only.

Resolves #497
For #226

title: GH#507: fix: page learning: names a plugin registers only on some posts are not saved as leftovers
body:
## What

Closes the risk #497 left: a shortcode or block that a plugin registers only on some posts of a page kind was saved as a leftover (`inert`) when the kind was learned on another post. The plugin could then be skipped on the posts that use it, which showed the shortcode as plain text.

Before a name is saved as a leftover, the active plugins' own code is searched for code that registers it.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
  - `front_code_check()` (new): takes the names that would become leftovers (this learn's unregistered names plus every kind's saved leftovers, via the new `front_unknown()` split out of `front_inert()`) and looks them up in each active plugin's code. A name that one plugin registers becomes that plugin's in the `shortcodes`/`blocks` owner maps, so pages using it load it. A name that several plugins register becomes `false` (unknown), so those pages load every plugin. Names not looked up in every plugin are returned as unchecked and are not saved as leftovers; a later learn continues.
  - `front_code_names()` (new): reads one plugin's `.php`/`.inc` files and `block.json` (skipping `node_modules`, `.git`, `tests`, and files over 2 MB). Shortcodes: `FRONT_CODE_SHORTCODE` matches the first argument of a call whose name holds `shortcode` (`add_shortcode()`, `addShortcode()`, `$this->add_shortcode()`), the third argument of `shortcode_atts()`, and a `const`/`$property` named `*shortcode*` = `'name'`, each also through `apply_filters()`. In a file that calls `add_shortcode()` with a variable (WooCommerce's list, Stripe's), any quoted name counts. Blocks: the `"name"` in `block.json`, or the first argument of `register_block_type*()`.
  - Budget per learn: `FRONT_CODE_BUDGET` 3 s and `FRONT_CODE_FILES` 40,000 files.
  - `front_inert()` drops unchecked names. `front_option_changed()` ignores writes to the new option.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `FRONT_CODE` option `seoprostack_plugin_front_code`: per active plugin, the main file's mtime plus name → found, keeping the newest 500 names per plugin, not autoloaded. `FRONT_VERSION` 5 → 6, so sites learn again with the check.
- `uninstall.php` removes the option. README (Public pages only, Unreleased) and changelog.

## Why

#507: the remaining risk accepted in #501. The owner then asked to try closing it ("sure, try it, test on plugin-testing.local").

## Verification

On plugin-testing.local (63 active plugins, PHP 8.5):

- **End to end, the #507 case.** A throwaway plugin with no page hooks registers `[sps507_cond]` at `init` only for addresses of posts with a custom field. Post A (no field) and post B (field) are both `single:post` and both contain the shortcode. Learning on A, then visiting B as a visitor:
  - 1.3.5 (control): A saves `sps507_cond` as a leftover; on B the plugin is skipped (18 skipped) and `[sps507_cond]` shows as text. Reproduces the bug.
  - This branch: owner `sps507-cond/sps507-cond.php`, no leftover; on B 17 plugins are skipped, the test plugin loads, and `SPS507-RENDERED` shows. On hello-world it is still skipped.
  - A name whose lookup hit the time limit was left unchecked, not saved as a leftover, and the next learn finished it.
- **Recall over real registrations.** Every shortcode and block the active plugins register was looked up as if unseen:
  - Shortcodes: 107 of 114 correct owner, 3 shared ("several", load everything), 0 wrong, 4 missed (PayPal Payments builds names via `$instance->get_id()`).
  - Blocks: 244 of 262 correct, 0 wrong. The misses are SEO Pro Stack's own (never skipped) or WooCommerce/FluentCRM names whose namespace already counts as registered.
  - Mentioned-only names stay leftovers: `one_third`, `button`, `tabs`.
- **Cost:** a cold lookup of all 63 plugins takes 1.6–3.0 s, once per learned name per plugin version. Warm lookups take 0.00 s. The cache is 34 KB.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --posts 2000`: passed (WordPress 7.1.2, PHP 8.3, default and all 88 features, uninstall clean, no PHP messages).

## Risk

- A plugin that registers a name only on some posts *and* builds the name in code elsewhere (like PayPal's) is still not found. That is narrower than before.
- The first learn of a page with a new unregistered name takes up to about 3 s longer, once.

Resolves #507
For #226

title: GH#226: feat: Load plugins only where needed replaces Freesoul Deactivate Plugins
body:
## Summary

Load plugins only where needed now replaces Freesoul Deactivate Plugins (free and PRO). It does not import Freesoul's lists.

The aim is safe, automatic speed gains that nobody has to set up, not a copy of every Freesoul feature. The #226 survey covered 15 installs: SEO Pro Stack skipped 408 of Freesoul's 1,362 skips, and it skipped 360 that Freesoul never did. Freesoul's lists are chosen by hand, so they don't prove a plugin is unused, and its device, role, AJAX, REST and cron rules are risky to guess. SEO Pro Stack skips a plugin only after learning that a screen or page kind doesn't need it.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: adds `replaces` for `freesoul-deactivate-plugins` and `freesoul-deactivate-plugins-pro`. The Plugins screen now suggests deactivating and deleting them, and the card shows "Replaces: …". Also removes the hint "Freesoul Deactivate Plugins skips it on the site" and stops reading `eos_dp_frontend_everywhere` / `eos_dp_unlogged`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `start()` returns early while Freesoul is active on the site or for the network, because both plugins filter the plugin list. On multisite one must-use file serves every site, so this covers sites where the per-feature wait can't apply.
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: updates the comment on why Freesoul isn't listed.
- `README.md`: adds a Replaces table row, a "Replaces Freesoul…" bullet under the feature, the Credits row (no more "not a replacement yet"), an Unreleased entry, and the count from `php scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write` (now 56 plugins).
- `changelog.txt`: adds an Unreleased entry.

`readme.txt` is unchanged. It has 51 bytes left and doesn't list replaced plugins one by one.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors. "README.md says 56 replaced plugins, as the code does". The 3 warnings are release-only (Unreleased section, slug note, existing tag).
- Disposable WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3 runtime check with the built zip:
  - Without Freesoul: SEO Pro Stack's must-use file is present.
  - Freesoul activated from the Plugins screen (its activation code fails under WP-CLI because it needs wp-admin, so the check doesn't use WP-CLI for this): the must-use file is removed and `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::enabled()` returns `false`. The Plugins screen row note says "SEO Pro Stack makes this plugin redundant: ‘Load plugins only where needed’ is on and takes over once you deactivate this plugin. Then you can delete it." Visitor pages return 200.
  - After deactivating Freesoul: the must-use file is back, `enabled()` returns `true`, and debug.log has no PHP messages (the canary notice arrived).

## Related

- #514: moves secondary plugin-loading settings into a closed Troubleshooting section.
- #515 / PR #516: a general rule for wp-admin view writes. Both PRs add to the Unreleased sections of `README.md` and `changelog.txt`, so whichever merges second may need a rebase.

Resolves #226

title: GH#521: fix: a deleted plugin still listed as active no longer makes features wait
body:
## What

A plugin deleted while still active stays listed in `active_plugins` / `active_sitewide_plugins` until someone opens the Plugins screen, but WordPress never loads it (`wp_get_active_and_valid_plugins()`). SEO Pro Stack now counts only listed plugins that WordPress would load (a valid path to a file that exists):

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` `start()`: the Freesoul Deactivate Plugins wait (ac127da) ignores entries whose files are gone. The loader runs from the must-use file before the plugin's classes load, so it checks inline.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php`: new `plugin_installed()`; `active_plugins()` (behind `replaced_active()` and the other "is X active" checks) leaves missing files out.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` `fdp_in_use()`: only installed Freesoul files count, so its must-use file is removed when only stale entries are left.

`stored_active_plugins()` is unchanged: the learned maps' fingerprints use the list as stored.

## Why

After the 1.3.7 deployment, the #226 survey showed one network subsite (site M) dropping from 70 skips to none. Its `active_plugins` still lists `freesoul-deactivate-plugins-pro/…`, whose files no install has, so the loader waited there for good and nothing was learned after the update cleared the map.

## Verification

- `php -l` and `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the three files: clean.
- On the affected subsite, read only, with the same expressions: the stale entry made the old check wait (`yes`) and makes the new check not wait (`no`).
- After the next release: an anonymous visit there learns the site, and the #226 survey shows site M skipping again.

Resolves #521

title: GH#524: fix: Hosting needs: no false lost-test-value warning for LiteSpeed Cache's object cache
body:
Resolves #524

## What changes

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` → `object_cache_facts()`:

- LiteSpeed Cache's own drop-in (`LSCWP_OBJECT_CACHE`) no longer gets the cross-request test value. It falls back to the database only when it cannot connect, and `cache_server()` already checks that against its configured host and port. Its Purge All (`Purge::_purge_all()` → `_purge_all_object()`), on every plugin update by default, empties the object cache, and shared Memcached evicts values nobody reads, so a day-old test value was lost while the cache worked.
- New `recheck_cache()`: besides the existing check for an extension the host has since turned on, it checks once more right away when the stored result is a lost test value for LiteSpeed Cache with its drop-in loaded. Sites showing the false warning clear it on the next admin screen. The new result never has that cause, so the recheck runs once. Another drop-in in LiteSpeed Cache's place is still tested daily.
- README → Object cache health and changelog (Unreleased) updated.

## Evidence (live Hostinger site, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, Memcached at `[::1]:11211`)

- `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` true, `LSCWP_OBJECT_CACHE` defined, Memcached answers; stored facts: `state => unreachable, cause => probe, name => LiteSpeed Cache`.
- Memcached stats: 1 GB limit, 92% used, `cmd_flush` 544,332, so the server is shared and often flushed.
- `litespeed.conf.purge-upgrade` = 1, so Purge All runs on plugin updates (77 plugins).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- After deploy: open Plugins on the site; the object cache warning is gone, and `wp option get seoprostack_hosting_object_cache` shows `state => working` with no `probe` key.

title: GH#528: fix: Hosting needs: an object cache turned on or off is checked again at once, not the next day
body:
Resolves #528

Stacked on #525 (GH#524): it extends `recheck_cache()`, which #525 adds. Merge #525 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What changed

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` → `recheck_cache()`: a stored daily result is checked again before the day is out when it disagrees with `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` now: stored `off` (or LiteSpeed Cache's `dropin` cause) while a cache is in use, or stored `working` while none is. The new result cannot disagree the same way, so each recheck runs once. It still runs only from the admin, cron or WP-CLI.
- README.md (Object cache health) and changelog.txt (Unreleased).

## Why

On a Hostinger site the daily check ran 27 seconds before LiteSpeed Cache wrote `object-cache.php`. Hosting needs then said "Memcached is available on this server but the site is not using it" all day, although the cache worked.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS and PHPStan (`phpstan.neon.dist`) on the changed file: no errors.
- On that site (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, Memcached), with WP-CLI loading this file in place of the installed one (`--skip-plugins=seoprostack`; the site's plugin files were not changed):
  - stored `off`, cache in use → `working`, new `checked`; called again → same `checked` (no repeat)
  - stored `working`, cache in use → kept, old `checked`
  - stored `dropin`, cache in use → `working`, new `checked`
- Control with the installed 1.3.7: stored `off` stays `off`.

title: GH#530: fix: Hosting needs: PHP workers from average time; no false LiteSpeed object cache warning (GH#524)
body:
Resolves #530
Resolves #524

Includes #525 (LiteSpeed Cache object cache false warning, GH#524), merged in here with `main` so both land in one merge; #525 is closed in favour of this PR.

## GH#530: PHP workers from the average time per request

- `SEOProStack_Hosting_Needs::traffic()` also returns `avg` (every sampled request) and `site_avg` (visitor pages, once 30 are sampled).
- `assess()`: Little's law now uses the average time per request instead of the p95 page time, which was rounded up to the top of its timing slot. The busiest hour (×3) and its bursts (×3) already allow for peaks.
  - **Now** uses the average of every sampled request, because the busiest-hour count includes admin screens, the REST API and cron, and they hold workers too.
  - Low, medium and high use the average visitor page time (GH#66 rule).
- `SEOProStack_Hosting_Plans::plans()` takes the Now time as an optional `now_seconds`.
- The traffic line shows both averages and keeps the 95% page time as information.

Live Hostinger site, 1,682 samples, `plan()` run read-only with the site's numbers: Now goes from 7 workers / 8 GB / 8 cores (busy 5.87, 4.00 s p95) to 4 workers / 8 GB / 4 cores (busy 2.96, 2.02 s average).

## GH#524: no false lost-test-value warning for LiteSpeed Cache's object cache

- `object_cache_facts()` skips the cross-request test value when LiteSpeed Cache's own drop-in is loaded (`LSCWP_OBJECT_CACHE`). Its Purge All (on every plugin update by default) empties the object cache, and shared Memcached evicts unread values, so the value was lost while the cache worked. Its server is still asked directly (`cache_server()`).
- New `recheck_cache()`: a stored lost-value result for LiteSpeed Cache is checked again on the next admin screen (once).

Live evidence: `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` true, Memcached answers at `[::1]:11211`, stored `cause => probe`; Memcached 1 GB, 92% used, `cmd_flush` 544,332.

title: GH#537: fix: Hosting needs: object cache checked only on web requests, not WP-CLI or command-line cron
body:
## Summary

Hosting needs' daily object cache check now runs only on web requests (admin screens, Site Health, cron started over HTTP). WP-CLI and cron run from the command line return the stored result.

On Hostinger, `/usr/bin/php` (WP-CLI and hPanel cron jobs) is the account's PHP (8.5), not the site's. A site whose pages ran PHP 8.1 without `memcached` had no object cache for visitors, but its per-minute command-line cron ran PHP 8.5 with `memcached`, so the stored result could say `working`.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` → `object_cache_facts()`: guard on `'' === self::live_sapi()` (the helper How PHP runs already uses, #517) instead of allowing `wp_doing_cron()` / `WP_CLI` from the command line. Docblock says why.
- README.md → Object cache health and Unreleased; changelog.txt → Unreleased.

## Interaction with open PRs

PR #529 (GH#528) rechecks when the stored state disagrees with `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` in this request. Without this guard, a command-line cron on a different PHP would flip the result each time it disagreed with the web. With it, the comparison happens only on web requests. #529's verification step (`wp eval ... facts()`) then returns the stored result; verify from an admin screen instead.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs -q` (clean) and `composer phpstan` on the file: no errors.
- Live evidence (Hostinger, 14 sites): a temporary web PHP file showed 13 sites using Memcached and one (PHP 8.1) with `memcached` not loaded and `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` false, while WP-CLI reported all 14 working. After enabling `memcached` for PHP 8.1 on the account, the web check showed the cache in use and sharing values with WP-CLI.

Resolves #537

title: GH#565: feat: Dark mode image contrast for transparent logos and icons (release 1.3.14)
body:
## What

New feature, off by default (Media tab): **Dark mode image contrast**. In Kadence Pro's dark mode (`body.color-switch-dark`), transparent logos, icons and drawings that would be hard to see on the background really behind them are recoloured with a CSS filter. Photos, images without transparency, images with a clear part already showing, banners/badges that carry their own contrast and images with their own filter are left alone. Class `seoprostack-keep-colours` opts an image (or block) out.

Resolves #565

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-dark-image-contrast.php`: bool setting; a last-priority `body_class` filter notes whether the theme draws `color-switch-*`; `wp_footer` (priority 5) enqueues the script only then. Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`.
- `assets/dark-image-contrast.js` (no dependencies, ~6.4 KB gzipped):
  - Samples each image near the window (IntersectionObserver; again on `load` for lazy loaders/`srcset`), after `img.decode()`, at most 128×128 px. Candidates: ≥5% transparent pixels and flat colours (top 12 colour buckets ≥80%). Only visible pixels count, so transparent margins in the file do not skew it.
  - **Background, padding included**: starts at the image itself (its own background fills its padding), then each ancestor, compositing translucent colours, near-uniform gradients and absolutely positioned overlays covering the image (Kadence row overlays, Cover backgrounds). Background pictures/video or unreadable colours → leave alone.
  - Allows for the theme's base dark image filter (Kadence Pro sets `img { filter: brightness(.9) contrast(1.2) }` under `.color-switch-dark`), read from a hidden probe image; any other filter on an image means hands off.
  - Changes only images with ≥60% of visible pixels under 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), and not mostly filled ones (<40% transparent) that already have ≥10% clear. Simulates `invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg)` (keeps hue), white, black; white/black are skipped for images with inner detail (strong edges between visible pixels ≥ ¼ of edges against transparency). Prefers the first leaving ≤20% under 3:1, and only if it improves by ≥25 points.
  - Marks with `data-seoprostack-dark`; CSS scoped to `body.color-switch-dark`, so switching to light restores instantly. Re-evaluates 400 ms after a switch (colour transitions).
- Docs: `README.md` (feature section, Unreleased), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (one short line, one Site Health line shortened to stay under 10 KB: 10,235 bytes).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan).
- Shared preview site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`, this PR included), Kadence theme with the dark mode switcher simulated as `STANDARDS.md` → Testing step 5 says (plus Kadence Pro's image filter), feature on, 11 cases, Chromium and WebKit identical, no page errors:

  - Left alone: inside a padded white card; image with its own white background and padding; dark row under a 90% white overlay; over a background picture; `seoprostack-keep-colours`; `.jpg`; red/navy banner with white text.
  - Switching to light: filter `none` on every marked image; back to dark: same marks.
  - Script printed only when the body has a colour switch class (absent on the normal front page).
- Script injected into a live Kadence Pro site in dark mode (Playwright): home page 4 logos changed (Sodexo → light blue, white Samsung logo on a light green box → black, grey script logo ×2 → light grey), book montage and banner left alone; partners page 11 logos changed, all clearer in before/after screenshots, a stroked logo with text in a box (ScoreApp) left alone. WebKit matches except two borderline logos (52–57% low there vs 63–66% in Chromium), which it leaves as they are.

body: ## What Dark mode image contrast: new sub-setting **Keep watermarks subtle** (on by default). Logos and drawings shown faintly on purpose (under 75% opacity) stay faint in Kadence's dark mode. A white watermark that would stand out on a dark page is made fainter; one that would vanish is inverted (hue kept), then made faint. `seoprostack-keep-colours` opts one out. New plugin presets for **Readabler** and **AI Engine** (free, and Pro through `also`). The settings come from the owner's live set-up on a client site, read over SSH without changing anything: Readabler's accessibility button bottom left and AI Engine's chatbot bubble bottom right, so the two don't overlap. - `records`: option name => the key that names each record. AI Engine keeps chatbots as a list, and lists were replaced whole, which would wipe a site's other chatbots. `pair()` keys the stored list by `botId` for `differences()`, `pick()` and `write()`. Only the preset's records that are stored are kept, so no record is ever added. `unpair()` puts the merged records back in their stored order. Undo still restores the whole stored list. - `also`: folder => name, so one file serves `ai-engine-pro`. A file of the same folder takes precedence. This is the pattern `SEOProStack_WP_Optimize::premium_preset()` uses, without the extra class.

title: GH#585: fix: correct stale comment counts when comments are deleted
body:
## Summary

Posts kept showing comment counts after their spam was deleted. WordPress recounts a post only when an *approved* comment is deleted, so a stored `comment_count` that was already wrong stayed wrong. On the live site, 119 posts had counts with no approved comments left.

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php` (Count terms and comments in the background):

- `comment_deleted()` on `deleted_comment`: for a deleted comment that was not approved, check its post once per request (the same indexed `COUNT(*)` core runs) and call `wp_update_comment_count()` only when the stored count is wrong. Posts whose count is right are not recounted, so their caches are not purged.
- **Recount now** first calls `repair_comment_counts()`: finds posts of types with comment support whose count does not match their approved comments (too high, or 0 with approved comments; up to 5,000), queues them, then runs the batch. Types without comment support are left alone (an anti-malware plugin keeps its own number in `comment_count` on its quarantine posts).
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).

## Evidence

- Root cause: comment moderation is on, so the deleted comments were not approved and WordPress did not recount. The deferred-count queue works: queueing post 8963 (count 41, no comments) and running `seoprostack_deferred_counts` set it to 0. The first mass deletion was before this feature existed.
- Repair query on the live site: 119 posts found in 7 ms; the quarantine post (count 62,121) not included; no order or product mismatches.
- `scripts/lint.sh phpcs` and `phpstan`: pass.

Resolves #585

title: GH#588: feat: LiteSpeed Cache preset sets up the crawler to prime the cache after purges
body:
## What

The LiteSpeed Cache preset now turns on LiteSpeed Cache's crawler where the server allows it and the site has a sitemap. After a purge (every plugin, theme or core update purges the cache, as the preset sets), the crawler puts pages back in the page cache, so visitors mostly get cached pages.

## Why

On a live Hostinger site the crawler was on but crawled the whole sitemap only every 3.5 days (LiteSpeed Cache's default Crawl Interval is 302400 s), so pages purged by updates stayed uncached for days. LiteSpeed answers the crawler with HTTP 201 and no body for pages it still holds, so a daily crawl of a warm site costs little. Hostinger also caps the crawler's load itself (`CRAWLER_LOAD_LIMIT_ENFORCE=25`). The preset's notes also said the crawler needs QUIC.cloud, but in LiteSpeed Cache 7.x it does not.

## How

- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`: `crawler` on, `crawler-crawl_interval` 86400 and `crawler-sitemap`, under `when: ["single_site", "litespeed_crawler"]`. Defaults: off, 302400 and empty. Notes and `settings` labels updated.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`:
  - New `litespeed_crawler` condition: a LiteSpeed server, the crawler allowed (the same check as LiteSpeed Cache's `Router::can_crawl()`, from `X-LSCACHE`), and a known sitemap.
  - `crawler_sitemap()` keeps the sitemap already set in LiteSpeed Cache. When none is set, it uses Rank Math's sitemap index if that module is on, then Yoast's, then WordPress's own (`get_sitemap_url('index')`), then the `seoprostack_crawler_sitemap` filter.
  - The `seoprostack_plugin_presets` filter fills the sitemap value for each site.
- Saves still go through `\LiteSpeed\Conf::update_confs()`, which also adds or removes the `litespeed_task_crawler` cron.
- Server IP stays out of the preset. Each site has its own, and a wrong one stops the crawler.
- Docs: README (presets table, LiteSpeed hosting, conditions), `docs/presets.md` owner decision, and changelog lines.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs and phpstan all pass. `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` passes.
- Throwaway Docker site (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, this branch):
  - Not a LiteSpeed server: no crawler settings in `presets diff`.
  - LiteSpeed server (`seoprostack_litespeed_server=enterprise`): `diff` lists Crawler `''→1`, Crawl Interval `302400→86400` and Custom Sitemap `''→<site>/?sitemap=index`. `apply` stores them and adds the `litespeed_task_crawler` cron.
  - `reset`: crawler off, interval 302400, sitemap empty, cron removed. `undo` puts them back.
  - A sitemap already set in LiteSpeed Cache is left unchanged.
  - No sitemap (WordPress sitemaps off, no SEO plugin): the crawler settings are left alone.
- Live (augustawards.com, Rank Math): `crawler_sitemap()`'s Rank Math branch gives `https://www.augustawards.com/sitemap_index.xml`, the sitemap already set there.

Resolves #588

title: GH#590: fix: LiteSpeed Cache crawler turns end before the host's 300-second request limit
body:
## Summary

**Fixes for other plugins** (on by default) now defines LiteSpeed Cache's `LITESPEED_CRAWLER_DURATION` as 240 seconds, unless the site already defines it. Each crawler turn then ends before LiteSpeed hosts such as Hostinger stop the request at 300 seconds.

Resolves #590

## Why

LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 plans 900-second turns and raises `max_execution_time` to 915. Hostinger's LiteSpeed server still ends PHP at 300 seconds: a probe straight to the origin got HTTP 503 at 301 s. The killed turn leaves `wp-content/litespeed/crawler/meta.data.pid`, which `Crawler::_check_valid_lane()` ignores only once it is an hour old, so the crawler worked about 5 minutes per hour. Live evidence is in #590.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: `litespeed_crawler_duration()` runs in `boot()` (`init`, priority 0). That is before LiteSpeed Cache's role simulation (`init` priority 5, which uses the duration as its cookie lifetime) and before any crawl starts. It skips when LiteSpeed Cache is not loaded (`LSCWP_V`) or the constant is already defined. The `seoprostack_litespeed_crawler_duration` filter changes the value; 0 leaves LiteSpeed Cache's own 900.
- Docblock, setting description, README (Fixes for other plugins; LiteSpeed hosting → the crawler; Unreleased), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`: passed.
- Throwaway site, WordPress latest + LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, `get_crawler_duration()`:
  - LiteSpeed Cache alone: 900
  - SEO Pro Stack, fix on: 240
  - filter returns 0: 900
  - fix off: 900
  - site defines 120 in `wp-config.php`: 120
  - No PHP messages from either plugin in `debug.log`.
- Live (augustawards.com, Hostinger): stale lane released, constant set in `wp-config.php` (backed up first). The next turn started at 01:50:08 and ended cleanly at 01:51:09 (`end_reason: end`, `is_running: 0`, no lane file left). The mobile crawler completed its list, and the desktop crawler took over.

title: GH#592: feat: Hosting needs checks LiteSpeed Cache's crawler and fixes what stops it
body:
## Summary

Hosting needs now shows LiteSpeed Cache's crawler on LiteSpeed servers, in the Plugins-screen row and as a Site Health test. It shows the last full crawl, the next one or where the current one is, with **Crawl now** and a link to the Crawler screen. It also finds what stops the crawler, each with a one-click fix through LiteSpeed Cache's own code:

- **A stopped turn**: the lane file is older than a turn + 5 minutes, and LiteSpeed Cache waits an hour. **Carry on now** calls `Release_lane()` and starts a turn.
- **Pages that failed** (`B` in the blocklist): **Try them again** runs `blacklist_del()`. Pages that can't be cached (`N`) stay.
- **Server IP is empty** while the host name resolves elsewhere (a CDN): **Use [address]** saves `SERVER_ADDR` through `Conf::update_confs()`, but only after a test request with `CURLOPT_RESOLVE` reaches LiteSpeed without Cloudflare's `cf-ray` header. It is not offered when LiteSpeed Cache is active for the network.
- **A crawl in progress with no turn for an hour**: the text points at WP-Cron or the server's cron job.

The fixes run through `admin-post.php`, each with its own nonce, for `manage_options`. Results show as a one-time notice. Nothing is stored. The Hosting needs row now takes a list of links per line. PHPStan ignores the `LiteSpeed\` classes the same way it already does for the other plugins it doesn't install.

Resolves #592

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan). `bash scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`: passed.
- Throwaway Docker site with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1. A mu-plugin set `SERVER_SOFTWARE=LiteSpeed` and a public `SERVER_ADDR`. I seeded a crawl at page 412 of 1,017, a 40-minute-old lane file and blocklist rows B, B, N. Then, over real admin requests:

title: GH#596: fix: crawler status after Crawl now, and Crawl now after a Purge All
body:
## Summary

Live testing of 1.3.19 on augustawards.com found two gaps in the new crawler check.

- **Status right after Crawl now.** After a finished crawl, LiteSpeed Cache's first manual turn runs `Crawler_Map::gen()`. That writes its `.reset` file (`crawler-map.cls.php:616`), and the same turn stops on it (`crawler.cls.php:917-929`: `end_reason=stopped_reset`, `this_full_beginning_time=0`). But WP-Cron's turns abort with "cache warmed already" before reading it, until the crawl interval has passed. So pages purged by an update were cached again only as visitors opened them, for up to a day.
  - Hosting needs now recommends **Crawl now** (row and Site Health) when the reset file is newer than the last full crawl's end and the next crawl is over an hour away.

title: GH#604: fix: dbDelta() no longer alters unchanged enum columns with capitals on every call
body:
## Summary

Since WordPress 6.9 (checked in 7.1.3 and `trunk`), `dbDelta()` compares a table's column type with a lower-case copy of the type in the plugin's `CREATE TABLE` statement (`$tablefield->Type !== $fieldtype_lowercased`; 6.8 compared `$fieldtype`). An `enum` or `set` column whose choices have capitals therefore always looks changed and is altered on every call.

Tutor LMS Pro 4.1.0 calls `dbDelta()` for `{prefix}tutor_notifications` on every request. A live admin profile showed `ALTER TABLE wp_tutor_notifications CHANGE COLUMN `status` `status` enum('READ','UNREAD')` on every admin screen and admin-ajax request, at 40–116 ms each.

**Fixes for other plugins** now uses `dbdelta_create_queries`, next to the existing Tutor LMS fix (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, `dbdelta_same_choices()`). For a table that exists, it leaves out of the statement any `enum`/`set` line with capitals that the table already has exactly: the same type byte for byte, the same `NULL`/`NOT NULL`, nothing else set, and a comma at the end. `dbDelta()` leaves columns a statement does not list as they are. Real changes are still applied, and new tables are created as written. The cost is one `DESCRIBE` of the table, only when the statement has such a column.

Docs: class header, setting description, README.md (Fixes for other plugins), changelog.txt, readme.txt.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Throwaway WordPress 7.1.3 site, table with `` `status` enum('READ','UNREAD') `` and `kind set('A','B') NOT NULL`:
  - same statement, twice: 0 ALTER each
  - new choice `'ARCHIVED'`: 1 ALTER, column updated
  - same statement again: 0 ALTER
  - new table: created, 0 ALTER
  - same statement with the fix's filter removed: 2 ALTERs (`status` and `kind`), as WordPress does now
  - no debug log entries
- Live verification follows the release (the admin profile should no longer show the `ALTER TABLE`).

Resolves #604

title: GH#610: feat: Site Health lists tables that cannot store emoji; Database character set converts them to utf8mb4 on request
body:
## Summary

A site moved from an older database keeps tables in the older utf8 (utf8mb3) character set: WordPress converts its tables only in the 4.2 upgrade. Saving an option, custom field or comment with an emoji to one of them fails without a message. On a live site this blocked Kadence's catalog refresh (its saved data contains 🎉) until 15 tables were converted by hand.

New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-charset.php` (registered in `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`):

- **Site Health test, always on** (it only advises; async, so it runs after the page loads): lists up to 20 of this site's tables that cannot store 4-byte characters, with collation and size, and how many more there are. It links to the setting or the Tools page.
- **Database character set** setting (Server tab, off): Tools → Database character set converts one table, or all up to 512 MB at once, with `ALTER TABLE … CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4` in the collation WordPress uses for new tables (`$wpdb->collate`), so converted tables do not add "Illegal mix of collations" errors (#550). Tables over 512 MB are refused on the web (checked under the lock, so a hand-made request cannot bypass it) and left to WP-CLI.
- **Safety**: tables in other character sets (latin1 and so on) are listed, never converted, as their text may be stored in the wrong character set. Each conversion re-reads the table first, takes an advisory lock (one at a time, not waited for), and sets `lock_wait_timeout` to 15 s so it never queues behind a busy table (and so never makes other queries queue behind it). Each one is logged in `seoprostack_database_charset_log` (not autoloaded, removed in `uninstall.php` by its literal name, as the class is not loaded there). Administrators only; super admins on multisite; nonce-checked.
- **Detection** uses `SHOW TABLE STATUS` and `SHOW FULL COLUMNS` for each table with the site's prefix. That includes tables whose default is utf8mb4 but whose columns are not. On the live shared host a query of `information_schema.COLUMNS` timed out.
- **WP-CLI**: `wp seoprostack charset list`, `convert <table>…`, `convert --all`; on a failure it reports how many tables were converted before it.

Changelog entries are in README.md, changelog.txt and readme.txt.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, phpcs, phpstan, js, shell, workflows).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --posts 2000` (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3): passed, including uninstall (no tables, options or cron left, no PHP messages). The first CI run caught a fatal error in `uninstall.php`, fixed in 1bafb02.
- Throwaway WordPress on MariaDB 11.4 (PHP 8.3), with `wp_options`, `wp_postmeta` and `wp_comments` turned to `utf8mb3_general_ci`, plus four test tables: a latin1 table with text, a latin1 table with no text, a plugin table in `utf8mb4_general_ci`, and a plugin table with a utf8mb4 default but a utf8mb3 column:
  - Survey and Site Health: 5 tables listed (the 3 core ones and the mixed table convertible; the latin1 one with text not). The no-text latin1 table and the other utf8mb4 table were ignored. Saving an emoji option failed, as on the live site.
  - Setting off: Tools page not offered; `convert` refused.

title: GH#616: fix: the update check after a plugin update loads every plugin with Load plugins only where needed
body:
## Summary

With **Load plugins only where needed**, the update check that follows a plugin update now loads every plugin again.

`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::update_check_due()` loads every plugin on an admin screen when a check is due, but at most once an hour (#535). Updating a plugin deletes WordPress's saved plugin check, so a new check is due straight away. Within that hour it ran on a screen that skips plugins. Paid plugins that remove WordPress.org offers for their own names were missing from that check, so it kept those offers. Correct update counts then counted them, because their installed versions equal the checked ones. The Updates screen checks again with every plugin and listed none.

Change (`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`):

- `update_checks_due()`: the due test, split out of `update_check_due()`.
- `updates_checked()` runs on `admin_init` at `PHP_INT_MAX`, after core's `_maybe_update_*` checks, on a request that loaded every plugin for updates. If no check is due any more, the checks ran here, so it removes `seoprostack_plugin_updates_full` and the next due check also loads every plugin. If one is still due, the checks do not run here (updates switched off) and the hourly limit stays.

The loader still only loads more plugins. Update checks and the saved update data are untouched (`STANDARDS.md` → Code rules).

## Evidence (live site, WP-CLI)

- Timeline: full load for updates at 15:58; the SEO Pro Stack 1.3.23 update at 16:04 deleted the plugin check; the admin bar later showed 3 updates on Pages while Updates listed none.
- Forced check with every plugin: 0 offers. The same check with only the plugins Pages loads: WooCommerce GoCardless 3.0.3 (WordPress.org) and WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.3.0.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpcs includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: clean
- `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: no errors
- `php -l`: no syntax errors

Resolves #616

title: GH#619: feat: Hosting needs recommends LiteSpeed Cache's Cache WP-Admin while its object cache works
body:
## Summary

Hosting needs recommends LiteSpeed Cache's **Cache WP-Admin** (Cache → Object) while LiteSpeed Cache's object cache works, with a **Turn on Cache WP-Admin** link for administrators (network administrators when LiteSpeed Cache is network-active).

Resolves #619

## Why

With it off, LiteSpeed Cache's object cache reads only transients on admin screens (`_can_cache()` in its `src/object-cache.cls.php`, 7.9.1) and asks the database for everything else. Admin screens still write and delete there, so the cache is as current as the database either way. A/B on a Hostinger site: Pages screen about 2.0 s off against 1.4 s on (noisy; dashboard changed little).

## Care with stale data

- Recommended only while the daily object cache check finds LiteSpeed Cache's cache working.
- The link re-checks the stored result, `wp_using_ext_object_cache()`, the PHP extension and the server, then saves only `object-admin` through LiteSpeed Cache's own code (`update_confs()`, or `network_update()` + `Activation::update_files()` when network-active), which rewrites `.litespeed_conf.dat`. That setting triggers no Purge All (`_conf_purge_all()` covers cache, ESI, debug and network-primary only).
- The text says to Purge All after changing the database outside WordPress, and, with it on and the cache unreachable, to Purge All once it works again (deletes made meanwhile never reached it).
- SEO Pro Stack's own direct writes to core tables were audited: each clears its cached copy, or touches only rows with no cached parent.

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: `admin_cache()`, `save_admin_cache()`, shared private `save_object_settings()` now also used by `save_object_cache()` (behaviour unchanged).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: `ADMIN_CACHE` admin-post action, `admin_cache_advice()`, `turn_on_admin_cache()`, result notice in `fix_notice()`.
- `README.md` (Hosting needs), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs` on both files, `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: clean.
- Live, before this PR: 8 Hostinger sites had it off and were turned on with `wp litespeed-option set object-admin true` (the same `Admin_Settings` save path); on each, `.litespeed_conf.dat` has `"object-admin":true` and a value added, updated and deleted through the options API read the same from the object cache and the database. Home and login pages return 200.
- After release: on one site, turn it off, confirm the recommendation and link appear in Hosting needs, click it, confirm `wp litespeed-option get object-admin` returns 1 and the recommendation goes.

title: GH#621: login-time hooks no longer make a plugin load on every admin screen
body:
## What

Load plugins only where needed: the admin map's `always` list is now the loader's `ALWAYS_HOOKS` plus a new `ADMIN_ALWAYS_HOOKS` (`determine_current_user`, `session_token_manager`, `logout_url`), instead of also every front-end login hook (`FRONT_ALWAYS_HOOKS`, `FRONT_LOGIN_HOOKS`). Plugins that only check logins, registrations or lost passwords, or set login cookies, now load on the admin screens that use them rather than on every one.

## Why it is safe

Admin screens that skip plugins are only GET/HEAD views by someone already logged in (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::filterable_request()` / `view_request()`). Login checks, registration, lost passwords and `wp_set_auth_cookie()` never run there; wp-login.php, saves, AJAX, REST, XML-RPC and cron load every plugin. Permission hooks (`PERMISSION_HOOKS`) still keep their plugins on every admin screen. The front-end map builds its own `always` list (`front_hook_kind()`) and is unchanged.

`MAP_VERSION` 10 → 11 so every admin screen learns again: screens learned while these plugins always loaded do not list them where they are used.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `ADMIN_ALWAYS_HOOKS`, `sensitive_plugins()`, plugin list label.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `MAP_VERSION`.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpcs` on both PHP files and `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: no findings.
- After deploy (one Hostinger site, 51 plugins): the admin map's `always` list no longer holds Tutor LMS Pro, Really Simple Security Pro, FluentCRM, Simple Cloudflare Turnstile or Secure Custom Fields; profile screens still show 2FA fields; logging in with 2FA/CAPTCHA works; no new debug log messages from those plugins.

title: GH#631: feat: admin screens answer a click at once; SEO Pro Stack screens drawn whole; release 1.3.28
body:
## Summary

With Load pages before the click → **Also in the admin** on, clicking a link to another admin screen responds immediately: the admin menu marks the new screen, and the content area shows its title followed by dots that appear one by one, on WordPress's usual background and layout, until the page arrives. A link in the screen's own navigation (tab bars, a `nav` element, the All | Published views) keeps that navigation in view, marks the clicked entry and shows the dots below it.

Pages still load as normal, so screens and plugins work as before; only what shows while waiting changes. Measured on a live site (50 plugins): warm admin screens take 0.65–3.8 s on the server and 0.1–0.5 s in the browser, so the wait after a click is almost all server time with nothing on screen changing.

No fade between screens: WordPress 7.0's cross-document fade is what **No fade between admin screens** (on by default) turns off, and its `@view-transition { navigation: none; }` wins anyway. An earlier commit here added one; it was removed.

## How

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-preload-pages.php`:

- `admin_navigation_style()`: inline style on `wp-admin`.
  - Title and dots in core's own `.wrap h1` sizes and font, on the element itself, so the leaving screen's styles cannot move it; padding rather than margin above it, as a margin passed up through screens that unfloat `#wpbody-content` (Fluent Boards) and moved the whole page, menu included, down 10 px. Dots animate only without reduced motion.
  - While the placeholder shows (`sps-nav-shell` on `<html>`): core's background (`#f0f0f1`; 11 of 29 top-level screens on the preview site colour their own), core's `#wpcontent` padding (WooCommerce, Fluent Forms, Lasso and Revive set it to 0, so the next screen's content jumped 20 px right), and plugin bars outside the content area hidden. `#wpbody` is left alone so phones keep core's space under the admin bar.
  - From the click (`sps-nav-busy`): menu entries and links that are not current lose backgrounds a screen gave them. Fluent Boards' `.toplevel_page_fluent-boards { background: … }` is meant for its `<body>` but WordPress gives the menu entry and link the same class, so the entry turned white once it stopped being current.
- `print_admin_navigation()`: inline script. A plain left click on a same-site admin link (not new-tab, download or export links, admin-ajax.php, admin-post.php or async-upload.php, or the same screen) is remembered, and its `beforeunload` listener is re-added on each click so it runs after the page's own handlers. On `beforeunload`, if no handler asked to confirm leaving (unsaved changes), the menu entry is marked current; then after 100 ms either:
  - another screen: title and dots replace the content area, or
  - a link inside `.nav-tab-wrapper, nav, [role="tablist"], .subsubsub` in the content area: its `nav-tab-active` / `is-active` / `active` / `current` / `selected` classes and `aria-current` move to the clicked entry at once, everything after the navigation's block (the child of its `.wrap`) is hidden, and the dots show under its first entry, the first dot where that entry's text starts (its link padding left out), which is where SEO Pro Stack's tab content starts too. This covers every plugin made from the starter (SEO Pro Stats' Settings tabs disappeared before), core's tab screens and other plugins' tab bars, without a change to the starter.
  - The screen is put back on a key or pointer press (Esc stops the load), on `pageshow` from the back-forward cache, and after 30 seconds.
- Not on screens inside frames (`IFRAME_REQUEST`).
- `print_menu_icon_colours()` (`admin_head`) and `print_menu_icons_done()` (`adminmenu`): core colours the menu's SVG icons only once the page has loaded (svg-painter), so every screen change showed grey icons first. A `MutationObserver` now colours each icon from `window._wpColorScheme` as the menu is parsed, before the first frame; hover and current colours still come from core.

`includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` → `print_whole_screen()` (SEO Pro Stack's own screens): SEO Pro Stack's settings screen is about 700 KB, and Chrome drew it once the admin menu was read, before the admin bar, header and tabs, so a tab change showed the menu alone for a frame. `<link rel="expect" href="#wpfooter" blocking="render">` holds the first frame until the footer is parsed (Chrome and Edge 124+), so the previous screen (with the placeholder) stays until the new one is drawn whole.

- Chromium drops pending `rel=expect` targets whenever HTML is fragment-parsed into the document before they are found (`createContextualFragment`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `innerHTML` that leaves the fast path), warning "Did not find element expected to be parsed". jQuery's load-time feature tests do so in the head, so the link is printed last in `admin_head` (`PHP_INT_MAX`).
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`: the flyout titles were set with `innerHTML` while the page was read; they are now parsed with `DOMParser` and moved in, same markup.

README (feature and changelog) and changelog.txt updated. Release 1.3.28: version in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt` (Stable tag, short changelog), `README.md` and `changelog.txt`.

Resolves #631

## Verify

On the preview site (plugin-testing.local, WordPress 7.1.3, 64 plugins), Chromium 153 via Playwright; the next page's response held for 3 s and the leaving page measured 600 ms after the click:

| From → to | While waiting |
|---|---|
| Fluent Boards → Comments | "Comments . . ." at 228,42, where the Comments heading lands; menu stays at y 44 (was 54); background `#f0f0f1` (was Fluent's `#f3f5fa`); Fluent Boards entry no longer white |
| WooCommerce Products → Comments | content starts at 226 px (was 206 px, so no 20 px jump right) |
| SEO Pro Stats Shared reports → Read Me | header and tabs stay, Read Me marked current, 7 blocks below hidden, dots under the tabs |
| Posts All → Published | Published marked current, list hidden, dots under the views |
| Users → Add User at 390 px | "Add User . . ." below the admin bar |

Earlier, recorded inside the page: menu marked 1–4 ms after the click, placeholder at about 103 ms; Pages 1.2–1.7 s, Tutor LMS 0.8–1.1 s, Users 0.8–1.8 s, Plugins 5.1–6.4 s to load. The old page keeps drawing frames while waiting.

- Esc while waiting restores menu and tab classes, `aria-current`, hidden blocks, `<html>` classes and `aria-busy` exactly (Fluent Boards, SEO Pro Stats tabs, Posts views); no page errors.
- A page that asks to confirm leaving: the prompt appears and staying leaves the screen unchanged.
- No placeholder left on any loaded screen; no PHP messages from SEO Pro Stack in the debug log.
- Menu icons, frames sampled while loading at 4–6× CPU throttling: 0 frames with an unpainted icon on Comments, Fluent Boards, Plugins and SEO Pro Stack; the first painted frame is during `loading`. Hover still turns icons to the focus colour.
- SEO Pro Stack tabs (Settings → Content → Server, Content → Free Plugins): 0 frames drawn before the footer (was 1, showing only the menu); screencast shows header, tabs and dots held until the new tab appears whole (about 1.0 s). No `rel=expect` console warning on the Content, Free Plugins or Read Me tabs. Flyouts: 166 entries, update-count markup intact.
- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan) passes.

title: GH#633: perf: halve SEO Pro Stack cost on the Plugins screen; GH#634 docs; release 1.3.29
body:
## Summary

Cuts SEO Pro Stack's own cost on the Plugins screen roughly in half, fixes the WP-CLI command in the docs for clearing the update check, and prepares 1.3.29.

Measured on a live site with 76 installed plugins (about 50 active), warm OPcache, fastest of 3 runs, temporary per-callback profiler; the changed files were swapped in for the measurement and the originals restored afterwards (hashes checked).

| SEO Pro Stack on `plugins.php` | 1.3.28 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Time | 379 ms | 179 ms |
| Queries | 111 | 57 |
| Size column (`render_column`) | 135 ms | 36–44 ms |
| Menu copy (`capture_menu`) | 71 ms | 15–23 ms |
| Whole screen, queries | 283 | 229 |

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php`: `missing()` keeps its result per plugin for the request. The Plugins screen asked twice per row (`action_links` through `missing_count()`, `row_meta` through `missing()`), so every `exists()` lookup ran twice (`wp_fc_tags` 54→27, `wp_fc_lists` 28→14, and so on). `add()`, `remove()`, their error paths and `save_added()` clear it.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-sizes.php`: `opcache()` first calls `opcache_get_status(false)` (microseconds) and reuses per-plugin totals from the `seoprostack_plugin_opcache` site transient while OPcache's state matches (start and restart times, cached script count, used and wasted memory, plugin folder). Otherwise it lists scripts as before (`opcache_get_status(true)`: 50–108 ms with 8,800 scripts) and stores the new totals. Any compile, recompile, invalidation or restart changes the state, so the figures stay current; on the live site the read dropped from 72–108 ms to 0.2 ms and re-read as soon as a new script was compiled.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `here_forms()` builds the current address's forms once per request instead of once for each of the ~300 menu entries `copy_item()` copies.
- `uninstall.php`: removes the new transient.
- Docs (#634): `wp transient delete update_plugins --network`. Checked with WP-CLI on a live single site: without `--network` the key "is not set"; with it the stored update check is returned (`update_plugins` is a site transient; WP-CLI's help says `--network` is needed for site transients on single sites too).
- README (Plugin sizes, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, version 1.3.29.

## Verification

- `php -l` on the changed files; `vendor/bin/phpcs` on them: clean; `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`: passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors, 1 warning (the existing WordPress.org slug note).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors (GitHub zip: only the expected updater findings; both zips: the two existing `UnescapedDBParameter` warnings in files not changed here).
- Live measurement above.

Resolves #633

## What

Other plugins can serve their own post types at short addresses (`/item/` instead of `/base/item/`) through Short addresses for custom post types, with a new filter `seoprostack_short_address_types`. - `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `short_types` in the learned routes comes from `types()` alone, so filter-added types are routed before plugins load.

title: GH#664: fix: a scheme picked in your own profile turns Modern admin colours off
body:
## What

With **Modern admin colours** on, a colour scheme picked in your own profile was overridden: the `get_user_option_admin_color` filter forced Modern, so the pick never showed.

Now, while the setting is on, `SEOProStack_Admin_Colors::own_choice()` (on `update_user_metadata`, before the save, so it also fires when the stored value is unchanged or not yet stored) handles a pick of any scheme other than Modern by the current user:

- **People who may change SEO Pro Stack's settings** (`SEOProStack_Settings::can_change()`): the setting is turned off through `SEOProStack_Settings::set()` and `seoprostack_setting_saved` fires as usual. A `$from_profile` guard stops `sync_current_user()` from resetting their profile to the WordPress default, so the scheme just picked stays.
- **Everyone else**: a per-site user option `seoprostack_own_admin_color` lets their own scheme apply to them; `filter_admin_color()` skips them. Turning the setting on again deletes that flag for every user, so Modern applies to everyone again.

Covers both the live picker (AJAX `save-user-color-scheme`) and saving the profile form. Saving the profile without changing the scheme leaves the setting on.

Also: the setting's description, README.md (feature section and changelog), readme.txt and changelog.txt describe the new behaviour; `uninstall.php` removes the new user option. readme.txt is 10,214 bytes (limit 10,240): one 1.3.31 line was shortened to make room.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- A throwaway WordPress site with Playwright, 12/12 passed: setting on sets the admin's profile to Modern; a live pick of Sunrise sticks after reload and turns the setting off without a reset to the default; turning it on again sets Modern; a form save of Ocean sticks and turns it off; a profile save without a scheme change keeps it on; an editor's pick of Coffee applies to them only, the setting stays on and the admin still sees Modern; turning the setting off and on again brings the editor back to Modern; no `debug.log` messages.

Resolves #664
