title: GH#659: feat: Hosting needs says when no server cron job runs scheduled jobs
body:
## What

With `DISABLE_WP_CRON` set and no cron job on the server, every plugin's scheduled jobs stop, and wp-admin said so only on WP Crontrol's screen. **Hosting needs** now checks this on every site.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`, new "Scheduled events" section:
  - `overdue_event()`: the oldest event past its time, from `_get_cron_array()` (autoloaded, no query). WP Crontrol's rewritten notice (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::crontrol_status_markup()`) now uses it too, along with the `CRON_LATE` / `CRON_MISSED` thresholds, which moved here from Plugin fixes.
  - `needs_server_cron()`: `DISABLE_WP_CRON` set and no Cavalcade or Cron Control (the runners WP Crontrol names).
  - A notice on the Dashboard and Plugins screens for `manage_options` (`manage_network_options` in the network admin, which shows the main site's events). It is a warning past 15 minutes and an error past an hour, names the event, and lists the commands for this site (`php …/wp-cron.php` for single sites and the main site; `wp cron event run --due-now --path=…`, with `--url=` on a network) and the `wp-cron.php` address. It goes away once the events run.
  - A Site Health test, "Scheduled events" (good, recommended or critical, with the same commands). It is only added with `DISABLE_WP_CRON`; otherwise core's own tests cover it.
  - When `needs_server_cron()` is true, `seoprostats_schedule_notice` is set to `false`, so SEO Pro Stats 1.4.2+ does not repeat the advice.
- `admin/data/hosting-providers.php`: an optional `cron_jobs` field (Hostinger: `hPanel: Advanced → Cron Jobs`), named in the notice and test when the site is on that host. Hostinger is the only host Hosting needs detects. The file is loaded on demand when Site Health runs from cron.
- The setting description, README.md (Hosting needs section and changelog), readme.txt and changelog.txt are updated. To keep readme.txt under the limit (10,212 of 10,240 bytes), two 1.3.31 lines were shortened.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- A throwaway WordPress site with `DISABLE_WP_CRON`, WP Crontrol 1.22.0 and Playwright, 23/23 passed:
  - The test is registered, and the SEO Pro Stats filter returns hidden in admin requests.
  - Nothing late: no notice, and Site Health is good.
  - An event 20 minutes late (`wp_schedule_single_event(time() - 1200, …)`):
    - A warning on the Dashboard and the Plugins screen, naming `sps_test_late` and "20 minutes", with both commands and the `wp-cron.php` address. It is not on Posts, and there is no Hostinger line.
    - Site Health is recommended, and its screen lists "A scheduled event is late".
    - WP Crontrol's notice is rewritten as a warning naming the event.
    - An editor sees no notice.
  - An event 70 minutes late: an error notice, and Site Health is critical.
  - After `wp cron event run --due-now`: no notice, Site Health is good, and WP Crontrol's notice is the success one.
  - Hosting needs off: no notice, and SEO Pro Stats's notice is no longer hidden.
  - No `debug.log` messages.
- With `HOSTINGER` defined, `test_cron()` from WP-CLI (outside wp-admin, so the provider file loads on demand) is recommended and ends "On Hostinger, cron jobs are in hPanel: Advanced → Cron Jobs."

Resolves #659

title: GH#678: feat: remove Modern admin colours; a one-time step keeps Modern for people who never picked a scheme
body:
## What

Removes the **Modern admin colours** setting (Settings → Admin), as the owner chose. Everyone sees the scheme saved in their profile again. The setting only filtered `get_user_option_admin_color`; it never changed other people's saved schemes.

Settings version 26 runs a one-time step in `SEOProStack_Setup::retire_admin_colors()`:

- It removes `modern_admin_colors` from `seoprostack_options` and deletes the `seoprostack_own_admin_color` marks.
- If the setting was on (or, on pre-0.3.0 sites, `wp_allstars_admin_color_scheme` was set) **and WordPress is older than 7.0**, it saves `modern` for this site's users who never picked a scheme, so their screens look the same as before. Users without a picked scheme are those with no `admin_color`, or with `fresh`, the value WordPress before 7.0 saves for every new user (`wp-includes/user.php`: `empty( $userdata['admin_color'] ) ? 'fresh'`). WordPress 7.0's own `upgrade_700()` makes the same `fresh` → `modern` change.
- It does not change other schemes, or the scheme of anyone with an own-choice mark (they picked it while the setting was on).
- On WordPress 7.0+, Modern is core's default, so nothing is written.

It runs one query to find the users, then batches of 500 updates or inserts, and clears each user's meta cache.

**Change from the brief:** the brief said "users with no saved scheme". On WordPress 6.x almost every user has `fresh` saved by core, so that version would have changed almost nobody, and they would have switched from Modern to Fresh. This PR treats `fresh` the way core 7.0 does.

Also removed: the feature class, the settings screen's live colour switch (`admin/js/seoprostack-tabs.js`, `colorSchemes` script data) and the setting's docs (README, readme.txt, TESTING.md, DESIGN.md). `uninstall.php` still deletes the legacy option and the marks, for sites that never ran the upgrade. Unreleased changelog entry added.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs` (changed files) and `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`: no errors.
- Throwaway Docker site, WordPress 6.8.3, settings version set to 25 with the setting on. Before: admin `fresh`, alice `fresh`, bob `sunrise`, carol none, dave `fresh` with a mark. After: admin `modern`, alice `modern`, bob `sunrise`, carol `modern`, dave `fresh`; the mark is gone, the key is gone, and the version is 26.
- Same site with the setting off: no `admin_color` written; key removed. A second run changes nothing.
- After `wp core update` to 7.1.3, with the setting on: no `admin_color` written; key removed; version 26.

Resolves #678

title: GH#688: feat: Search custom fields can leave fields out (filter and Fields to leave out)
body:
## Summary

Search custom fields can now leave fields out. A search result never shows a
matched value, but the match tells which post holds it, so fields a site's
pages never show (private notes, contact details kept for the owner) should
not be searched.

- New filter `seoprostack_field_search_field` (bool `$search`, ACF field
  array, context `site` or `admin`). It runs once per request and context for
  each field, before the fields inside it, so returning false for a group,
  repeater or flexible content field leaves out everything in it. The context
  lets a plugin keep its private fields searchable in admin lists.
- New Troubleshooting setting **Fields to leave out** (`field_search_skip`,
  `lines`): field names or keys, one per line, for site owners without code.
  It sets the filter's starting value, so it applies in both contexts.
- `field_keys()` takes the context (default `site`, so existing calls without
  an argument still work) and caches per context. `search()` passes
  `is_admin() ? 'admin' : 'site'`. Nothing else in the SQL changes.
- Docs: the feature file's header, README (feature section and Extending) and
  `changelog.txt` under `= Unreleased =`. No version change.

## Verification

Throwaway WordPress 7.1.3 (Docker, PHP 8.3, MariaDB 10.6) with Secure Custom
Fields 6.9.5 and Search custom fields on. A local field group with a shown
text field, a hidden text field and a group with a text sub field; one word
saved in each; the main search query run for each word in its own process.
`sql=` is a hash of the `posts_search` clause as sent (placeholder escape
removed).

| Run | `shownzq1` | `hiddenzq2` | `innerzq3` (in the group) | Context seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (1.3.37), no filter | found | found | found | — |
| This branch, no filter, empty list | found | found | found | — |
| Filter leaves out the hidden field and the group | found | not found | not found | `site` |
| Same, as an admin list search | found | not found | not found | `admin` |
| List: `sps_v_hidden` (a name) | found | not found | found | — |
| List: `field_sps_v_group` (a group's key) | found | found | not found | — |

- With no filter and an empty list, the SQL hashes for all three words are
  identical on `main` and this branch (`ce27766187ee`, `a6e6549c4296`,

title: GH#696: fix: admin menu marker rows no longer log a read_post notice with GOTMLS
body:
## Summary

Organise the admin menu adds hidden marker rows to `$submenu` so core's `get_admin_page_parent()` opens the right menu. Those rows used to ask for the capability `do_not_allow`. Core checks each row's capability while it prints the menu (`wp-admin/menu-header.php`). GOTMLS Anti-Malware registers post types with `'read_post' => 'do_not_allow'`, so core's `map_meta_cap()` treated `do_not_allow` as `read_post` with no post. The result was a `_doing_it_wrong` notice on every admin page: about 3,480 traces in the shared preview site's debug log since 1 Oct.

The rows now ask for their own capability, `seoprostack_menu_marker` (`SEOProStack_Admin_Menu::MARKER_CAP`). `marker_cap()`, a `map_meta_cap` filter at `PHP_INT_MAX`, turns it into the primitive `do_not_allow`, so no one has it, super admins on multisite included. A primitive is not mapped again, so no notice. The `map_meta_cap` filters that already return `array('do_not_allow')` are unchanged: they return primitives.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`: `MARKER_CAP`, `marker_cap()` registered in `boot()`, and the two marker rows plus the check that skips them in `build_menu()`.
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Shared preview site with GOTMLS active: see the comment below for the debug log count before and after loading admin screens, and the menu check.

Resolves #696

## Summary

Resolves #719.

- Add an always-on Tools → Site Health test for Really Simple Security's marked auto-prepend, directory-indexing and uploads rules, non-stub headers file, and `rsssl_*` cron hooks.
- Add a POST-only, nonce/capability-protected cleanup action. On networks, preflight every site's stored activation lists before clearing cron and each site's uploads rules in batches of 50.
- Keep the RSSSL headers stub for cached prepend references, the HTTPS redirect, `wp-config.php`, unrelated rules/tasks, and all plugin settings.
- Refuse ambiguous/nested/prefix-colliding markers, symlinked files and unrecognized headers-file ownership instead of silently claiming success.
- Document cleanup in README.md, docs/replaced-plugins.md and changelog.txt.

## Files and reference pattern

Scope: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-security-headers.php`, `README.md`, `docs/replaced-plugins.md`, `changelog.txt`.
Site Health follows `SEOProStack_Hardening::tests()` and `test_files()`. Canonical `.htaccess` changes use core's marker writer after exact-marker validation; semicolon INI and legacy uploads delimiters need narrowly matched local writes.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime verified through the production Site Health callback and cleanup action on disposable Docker sites:

- Multisite on PHP 8.3, two sites, Really Simple Security 9.8.3 network activation/deactivation, followed by seeded exact leftovers from the reported incident. Pro/Pro Multisite activation guards were verified using their stored plugin identifiers; a licensed Pro firewall installation was not used.
- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 single site: successful cleanup and repeat cleanup; bad nonce, GET, missing capability, Pro Multisite and skipped-plugin activation refused.
- Both sites: all cron argument variants cleared, unrelated hooks preserved, current-site uploads rules cleared, headers file equals RSSSL's own stub, redirect and unrelated blocks preserved, `wp-config.php` hash unchanged, Site Health clean.
- Prefix-collision, nested-block and unrecognized headers-file cases refused without altering those files.
- Public pages return HTTP 200; unauthenticated wp-admin returns the normal HTTP 302 login redirect. Cron runs successfully; no `Event schedule does not exist` entries in the multisite debug log.

## Decisions

No automatic cleanup and no settings migration. Network health checks inspect only the current and main sites; the explicit action performs the full bounded network check. title: GH#725: fix: Dark loading screen after SEO Pro Stats, Rank Math System Status rows; release 1.3.43
body:
Resolves #725

#724 (GH#722) is merged; this PR now targets `main` and also releases **1.3.43** (version in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`; the 1.3.43 changelog includes #718 and #722, which were unreleased). `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors, 1 standing warning (WordPress.org slug note).

## What

1. **White flash between admin screens in Dark.** The user's screen recording (Brave) showed the whole content area turning light grey/white for about 2 seconds after a click from SEO Pro Stats to Dashboard. That is SEO Pro Stack's own loading screen (Preload pages: the next screen's title with dots, `html.sps-nav-shell`). Its dark rule needed `sps-dark` on `<html>`, but SEO Pro Stats' screens (and Tutor's course builder) keep their own look (`screen_applies()` is false), so they never had it, and the loading screen fell back to `#f0f0f1`.
2. **Rank Math → Status & Tools.** System Status's rows (`.rank-math-panel .components-panel__body > .components-panel__body-title`, `#f8f9fa`), their loading bars and Database Tools' odd rows stayed light in Dark.

## How

- `includes/admin/class-seoprostack-admin-whole-theme.php`: `head()` now prints the mode script on every logged-in admin screen. `head_script($applies)` adds `sps-mode-dark` ("this person's wp-admin is dark") everywhere, and adds the mode's own classes (`sps-theme-*`, `sps-dark`) and the other plugins' mode sync only where the screen turns dark, as before.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-whole-theme.js`: `paint()` keeps `sps-mode-dark` in step when the mode changes.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-preload-pages.php`: the loading screen's dark canvas and title use `html:is(.sps-dark, .sps-mode-dark)`.
- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css`: dark rules for Rank Math's `status.css` (System Status rows, toggles and icons, loading bars; Database Tools rows; table head text).
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

## Runtime testing

Risk: low (admin styling and one class on `<html>`). Level: runtime-verified on the local test site, with the changed files deployed there.

- Flash: Chrome (headed, real channel) with a TLS proxy streaming the Dashboard slowly (2.5 s), and a real click on Dashboard in the admin menu from `admin.php?page=seoprostats-dashboard`, recording screencast frames:
  - before (old `class-seoprostack-preload-pages.php` restored): 13 frames 77% white, light grey "Dashboard ." screen, matching the recording;
  - after: 0 white frames in 3 runs, browser preference dark and light; the frame at 183 ms shows the dark "Dashboard ." screen.
- Earlier runs on Dashboard → Posts and quick double clicks (Posts, then Media) showed no white frames either before or after.
- Rank Math: System Status rows `rgb(44, 51, 56)` with `rgb(240, 240, 241)` text, opened rows dark, Database Tools rows dark (screenshots checked).
- `php -l` on both PHP files; `scripts/lint.sh js phpcs`: passed.

## Decisions

- No early `<html>` background or `color-scheme` (the issue's first idea): Chrome keeps the old page until the new one paints, and tests showed no white from the browser itself. The flash was SEO Pro Stack's own loading screen.
- The loading screen follows the person's mode, not the screen being left, because it stands in for the next screen.
- Database Tools' row titles keep their contrast-guard colour (about 4.9:1); out of scope.

title: GH#712: feat: Dark mode fallback for every plugin's screens, and a committed dark-audit sweep
body:
## Summary

Dark mode now reaches every plugin's and theme's admin screens, not only those with a hand-written section, and the repository has an audit to measure it.

- `includes/admin/class-seoprostack-dark-fallback.php` (new, `SEOProStack_Dark_Fallback`): in Dark, each stylesheet from wp-content (not WordPress's, not SEO Pro Stack's, not plugins with their own dark mode) gets a cached copy holding only the rules that paint a light surface, a light border or dark grey text, recoloured with the palette, behind `:where(html.sps-dark)`, printed right after the original via `style_loader_tag`. Reads hex, rgb/hsl, `oklch()`, named colours and the stylesheet's own colour custom properties; keeps saturated brand colours and images; leaves the block editor's canvas out. Copies live in `uploads/seoprostack-dark`, keyed on file, mtime, size and `VERSION`; at most 0.15 s per screen, the rest at shutdown after the response is released (`fastcgi_finish_request()` / `litespeed_finish_request()`). Deleted on deactivation (registered on every request, so WP-CLI deactivation cleans up too) and in `uninstall.php`. Filters `seoprostack_admin_dark_fallback` and `seoprostack_admin_dark_fallback_style`.
- `scripts/dark-audit.mjs` (new): Playwright audit of the admin menu's screens in Dark: light surfaces (brand colours marked, full-width flagged), text below WCAG AA, `report.json` and per-screen `summary.md`, `compare`, `shot`. Site and login only from environment variables; only the site's own `/wp-admin/` addresses; site previews (editor canvas, site icon preview) skipped.
- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css`: core privacy request rows, popular tags and feature filter boxes; Settings → Connectors (WordPress 7 injects its styles by script) with AI Engine's banner; Bit Flows and Bit Social's content area (their script imports other stylesheets into a cascade layer, so it needs `!important`).
- `DESIGN.md` (Fallback for other plugins: approach, limits, measured figures), `TESTING.md` (Dark mode audit), `README.md`, `changelog.txt`.

## Results

Shared preview site, every recommended plugin, 272 admin menu screens (266 dark; 6 keep their own look on purpose: SEO Pro Stats ×2, Tutor course builder, SEO Pro Directory, WP Plugin Starter, YellowPencil's editor). Baseline = same branch and audit with the fallback switched off by filter (stricter than main: it includes this PR's hand-written rules).

| Measure | Before | After | Drop |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Light surfaces | 227 | 32 | 85.9% |
| Not brand colours | 218 | 23 | 89.4% |
| Full-width, not brand | 19 | 0 | 100% |
| Text below AA | 24 | 19 | 20.8% |

Final run on 1453f9c3 (the branch with 1.3.44 merged in), after a warm-up pass that made the copies: 272 screens, 266 dark, 0 errors (`site-editor.php` hit a transient `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` and was re-audited alone: dark, nothing light). The warm-up pass itself gave 33: Complianz's amber "Open" task badge, a brand colour shown only while a task is open. Against the first baseline on main (237 / 227 / 22 / 24): 86.5% fewer light surfaces. Settings → Connectors renders late and was counted in an earlier run (36); it is now covered. No screen got more light surfaces or more low-contrast text. Leftovers are mostly drawn by script (Social Engine's styled-components panels, FluentCommunity's first-run wizard, Element Plus fields and buttons, a React Select field) plus small notices and tiles.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (loads extra stylesheets on admin screens in Dark only)
- `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Deactivation cleanup from a non-admin request (CLI `wp-load.php`): `is_admin()` false, `SEOProStack_Setup::remove_dark_copies` hooked on `deactivate_seoprostack/seoprostack.php`, calling it removed `uploads/seoprostack-dark` (1,362 copies); the next audit made them again.
- Audit before/after on the preview site, as above; screenshots of Bit Flows, Bit Social, AutomatorWP and the leftovers inspected.
- Light mode: AutomatorWP and Products open light, no `sps-dark`, no fallback copies loaded.
- SEO Pro Stats and other opted-out screens: not dark, no copies loaded.
- Debug log after the preview and the audits: no messages from SEO Pro Stack's code. The only lines naming it are the known GOTMLS `read_post` notice (#744), where `SEOProStack_Admin_Bar_Sources` is just the admin bar object in core's stack.
- Shutdown copies: with every copy removed, 15 WooCommerce screens remade 81 copies (some deferred to shutdown) and gave the same figures as the full run.

title: GH#763: Keep Kadence Pro dark palette with Kadence Blocks design tokens
body:
Resolves #763

## What

**Fixes for other plugins** now keeps Kadence Pro's dark palette when Kadence Blocks 3.8.0+ design tokens are active.

Kadence Blocks' `Palette_Filter` (on `kadence_palette_option`, priority 10) answers every palette read with the active palette's token colour, because the filter isn't told which palette set was asked for. Kadence Pro's dark mode reads `second-palette`, so `body.color-switch-dark` got the light colours: the page stayed light and a dark mode logo (light artwork on a transparent background) vanished on the white header. This happened on two live client sites (Kadence 1.5.2, Kadence Pro 1.2.6, Kadence Blocks 3.8.0).

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: added only when `KADENCE_BLOCKS_VERSION` >= 3.8.0.
  - Priority 9 notes the theme's colour for the slot being read.
  - Priority 11: if Kadence Blocks changed it, the set that was asked for is read from the second argument of the theme's `palette_option()` call, using a backtrace of up to 8 frames that only runs for changed colours. When that isn't the active set, the theme's colour is returned. Reads of the active set keep the token colours.
  - A read that doesn't come through `palette_option()` falls back to comparing colours: the theme's colour is returned if it isn't the active set's colour for that slot.
  - The active set comes from `kadence_global_palette`, through the theme's own `kadence_active_palette` filter. It falls back to the theme's defaults when nothing is stored, and is decoded once per stored value. Palette10's `#FfFfFf` complement marker is handled.
- `phpstan-plugin.neon`: adds the `Kadence\` namespace to the existing ignore for plugins and themes not installed during analysis. `Kadence\kadence()` is called only after `function_exists()`.
- `README.md` (Fixes for other plugins, Changelog) and `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- A throwaway PHP check (not committed) copied the theme's `palette_option()` logic, added a Kadence Blocks-like priority-10 token filter and loaded this class. All 17 cases passed:
  - light reads get the token colours;
  - dark (`second-palette`) reads get the theme's dark colours, including palette10 against the light complement marker, a slot whose token matches the light colour, and a slot where both palettes share a colour (from CodeRabbit's review);
  - reads that don't come through `palette_option()` use the colour fallback;
  - with no stored palette, the theme's defaults are used.
- Not run end to end: the local preview site has no Kadence Pro. The live sites run an equivalent must-use hotfix, which was browser-checked (light → dark → light, correct logo each time). After release, remove that hotfix and repeat the toggle check on both sites.

title: GH#770: Kadence colour check for fixed Customizer colours
body:
## Summary

New Site Health check, **Kadence colour check** (Content tab, on by default; it only reports until someone clicks). It finds Kadence Customizer text/background pairs where one side is a palette colour and the other is fixed. It lists the pairs under WCAG AA (4.5:1, 3:1 for buttons) in the light palette or Kadence Pro's dark palette, showing both values, and offers a one-click switch of the fixed colour to the nearest palette colour (1–9) that passes in both modes with every colour it is paired with.

- Before writing, a fix keeps the theme mods it replaces in `seoprostack_kadence_colours_backup` (not autoloaded, tied to the active stylesheet, first value kept). **Restore** in Site Health puts them back. Uninstall deletes the option.
- Pairing: `{base}_color(s)|_typography|_font|_widget_title|_widget_content` → `{base}_background`, dropping words from the end until one is set. Footer rows fall back to `footer_wrap_background`. Backgrounds covered by an image or gradient are skipped, and see-through backgrounds are blended over palette 9.
- Slot choice keeps greys grey: a neutral fixed colour gets a neutral slot when one passes, so footer text does not become the accent; coloured links may take an accent.
- Kadence only (template `kadence`, `Kadence\kadence()` loaded). Writes only when Kadence stores settings as theme mods; needs `edit_theme_options` and a per-fix nonce.
- Palettes are read from `kadence_global_palette` and the theme defaults, not `palette_option()`, so the #763 Kadence Blocks token override does not skew the dark values.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: pass.
- Preview site (Kadence theme; Kadence Pro dark mode simulated with `KTP_VERSION` + `dark_mode_enable`, `second-palette`), using the issue's scenario. The site's theme mods and palette were snapshotted and restored afterwards (verified equal):
  - `footer_bottom_widget_content`/`_widget_title` `#f2f2f2` on `footer_bottom_background` `palette8`: light 1.07:1, dark 14.58 → flagged, fix `palette5` → light 7.18, dark 10.98.
  - `footer_bottom_link_colors` `#dff2dd`/`#98f286`: light 1.12/1.3 → `palette5`/`palette1` → 7.18/10.98 and 5.17/7.15.
  - `header_button_color` `#ffffff` on `palette2`/`palette1`: dark 1.16/2.28 → `palette9` → light 7.92/5.42, dark 15.95/8.09.
  - Findings after fix: 0. Restore: values identical to before, backup option removed, findings back to 6.
  - Test is not added when the template is not Kadence.

Resolves #770

title: GH#781: Kadence colour check follows social and category styles
body:
## Summary

The Kadence colour check (#770, 1.3.49) paired every text colour with the background of the same name, whatever the element's style. Two styles made that wrong (found on live sites after 1.3.49):

- **Social icons** (header, mobile header, footer): the `outline` style sets the button background to transparent (`.social-style-outline .social-button{background:rgba(0,0,0,0) !important}` in Kadence's CSS), so `*_social_background` is never painted; brand colours (`always`, `untilhover` for the normal state, `onhover` for hover) ignore the saved colours. These are now skipped.
- **Category colours** (`{type}_title_category_color`, `{type}_archive_item_category_color`): with the `pill` style Kadence paints the colour as the pill's **background** behind white text. The check now pairs Kadence's white with the category colour instead, labels it "Category pill text (white, set by Kadence)", and offers no fix for it, since the white is not a setting.

File: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-colour-check.php` (new `style()`, pill pairs in `pairs()`, locked fields in `findings()`, `label()`, `describe()`).

## Verification

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Social, filled, fixed colour on palette3 | still listed, palette fix offered |
| Social, outline | not listed |
| Social, brand `always` | not listed |
| Social, brand `untilhover` | hover state only |
| Category, normal style, fixed red on palette7 | still listed |
| Category, pill, fixed red (white on red) | not listed |
| Category, pill, palette1 (white fails in dark, 2.3:1) | listed as locked white text, no fix link |

title: GH#785: Kadence colour check names the site's own CSS
body:
## What

The Kadence colour check reads Kadence's Customizer settings only. When it lists something on a site with CSS of its own, Site Health now names those sources and says to look at the page in light and dark mode before changing a colour, because that CSS can change the colours.

Sources:

- Additional CSS, when it has a rule (comments only do not count)
- YellowPencil, when it has saved styles (`wt_*css` options or `_wt_css` post meta)
- A child theme's `style.css` with rules beyond its header
- Anything a plugin adds with the new `seoprostack_kadence_custom_css` filter (an array of names; non-strings are dropped)

No note when nothing is listed or there is no custom CSS. Findings, fixes and status are unchanged.

## Why

After 1.3.50, one site listed its category pill as white on `palette1` (dark 3.25:1). YellowPencil there sets `.post-title .category-links a { color: var(--global-palette9) !important }`, so the page shows navy text at 4.74:1 in dark mode (4.54:1 light): it passes.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-colour-check.php`: `test()` adds the note; new `custom_css()`, `has_rules()` and `yellow_pencil_css()`.
- `README.md`: Kadence colour check section.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (PHPCS, PHPStan and the rest).
- Preview site (Kadence, YellowPencil active with no saved styles), worktree class run against real settings, with theme mods, palette and `wt_css` saved first and restored afterwards (`state restored: true`):
  - nothing listed (with or without Additional CSS): no note
  - pill listed, no custom CSS: no note; Additional CSS with only a comment: no note

title: GH#804: HTTPS check in Site Health and on the Security tab, with an SSL Labs link
body:
## What

Adds a read-only **HTTPS check** to Tools → Site Health and to a section of the Security tab. It replaces Really Simple Security's SSL Labs status box:

- **Certificate**: whether it's trusted (checked against WordPress's CA bundle, so an incomplete chain also shows up), whether it names the host (wildcards included), who issued it and how many days it has left. Expired, untrusted or wrong-name certificates are critical; under 14 days left is recommended. When a certificate is untrusted, the message gives OpenSSL's own reason.
- **TLS version and cipher**: below TLS 1.2 is critical; below 128-bit is recommended.
- **TLS 1.0 and 1.1**: whether the site refuses them. When the server's own OpenSSL can't offer them, the check says it can't tell instead of counting them as refused.
- **HSTS**: whether the home page sends it and for how long. Missing, or shorter than six months, is recommended.
- **Full report and grade on SSL Labs**: a link to `https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d={host}` that opens in a new tab. It isn't shown for local hosts.

Nothing is sent to SSL Labs. Its API terms (v2.2) forbid commercial use and use on a public website without Qualys's permission. For the same reason, SSL Quality Checker's API approach isn't copied, and the plugin isn't recommended (`docs/plugin-directory.md`).

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-https-check.php`: `stream_socket_client` to the site's own host and port. Each connection has a 5-second timeout and its warnings are kept out of the log. The check runs only in Site Health's async test (and its weekly cron) and from **Check now** (admin-post, nonce, `manage_options`), never on a visitor's page.
- The last result is saved to the `seoprostack_https_check` option, which isn't autoloaded and is removed by `uninstall.php`. `wp seoprostack health` runs the check without saving the result.
- The test name is `seoprostack-https`, with a hyphen: `site-health.js` turns the first underscore into a hyphen, so the AJAX action wouldn't match an underscored name.
- Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES` and in the health CLI's test list.
- Docs: README (feature section, replaced-plugins row, changelog), `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt`.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: passes.
- Preview site (`plugin-testing.local`, mkcert certificate):
  - `check()` gives certificate critical with OpenSSL's reason, TLS 1.3 OK, old TLS refused, and no HSTS (recommended).
  - In the browser, Site Health shows one entry, "The site’s certificate has a problem". The Security tab section renders, and Check now redirects back with "Checked 1 second ago". The option isn't autoloaded, there's no SSL Labs link for `.local`, and no new debug log lines name the plugin.
  - `wp seoprostack health --format=json` lists `seoprostack-https` as critical, and the stored `checked` time is unchanged (1792195802 before and after).
- `check()` with `home_url` filtered to other hosts:
  - A live Cloudflare site: everything good (Google Trust Services, 53 days left; TLS 1.3; old TLS refused; HSTS 730 days with subdomains).
  - badssl `expired`, `wrong.host`, `self-signed` and `incomplete-chain`: each certificate is critical with the right reason.
  - The badssl hosts that accept TLS 1.0/1.1 are flagged, which proves the client really offers the old versions.
  - `tls-v1-0:1010`: protocol critical (only TLS 1.0/1.1).
  - `tls-v1-2:1012`: old TLS refused.
  - `hsts`: 182 days is good.

Resolves #804

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

## Skipped checks

- `qlty check`: skipped, Qlty is out of credits on this limited repository (`reference/ci-gate-policy.md` rule 14). https://qlty.sh/gh/wpallstars/projects/seoprostack/builds/01a14739-b0b6-72fb-9278-510045896d30

title: GH#787: skipped WebP/AVIF records no longer block the CompressX cleanup
body:
## Summary

`wp seoprostack convert-images --cleanup-compressx` refused forever when an attachment had a `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` marker but no record: `convert_attachment()` wrote exactly that for a missing file or a non-picture, and `conversion_failed()` counted it as failed.

- `convert_attachment()`: the skip branch now stores a record with `skipped => missing|not_image` (keeping any earlier copies listed, and clearing a stale `incomplete` marker from `run_batch()`).
- `conversion_failed()` → `record_state()`: skipped records and legacy marker-without-record are not failures. One whose picture file exists now is `back`: converted inline by the WP-CLI cleanup, queued again (DONE deleted, batch scheduled) by background batches, left alone by `--dry-run`.
- The cleanup error names the blocker: CompressX active, feature off / no format, batch lock, N pictures waiting, or the IDs (up to 10) of attachments whose copies failed or whose conversion stopped; prefixed with the site ID on multisite. `--dry-run` prints the same as a warning without changing anything.

  - Temporary attachment with a missing file: `convert_attachment()` → WP_Error, record `skipped=missing`, DONE set, state `ok`; with a stale `incomplete` record first, the marker is cleared.
  - Temporary PDF attachment: `skipped=not_image`, state `ok`.

title: GH#803: Kadence query filters use term slugs in addresses, without a redirect
body:
## Summary

New setting, off by default: **Kadence query filters use term slugs in addresses** (Content tab, a child of **Kadence query filters accept term slugs**). Kadence Blocks Pro taxonomy filters then put the term slug in the address (`?_makes=audi`) instead of the ID, and a link with the slug opens filtered, with no 302.

Resolves #803

## How

Kadence draws every query loop's results **and** its filter HTML through one REST route, `/wp/v2/kadence_query/query`: on page load the loop's blocks call it with `rest_do_request()` and the page's `$_GET` (`Kadence_Blocks_Pro_Query_Children_Block::do_query()`), and on a filter change `query.js` fetches it. Everything Kadence reads for filtering comes from `$_GET` (`Kadence_Blocks_Pro_Query_Index_Query_Builder::get_filters()`, `get_query_args_from_facets()`). So one pair of hooks covers page load and AJAX alike, in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-filters.php`:

- `rest_request_before_callbacks` (`rest_term_ids()`): for that route only, takes the loop from `ql_id`, and changes slugs in its taxonomy filter arguments (by filter slug or hash) to term IDs in `$_GET`, `$_REQUEST` (when set) and the request's query params, reusing `term_ids_for_slugs()` / `term_ids_value()` from #776. IDs, unknown slugs and the split character work as before.
- `rest_request_after_callbacks` (`rest_term_slugs()`): puts the original `$_GET` / `$_REQUEST` values back, then rewrites `value="<id>"` and `data-value="<id>"` in the response's `filters[<uniqueID>]` HTML to term slugs for the loop's taxonomy filters (one `get_terms()` per filter). Kadence's own script then pushes the slug and pre-selects the option a slug names.
- In this mode the #776 `template_redirect` is not hooked.

### Decisions

- **REST response, not `render_block`** (the issue suggested `render_block`): filter HTML is built inside the REST route and swapped in by fetch after each change, so `render_block` would miss every refreshed filter. The REST hooks catch both. As a bonus, loops in Kadence Elements and block templates work too, since the loop ID comes from `ql_id`, not the post content.
- **`$_GET` is put back** after the route runs, so the rest of the page still sees the slug.
- **All-digit slugs keep their ID**: `?x=2024` must stay a term ID, otherwise it would match another term.
- Only `source = taxonomy` filters change; meta, price and WooCommerce attribute filters (already `facet_value`) are untouched.

## Runtime Testing

Shared preview site (Kadence Blocks Pro 2.8.20.1, PHP 8.5), built with `scripts/preview-site.sh` (main + #810, #811, #812). Throwaway fixture: a `kadence_query` loop (posts, 5 per page) with a category drop-down (`cat`) and checkbox filter (`cats`), result count, card and pagination, on a page. Categories: `uncategorised` (ID 1, 4 posts), `sps-sticky-cat` (ID 18, 12 posts). Fixture deleted and both settings put back to off afterwards.

| Settings | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| both off | `?cat=1` / `?cat=18` / `?cat=uncategorised` | 200; 4 / 12 / 0 results; option values IDs (as 1.3.52) |
| accept slugs on, addresses off | `?cat=uncategorised`, `?cats=uncategorised,sps-sticky-cat` | 302 → `?cat=1`, `?cats=1%2C18` (#776 unchanged) |
| both on | `?cat=uncategorised` vs `?cat=1` | 200, no redirect; both 4 results; options `value="uncategorised"`, `value="sps-sticky-cat"`; checkboxes `data-value` slugs |
| both on | `?cat=sps-sticky-cat`, `&pg=2` | 12 results; page 2 shows 6-10 of 12 |
| both on | `?cats=uncategorised,sps-sticky-cat` vs `?cats=1,18` | 16 results each |
| both on | `?cat=no-such-term` | 0 results, left alone |
| both on, REST `kadence_query/query?ql_id=…` | slug vs ID, with `_sort=title|asc`, `_search=sticky`, `pg=3` | identical `foundPosts`/`postCount`/`page`; filter HTML slugs in every response |

Browser (Playwright, Chromium, visitor):

- Load `?cat=sps-sticky-cat`: drop-down shows SPS Sticky Cat, 1-5 of 12 results.
- Pick Uncategorised: address becomes `?cat=uncategorised`, 1-4 of 4.
- Tick checkboxes: `?cats=sps-sticky-cat` (12), then `?cats=uncategorised%2Csps-sticky-cat` (16).
- Load `?cat=1`: 4 results (ID link still filters; the drop-down shows no choice, since its values are slugs; documented).
- Console errors: none. Debug log: no entries from `class-seoprostack-kadence-filters.php`.

Note: WP-Optimize's page cache on the preview site served the plain page with ID values until bypassed; the README says cached pages keep IDs until the cache is cleared.

title: GH#809: Media in cloud storage can remove local copies after a confirmed upload, and bring them back
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of Media in cloud storage: optional, per-site Remove local copies after upload (off by default). Removes only files in the attachment’s completed record for the current endpoint, bucket and prefix, all or nothing per picture: every local file’s size and SHA-256 is checked before any goes, then HEAD 200 with the recorded size and a served public address. Each file is recorded in _seoprostack_storage_removed (size, SHA-256, mtime, signature, public address) before unlink. Watermark originals, AVIF copies and unrecorded files are never touched. Restore: wp seoprostack media-storage restore [--attachment=<id>] [--all] downloads with a new signed SEOProStack_S3_Client::get(), verifies size and SHA-256, writes via temp file and rename with the recorded mtime, never overwrites, uses the batch lease, and refuses on missing constants or a changed connection. Just in time: image editor, wp media regenerate, Regenerate Thumbnails, core REST /edit and /post-process, upload size step, WP-Cron, WebP/AVIF conversion and watermarking (including the mark picture) bring files back first; reading media details never does. Removed pictures show from the bucket on pages, wp-admin, REST edit responses and the block and classic editors, while saved content keeps local addresses (save_local() reverses on save). After a connection change, pages keep the address files were removed under. Switching removal or the feature off restores everything in background batches. README documents restore-before-deactivation and an optional missing-file rule; uninstall clears the new records; TESTING.md gains a checklist line.

title: GH#819: Parallel cloud media transfers and guaranteed removal time
body:
## Summary

Resolves #819.

- Upload changed files in signed groups of up to six using bundled Requests, with a filterable cap and an aggregate payload-memory bound.
- Persist every attempted group before network I/O, confirm successful peers even when a PUT fails, and publish only complete attachment inventories. Failed metadata persistence stops PUTs and retains the retry.
- Reserve the first 12 seconds of each 25-second batch for local-copy work; uploads use the remaining time, including unused local-copy time. Concurrent HEADs verify the whole attachment before any local deletion.
- Preserve redirect refusal, redacted errors, outbound-host blocking and proxy compatibility. Sequential proxy requests share a group deadline.
- Document limits and update all three user changelogs.

## Files Changed

- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — isolated WordPress and MinIO, never a live site or the shared preview.
- Final head on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4.33, eight files per attachment, simulated one-second PUT latency: ten attachments took **82.29 s serial vs 21.06 s concurrent (3.91x)**; peak concurrency six; identical object keys and completed records. An earlier minimum-runtime run measured 3.19x.
- WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3.35, seven files and 500 ms PUT latency: **36.81 s vs 10.72 s (3.43x)**. WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 7.4 with eight files and one-second latency measured 3.96x.
- Passed: unchanged files make no PUT; refused PUT leaves failed state, attempted keys, successful-peer confirmations and retry; retry recovers; failed attempted-key persistence makes no PUT; ten attachments removed while another upload proceeds; restoration; changed digest refused; missing HEAD retains every local file; expired deadline defers safely.
- Proxy fallback regression: successive timeouts fell from 0.550 s to 0.147 s, and the unsent third request returned `storage_budget`.
- Final runtime log inspection found no new product messages. Earlier temporary benchmark assertions were diagnostic fixture failures, not plugin PHP failures.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all checks pass, including PHPCS, PHPStan, shell and workflow lint; no JavaScript build is declared.
- Both existing smoke tests passed: WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4 and latest/PHP 8.3, with 10,000-post fixtures.
- Release preflight passed with zero errors. Plugin Check reported zero non-exempt errors on both builds. Those packaging checks precede the final transport-only refactor; full lint and minimum-runtime verification were rerun on the final head.
- Addressed all five terminal Codacy annotations: core filesystem reads replace local error-control operators; endpoint validation, HEAD normalization, fallback routing and response conversion are separate bounded methods. Scoped PHPCS, PHPStan and the Generic cyclomatic-complexity sniff pass.

## Acceptance and limits

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| At least 3x throughput, unchanged records/keys | 3.91x on the minimum runtime with representative latency/file count; record equality checked |
| Group failure remains atomic and retryable | Refused PUT and failed metadata-persistence cases pass |
| Removal progresses while uploads wait | Ten removals plus upload progress in one batch |
| Existing checks | Lint, both smoke variants, preflight and Plugin Check pass |

Actual Hostinger/Cloudflare R2 throughput is **not measured** by these controlled tests and remains a rollout measurement. No live credentials or site changes were used. Speedup varies with latency and file count: a seven-file, 500 ms run on the older runtime measured 2.45x, so this is not a universal speed guarantee.

Pre-existing warnings are not repaired here: `readme.txt` already exceeded 10 KiB on main (10,937 bytes; now 11,037 after the required changelog line); release-only Unreleased/tag/slug warnings; Plugin Check warnings in unchanged whole-admin-theme, added-keys and database-charset files. ## Summary

Resolves #818.

- Upload registered AVIF siblings through the existing confirmed-file inventory, removal and restore paths.
- Requeue legacy uploads without changing destination identity or deleting confirmed objects.
- Resolve AVIF picture sources from exact indexed bucket URLs with per-copy version queries.
- Update settings and user documentation in the four scoped files.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified on commit `0b137999`.

An isolated WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.3 / MinIO environment exercised the real plugin and S3 client. No live site or production bucket was changed; temporary verification files are not shipped.

| Acceptance | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Upload and remove registered AVIF copies | `wp seoprostack convert-images --force` and `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --limit=10`: three AVIF files confirmed in the bucket, recorded as removed, absent locally |
| Restore byte for byte | `wp seoprostack media-storage restore --attachment=5`: all eight inventory files restored with matching SHA-256 |
| Front-end AVIF delivery | Published post fetched over HTTP contains responsive `source type="image/avif"` with encoded Unicode bucket paths and per-copy `?v=`; all three AVIF objects return HTTP 200, `image/avif` and matching digest |
| Local behavior | After restoration with cloud delivery off, picture sources remain local |
| Legacy inventories | Simulated originals/WebP removed with local AVIF left behind: automatically enters waiting queue; upload adds AVIF and preserves all five confirmed original/WebP objects; upgraded inventory leaves queue |
| Idle upgrade | Clearing the scheduled event and inventory-version flag results in the next eligible request scheduling backfill without invalidating serving inventories |
| Negative cases | Stale and unregistered AVIF excluded; unrelated URLs and incorrect version queries not rewritten |
| Diagnostics | Debug log empty after final conversion, upload, HTTP page rendering, restore and legacy upgrade |

PHP 7.4 compatibility is checked by the existing PHPCS rules. title: GH#836: File and account integrity checks (core and plugin checksums, uploaded PHP, new administrators)
body:
## Summary

New Security feature, **File and account integrity checks**. It is off by default, as the brief asks. Once a day it runs read-only checks, in parts of up to 20 seconds. The main site runs them once for a whole network. There are four Site Health tests, and `wp seoprostack health` shows them too:

1. **WordPress core files**: core code files are compared with `get_core_checksums()`. It also reports extra `.php` files in `wp-admin/` and `wp-includes/`. Core's bundled `hello.php` is checked against core's checksums, as WP-CLI does.
2. **Plugins from WordPress.org**: compared with `https://downloads.wordpress.org/plugin-checksums/{slug}/{version}.json`. I read that address from `wp-cli/wp-cli` `WpOrgApi::PLUGIN_CHECKSUMS_ENDPOINT` and `get_plugin_checksums()`. A plugin counts only when WordPress.org's own update check gives it a `w.org/plugins/` ID, so a premium or GitHub plugin with the same slug is never compared. SEO Pro Stack itself always uses check 3.
3. **Other plugins**: compared with the size, mtime and SHA-256 recorded on `upgrader_process_complete` or when the plugin is first seen. A file is hashed only when its size or mtime changed.
4. **Uploaded PHP and new administrators**: finds PHP files in uploads, plus `.cache` files that contain PHP. "Silence is golden" `index.php` files are ignored. It also lists administrators and super admins first seen in the last 7 days.

A finding is `critical`, shown by path or user name only. A check that is in progress, could not run, or is stale shows `recommended`. An email goes out only when a finding is new. A failed email is retried at the next check. The `seoprostack_integrity_ignore` filter takes `fnmatch()` patterns. The health audit only reads the last results.

### Structure

`STANDARDS.md` asks for one feature class in `includes/features/`; helpers live in `includes/` (as `class-seoprostack-update-offers.php` and `class-seoprostack-s3-client.php` do). Each class stays inside `phpmd.xml.dist`'s code-size rules:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `includes/features/class-seoprostack-integrity-checks.php` | `SEOProStack_Integrity_Checks`: settings, schedule, running a check, saving results |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-scan.php` | the steps, core files, new administrators, noting findings and the ignore filter |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-folders.php` | walking `wp-admin`/`wp-includes` and uploads for PHP files |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-plugins.php` | checking each plugin against checksums or its record |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-records.php` | per-plugin records, the updater hook, which plugins are WordPress.org's |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-wporg.php` | WordPress.org's core and plugin checksums (md5, its format) |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-files.php` | listing folders and hashing files |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-email.php` | emailing new findings |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-report.php` | Site Health tests and the note under the setting |

Option and transient names use SHA-256 of the plugin file or slug and version; local records store SHA-256 hashes. md5 is used only to compare with WordPress.org's published md5 checksums.

Other files changed: `class-seoprostack-setup.php` (FEATURES), `class-seoprostack-health-cli.php` (`boot_tests()`), `uninstall.php` (options, per-plugin records, both events), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt` and `TESTING.md`.

## Runtime Testing

`runtime-verified` on throwaway Docker sites (WordPress 7.1.3), run on PHP 8.3 and on PHP 7.4 with the final code, and on PHP 8.3 with the single-class build from before the split, side by side. All three runs gave the same results at every step below (findings, Site Health text, three emails in total); the only differences are the SHA-256 option names and record sizes. The site had the GitHub build contents, Classic Editor, Hello Dolly, Akismet and a local "premium" plugin. A must-use mail catcher recorded email. The shared preview was not touched.

- Default: off, with no tests and no events. Switching it on schedules a daily event at 04:00 and a first run a minute later. All four tests show `recommended` until the first check finishes, then `good`. All records are `autoload=off`.
- Tampering added an empty `wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php`, `uploads/x.cache` containing `<?php`, a silence `index.php`, a `wpsupport_x` administrator, and a one-byte change to both a premium file and `classic-editor.php`. One run then gave four `critical` tests with exactly those items; the silence file was not reported. One email listed them. A second run sent no email.
- The `wp seoprostack health` audit left the hash of every integrity option unchanged and created no check state.
- An ignore pattern for `uploads/*.cache` removed that finding, and no email was sent when a finding disappeared. After undoing everything, all four tests were `good` and no email was sent.
- `wp plugin install premium-test-1.1.zip --force` recorded version 1.1 straight away (`1.1 local inc/a.php,premium-test.php`), and the next check reported nothing.
- Time box: with `BUDGET = 0`, the check ran in 456 parts and found the same items as one 20-second run (plus the class file the test edited to set the budget). The new `shell.php` added for that run sent a second email, and a further new file (`shell2.php`) a third.
- Switching off removed both events. Uninstall left 0 `seoprostack_integrity%` rows and no events. `debug.log` stayed empty.

## Checks

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan).
- PHPMD 3.0.0 with `phpmd.xml.dist`: no findings. With stricter margins (cyclomatic ≥ 9, NPath ≥ 150, class complexity ≥ 45) also none; the same strict run on the pre-split file reproduces Codacy's 38 findings.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors; its warnings are release-time ones (readme size, Unreleased section, existing tag) and listing notes.

Notes: for check 3, a version that changes outside WordPress's updater (Git or FTP) is recorded again without a report; the README says so. `mu-plugins` and themes are not checked yet, which is outside the brief's scope.

Resolves #836

body:
## Summary

Adds an off-by-default second source for Known vulnerabilities (Security): Wordfence Intelligence's free Scanner feed, downloaded daily with the owner's API key from wp-config.php (SEOPROSTACK_WORDFENCE_API_KEY, never saved or shown; the request carries only the key). The feed (about 80 MB, 42k records) is read a record at a time (includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-parser.php) and matched by type, slug and affected ranges (…-matcher.php) against every installed plugin, theme and the WordPress version, in parts of at most 20 seconds. New matches are emailed once (…-email.php). | Criterion | Result | Evidence |

| Account merge | Pass | Browser shortlist joins account `[1,385,195]`, browser key becomes `[]`; existing account Saved/Liked remain unchanged |

| Cache safety and backwards compatibility | Pass | Server HTML has four empty list containers and an empty shortlist badge; reactions configuration has no nonce; existing Saved posts block still renders Saved |

title: GH#853: Integrity checks stop reporting exit-guarded upload logs, 403 stubs and .l10n.php translation caches
body:
## Summary

Integrity checks (#836) no longer report three kinds of file that cannot run code. Any file that holds code that can run is still reported.

- **Uploaded PHP, exit-guarded logs** (`harmless()` → `guard_end()` + `open_tag_after()`): a file up to 8 MB that starts with quiet tokens, then `exit`/`die` with nothing, a number or a plain string, then `?>`, and has no later `<?` anywhere. The rest is streamed in 64 KB parts; a `<?` split across two reads is still found; over 8 MB is reported.
- **Uploaded PHP, "403 Forbidden" stubs** (`forbidden_stub()`/`stub_token()`): up to 2,048 bytes (taken from bytes read, not an earlier `filesize()`), only `header(...)` calls and `exit`. `(` may follow only `header` or `exit`. `$_SERVER` may be read only as `$_SERVER['SERVER_PROTOCOL']`, because request-controlled keys such as `QUERY_STRING` could send a redirect.
- **String literals in stubs and exit messages** (`plain()`): only letters, digits, spaces and `. , ! ? _ / -`, single or double quoted, with an optional `b` prefix. With no colon, joined literals cannot form a header name (`'Loc' . 'ation: …'`). With no backslash, `<` or quotes, there are no escapes or markup (`b"\x3cscript…"`).
- **Plugins from WordPress.org** (`translation_cache()`): a `name.l10n.php` missing from the checksums is skipped only when `name.mo` sits beside it, it is under 1 MB, and its tokens are only the open tag, `return`, `array(`/`[ ]`, `=>`, `,`, `.`, literal strings and integers, with `(` only after `array`. So `'system'('id')` or `[...][0]()` cannot pass. This is the format `WP_Translation_File_PHP::export()` writes, including the `'a' . "\0" . 'b'` that plural forms produce.
- The `seoprostack_integrity_ignore` doc comment names these built-in exceptions, so nobody adds broad patterns for them.

## Files Changed

TESTING.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-folders.php, includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-plugins.php, includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-scan.php

## Review

An independent read-only review found two bypasses in the first version: a `b"…"` binary-prefixed literal with escapes, and `'Loc'.'ation: /x'` concatenation. Both are fixed by the character allow-list above (commit 51ae5292), and both inputs are now in the fixture set and reported.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (security boundary: false acceptance would hide a real compromise)
- **Verification:** `scripts/lint.sh` passed in full (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan) at the final head.
- **Fixture harness:** 36 cases ran on PHP 8.5 and PHP 7.4 (`wordpress:php7.4-apache`), and every one gave the expected result. They include the issue's a/b/c/d/x/y/z table, a `<?` split across a 64 KB read, a file over 8 MB, `$_SERVER['X'](…)`, `header($_SERVER['QUERY_STRING'])`, `Location` and `Refresh` headers (plain, escaped, binary-prefixed and joined), `die('<script>')`, heredoc, interpolation, and `'system'('id')` and `[..][0]()` in `.l10n.php`.
- **Production check:** the new code was run read-only on the production site that reported the four false positives in 1.3.57. `uploads/index.php` (88 B), `uploads/code-profiler-pro/log.php` (69 KB) and `uploads/mailchimp-for-wp/debug-log.php` (104 KB) were each found harmless, and `mainwp-child-reports-en_US.l10n.php` was found to be a translation cache.

## Decisions

- The rules for 403 stubs and exit messages are stricter than the brief asked for. A redirect or markup stub in uploads is itself a sign of compromise.
- Unmatched `.l10n.php` files are not stored in the record, so they are tokenised again on each run. They are rare and small, and the checksums are cached for a week.
- The `.l10n.php` exception applies only to plugins from WordPress.org, as the brief scopes it.

Resolves #853

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: GH#854: Wordfence feed is accepted only with at least 1,000 records, so an early-closing reply keeps the last matches
body:
## Summary

Premise check: partly correct. The bot's claim that scan() ignores all following bytes is wrong: finished() already requires MIN_FEED bytes and only whitespace to EOF. But a well-formed reply of 1 MB or more that closes early was accepted. Example: { + 2 MB of spaces + }, which main returns true for. That replaced the last matches with none. Fix: SEOProStack_Vulnerability_Feed_Matcher counts records that have an id across every part (persisted in the check's found state), and Parser::finished() also requires MIN_RECORDS (1,000; the live feed has 42,481). A check state from 1.3.57 without the count reads its copy again from offset 0, with no new download, so the count is whole.



## Files Changed

TESTING.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-check.php, includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-matcher.php, includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-parser.php

title: GH#869: fix: restore watermarked site icons and logos
body:
## Summary

Restore a marked attachment from its kept original when assigned as `site_icon`, `site_logo`, `custom_logo`, Kadence `mobile_logo`, or given an attachment context. Handle both initial option creation and updates, including direct theme-mod option writes. Keep restoration hooks active with watermarking off. Log failed restores and show a one-time capability-checked admin warning without deleting attachments.

Interactive follow-up (09b0fcc5, also CodeRabbit's finding): the Customizer's `crop-image` AJAX crops a new attachment from the chosen picture's file, so a marked picture passed its mark to the cropped icon or logo, which has no record to restore. `site_image_crop()` runs before WordPress's handler (priority 0 vs 1) with the same nonce (`image_editor-<id>`) and `edit_post` checks, and makes WordPress crop a clean temporary copy of the kept original (at the attached file's size, so `-scaled`/`-rotated` pictures crop correctly); `wp_create_file_in_uploads` moves the crop beside the source. The chosen picture stays marked. Changelog lines in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`, and a README feature note.

## Files Changed

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`
- `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`

- Preserve ordinary failure back-off if a group contains both a real failure and a budget deferral.

## Scope

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`, following the existing upload inventory and retry patterns. Matching user-facing changelogs in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, and `readme.txt` follow STANDARDS.md; the canonical issue scope records these paths.

title: GH#907: editors see plugin settings read-only; Rank Math Analytics (1.3.72)
body:
## What

Editors (the roles chosen in **Editors use the business plugins**) see the business plugins' settings but cannot change them. Settings screens that show passwords, API keys or licence keys stay administrator-only, as the owner decided. Editors also see Rank Math's Analytics again.

Resolves #907

## How

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-editor-settings.php` (`SEOProStack_Editor_Settings`), booted by `SEOProStack_Editor_Access::boot()`. It holds rules for each plugin, taken from a check of that plugin's settings screens and save paths. It follows the FluentSMTP pattern from #905:
  - every save is refused on the server with a 403 and "please ask an administrator". This covers REST (`rest_pre_dispatch`), AJAX, admin-post and forms posted to the screen (`wp_loaded`:1, before WooCommerce saves its settings), plus links that act when opened (Rank Math's `reconnect` and OAuth reply);
  - the read-only screens show a kept notice (`sps-keep`). A script adds it, so it also appears inside the Fluent apps at `#/settings`;
  - screens and routes that show secrets, or that export settings or change set-up, are refused and removed from the menu.
- Rules for each plugin:
  - **WooCommerce**: these settings are read-only: General, Products, Shipping (zones, classes), Tax (rates), Accounts, Emails and Advanced page set-up. These are administrator-only: Payments, Integration (MaxMind key), REST API keys, webhooks, Status and Extensions, plus `payment_gateways`, `system_status`, `webhooks` and the matching settings groups over REST.
  - **Rank Math**: these settings are read-only: General, Titles & Meta, Sitemap and Instant Indexing. Titles & Meta becomes administrator-only once `facebook_secret` or `maps_api_key` is set, and Sitemap once `youtube_api_key` is set. Status & Tools, the wizard, registration and the `rank-math/set-*` and `fix-site-seo` abilities are administrator-only.
  - **Tutor LMS**: Settings, Tools and Add-ons are administrator-only, along with their AJAX actions. The settings include payment credentials and the YouTube API key.
  - **FluentCRM / Fluent Support / Fluent Booking / Fluent Boards**: writes to settings are refused. The routes that return keys, integrations or licences answer only administrators.
- Rank Math Analytics fix: Rank Math loads its modules on `after_setup_theme`:2, before features boot on `init`, so the `rank_math_analytics` check failed. `SEOProStack_Editor_Access::early()` now adds the `user_has_cap` filter as the plugin loads. Before `init` it reads the stored option, as `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::early()` does, so no translations load early.
- WordPress's own Settings screens and SEO Pro Stack's own settings stay administrator-only. SEO Pro Stack's settings hold the maintenance bypass link and admin tools.

title: GH#913: fix(plugin-loading): match namespace for shared menu callbacks (1.3.75)
body:
## Summary

With **Load plugins only where needed**, editors lost the Fluent Boards and Fluent Booking menu entries on screens that skip those plugins (Dashboard, Posts, Media).

`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::plugins_sharing_callback()` treated another plugin as bundling a menu callback's code when it had a file at the same relative path declaring a class with the same short name, without checking the namespace. Fluent Boards, Fluent Booking, FluentSMTP and FluentAuth each ship `app/Hooks/Handlers/AdminMenuHandler.php` in their own namespace. The saved menu copy therefore listed FluentSMTP as an owner of the Boards and Booking pages. `restore_menu()` then skipped those entries on every screen where FluentSMTP loaded.

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: a copy counts only if it declares the callback's namespace, or no namespace for global code (new `in_namespace()`). WP Sheet Editor's shared framework, the case this was written for, is global code in each copy, so it still counts.
- `MAP_VERSION` 11 → 12, so sites relearn their screens and menu copy once and drop the wrong owners.
- Version 1.3.75: `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (and badges), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors. The one warning (WordPress.org slug) was already there.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors in either zip. The warnings were already there.
- On the reporting site, all five `AdminMenuHandler.php` copies declare different namespaces (`FluentBoards`, `FluentBooking`, `FluentAuth`, `FluentMail`, `WPSocialReviews`).
- After deploy, I will check as a plain editor that the menu shows both plugins on the Dashboard.

Resolves #913

- **Kadence blocks first** (`editor_tidy_kadence`): in the post editor, core blocks with a Kadence (or Pro) counterpart get `supports.inserter` false via `blocks.registerBlockType`, only when the Kadence block is registered, offered in the inserter and not switched off in `kt_blocks_unregistered_blocks`.
- **Fix found while testing:** on sites where a plugin registers a script before `init`, core builds the `wp-preferences` inline data before the feature's filters exist, so welcome guides and fullscreen were never read as off there either. `reload_preferences()` swaps that script's `serverData` for the filtered value when core read it first.

Why not Preferences → Blocks (`hiddenBlockTypes`): core turns hidden types into disallowed types, which breaks pasting headings/lists/tables/images, transforms, duplicates, Word documents in the editor and patterns that use them. The inserter flag only hides them.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-editor-tidy.php`, `admin/js/seoprostack-editor-tidy.js` (new), docs and version files.

title: GH#925: Image loading keeps cache plugins' lazy loading off logos and eager pictures (1.3.80)
body:
Resolves #925

## What

On sites with LiteSpeed Cache's **Lazy Load Images** on, logged-out visitors saw the header logo flash on every page change. LiteSpeed rewrote the logo to a grey `data:image/svg+xml` placeholder (`data-lazyloaded="1"`, real file in `data-src`) and swapped the file back in with its script after load, even though WordPress had marked the logo `fetchpriority="high"`.

Image loading already decides which pictures load straight away, but only through the native `loading` attribute, which page-rewriting lazy loaders ignore. Those pictures now also get `data-no-lazy="1"`. LiteSpeed Cache (7.9.1 checks it in `src/media.cls.php`) and WP Rocket both skip pictures with it.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`
  - `attachment_image()`: logos and `fetchpriority="high"` attachment images get `data-no-lazy="1"`. Excluded images still lose `loading="lazy"`.
  - `content_image()`: the first N content pictures, high-priority pictures and excluded pictures get `data-no-lazy="1"`.
  - `keywords()`: core's `custom-logo` class is now a default exclusion. This covers Kadence's main logo and its mobile `extra-custom-logo`.
  - Settings descriptions and the file header explain the behaviour.
- README (feature section and changelog), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, version 1.3.80. #924 holds 1.3.79.

Pages are still not rewritten: the change uses the same core filters as before. Pictures further down the page are still lazy-loaded by the cache plugin.

## Verification

- `php -l includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: no syntax errors. PHPCS and PHPStan run in CI's Lint job; they are not installed locally.
- Before: on a regional review site (Kadence, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.78, Image loading on), the logged-out home page served both `custom-logo` images with `data-lazyloaded="1"` and a placeholder `src`.
- After release, on that site: fetch the page logged out with a cache-busting query. The logo should have a real `src` and `data-no-lazy="1"`, and lower images should keep LiteSpeed's lazy loading. Then move between pages in a browser and check the logo does not flash, on desktop and mobile, in light and dark mode.

title: GH#927: feat: host-independent email protection
body:
## Summary

Resolves #927.

- Add default-on Email protection on Security for rendered content, blocks, widgets and menus, without changing stored data.
- Encode text and mailto URIs with a per-response XOR key; restore using a conditional deferred local script, textContent and mailto-only hrefs.
- Preserve link markup and ignored contexts; document JavaScript requirements, limitations and the bypass filter.

## Files and reference

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php`, `assets/js/email-protection.js`, the registry in `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`, README/readme/changelog. Follows Image loading's feature schema and the WordPress 6.2 tag processor pattern.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified
- **Final head:** 1d7b9e0f90545c689ee949c518e7325216b060e2

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS, PHPStan; no build script).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: final-head run passed with zero errors in both zips. Existing warnings remain in the unchanged whole-admin theme, database keys and database charset files; expected GitHub-updater findings are classified by the existing script. No new feature findings.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: final-head run passed, including default/all-feature HTTP paths, cron, query checks and uninstall; no PHP messages.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker`: final-head run passed, 0 errors and 4 expected release-time warnings (Unreleased headings, listing slug, existing version tag). Local PHP 8.5 syntax is supplemented by the PHP 7.4 smoke test. Offline checks do not verify remote assets; no publication is requested.
- Docker WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3: browser and HTTP checks passed for the final encoding/decoder implementation. The subsequent final change only extracts the unchanged plain-response expression into `plain_context()`; exact-head lint and minimum-version smoke were rerun. The disposable site was removed after verification.
- Direct WordPress checks cover every registered output filter, real `do_blocks()`, repeated filtering, skipped raw elements/attributes, the bypass filter, feed output and outgoing `wp_mail` data without delivery.
- Independent read-only review found entity-text preservation and raw-element boundary defects; both were hand-fixed and runtime-checked, including custom elements and non-HTML whitespace. No test infrastructure added.
- Codacy reported cyclomatic/NPath complexity in `protect()` on the previous head. The context expression was extracted unchanged into `plain_context()`, reducing both methods below the reported thresholds without weakening the scanner configuration.

### Acceptance matrix

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Raw page hides paragraph/mailto addresses | HTTP 200 raw HTML has no readable protected addresses; ignored script/style/textarea/input/title contexts preserved. |
| Browser restores text and usable links | Exact text, apostrophe/entity addresses, class, nested strong and mailto subject/cc retained; keyboard focus and accessible link name verified. |
| Feeds, REST and outgoing email unchanged | WordPress feed/mail checks and HTTP 200 REST rendered-content assertions passed. |
| Release checks and PHPCS | Lint, Plugin Check, minimum-version smoke and release preflight passed. |
| Conditional decoder, fallback and off switch | One deferred script on protected page, none on no-address homepage; four visible noscript fallbacks; switching off returns original text/href and no decoder. |

The disposable debug log contains two early WP-CLI probe errors from calling core's `render_block` filter without its required extra arguments. The corrected probe uses real `do_blocks()` and passes; subsequent application/browser requests added no messages. These were verification invocation errors, not product-path failures.

## Decisions

Deters HTML-only scrapers, not JavaScript-capable bots. No external services, persistence or global buffering. Attributes other than mailto hrefs intentionally stay unchanged.

title: GH#945: Avatars: Show Avatars on, copy authors' Gravatar pictures, stop Kadence Local Gravatars (1.3.84)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #945.

Avatars without Gravatar now gives every site working, self-hosted avatars by default (owner's request):

- **Show Avatars on** (settings version 34): `migrate()` turns `show_avatars` on once where the feature is on, new installs included. On a live site it was off, so `get_avatar()` returned false and Kadence's author meta printed an empty 32 px box although the authors' profile pictures were stored.
- **Copy pictures from Gravatar** (`avatar_gravatar_import`, on by default): the WP-Cron hook `seoprostack_avatar_gravatar_import` takes 20 people at a time who can write posts and have no picture here, downloads `secure.gravatar.com/avatar/{sha256}?s=512&d=404&r={rating}` and stores it with the existing profile picture code. Only the server contacts Gravatar. 404 means not asked again until the email address changes; a failed request retries the next day; uploaded, removed or Avatar Privacy pictures are never replaced. Listed under External services in `readme.txt`.
- **Kadence Pro's Local Gravatars** (and the Local Gravatars plugin): its own filters (`get_local_gravatars_max_process_time`, `get_local_gravatars_fallback_url`) stop it re-downloading local avatars into `wp-content/gravatars/`. Kadence Pro's setting is not written.
- `uninstall.php` removes the new user meta and cron hook; `AGENTS.md` records the owner's on-by-default choice.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan all passed.
- Docker test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`, WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3):
  - `show_avatars` 0 with settings version 33 → `1` after upgrade to 34; first batch scheduled.
  - Author with a Gravatar → 4 local sizes in `uploads/seoprostack-avatars/users/`, `get_avatar()` uses them; editor without one → marker 0, silhouette; subscriber not asked; no reschedule when the queue is empty.
  - Email change → re-queued; new address without a Gravatar keeps the earlier copy.
  - Kadence Pro's `dist/local-gravatars.php` loaded: avatar markup unchanged and no `wp-content/gravatars/`; control with our filters removed reproduces the rewrite to `/wp-content/gravatars/…`.
